```{r load}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(ggbeeswarm)
library(ggrepel)
library(kableExtra)

dat <- readRDS("../../output/perio_bugs_corrected.rds") |>
  # row in the full table, which keys the precomputed replicability similarities
  mutate(perio_row = row_number()) |>
  # studies the full-text review proposes excluding: not a health vs periodontitis comparison
  filter(!grepl("^proposed exclusion", `Review status`))

# one row per study: metadata are shared by the increased and decreased signatures
studies <- dat |>
  distinct(Study, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(-`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, -`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`, -`Abundance in Group 1`) |>
  mutate(Year = as.integer(Year))

# colors: health/periodontitis, periodontitis classification, profiling method
# (method colors match the overview figure of the main report; grey is always "not reported")
pal_group <- c(Health = "#2a78d6", Periodontitis = "#eb6834")

class_levels <- c(
  "Chronic periodontitis", "Chronic and aggressive periodontitis", "Aggressive periodontitis",
  "Periodontitis (stage/grade)", "Refractory periodontitis", "Periodontitis (type not specified)"
)
class_short <- c("Chronic", "Chronic + aggressive", "Aggressive", "Stage/grade", "Refractory", "Not specified")
pal_class <- setNames(c("#1baf7a", "#6250d6", "#e87ba4", "#eda100", "#e34948", "grey65"), class_short)

method_levels <- c("16S rRNA sequencing", "Shotgun metagenomics", "DNA-DNA hybridization",
                   "PCR", "Other / not reported")
pal_method <- setNames(c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#008300", "#d55181", "grey65"), method_levels)

theme_meta <- theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank()
  )
theme_set(theme_meta)

derive_fields <- function(st) {
  mutate(st,
    classification = factor(
      class_short[match(`Periodontitis classification`, class_levels)], levels = class_short
    ),
    method = case_when(
      `Sequencing type` == "16S" ~ "16S rRNA sequencing",
      `Sequencing type` == "WMS" ~ "Shotgun metagenomics",
      `Sequencing type` %in% c("PCR", "16S,PCR") ~ "PCR",
      `Sequencing platform` == "DNA-DNA Hybridization" ~ "DNA-DNA hybridization",
      .default = "Other / not reported"
    ) |> factor(levels = method_levels),
    period = cut(Year, c(-Inf, 2004, 2009, 2014, 2019, Inf),
                 labels = c("1995–2004", "2005–2009", "2010–2014", "2015–2019", "2020–2025"))
  )
}
studies <- derive_fields(studies)

# systemic condition entries that are not a disease: participants screened for one condition only, or
# not restricted (from the full-text review)
systemic_no_disease <- c("non-diabetic", "hiv-negative", "not restricted")

# group-level measures in long format
features <- tribble(
  ~feature,   ~label,                          ~mean_col,                        ~sd_col,
  "age",      "Age (years)",                   "age mean",                       "age sd",
  "males",    "Males (%)",                     "percent males",                  NA,
  "smokers",  "Smokers (%)",                   "percent smokers",                NA,
  "pd",       "Probing depth (mm)",            "pocket depth mean (mm)",         "pocket depth sd",
  "cal",      "Clinical attachment loss (mm)", "clinical attachment loss (mm)",  "clinical attachment loss sd",
  "bop",      "Bleeding on probing (% sites)", "bleeding on probing percent",    "bleeding on probing sd",
  "plaque",   "Plaque (% sites)",              "plaque",                         "plaque sd",
  "supp",     "Suppuration (% sites)",         "suppuration percent",            "suppuration sd"
) |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = label))

long <- pmap_dfr(features, function(feature, label, mean_col, sd_col) {
  map_dfr(0:1, function(g) {
    col <- function(x) if (is.na(x)) NA_real_ else studies[[paste("Group", g, x)]]
    num <- if (feature %in% c("males", "smokers")) col(paste("num", feature)) else NA_real_
    tibble(
      Study = studies$Study, feature = feature, label = label,
      group = c("Health", "Periodontitis")[g + 1],
      mean = col(mean_col), sd = col(sd_col),
      n = studies[[paste("Group", g, "sample size")]],
      num = num
    )
  })
}) |>
  # plaque indices (e.g. Silness-Löe 0-3) are not comparable with % sites
  left_join(select(studies, Study, `Plaque measure`), by = "Study") |>
  filter(!is.na(mean), feature != "plaque" | `Plaque measure` %in% "% sites") |>
  select(-`Plaque measure`)

# studies with values for both groups
paired <- long |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(Study, feature, label), names_from = group,
              values_from = c(mean, sd, n, num)) |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_Health), !is.na(mean_Periodontitis)) |>
  # smokers excluded from both groups: no contrast
  filter(!(feature == "smokers" & mean_Health == 0 & mean_Periodontitis == 0))

paired_tests <- paired |>
  summarise(
    studies = n(),
    diff = median(mean_Periodontitis - mean_Health),
    p = wilcox.test(mean_Periodontitis, mean_Health, paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE)$p.value,
    .by = c(feature, label)
  ) |>
  mutate(p_label = ifelse(p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste("p =", signif(p, 2))))
```

## About this report

This report describes PerioSigDB: how participant and clinical characteristics differ between periodontitis and comparison groups and across studies, how PerioSigDB compares with BugSigDB, and how the taxa it links to periodontitis are reported in other conditions.

The metadata summaries use the **study** as the unit of analysis (n = `r nrow(studies)`), because metadata are recorded once per study and shared by its increased and decreased signatures. Later comparisons use studies, signatures or, for BugSigDB, study units (study × condition × direction × body site group), as stated for each figure. A study unit collapses a study's repeated signatures for the same condition, direction and body site group into one, while keeping its different comparisons (e.g. stool and saliva, or increased and decreased) separate.

**Data version:** the corrected PerioSigDB, which adds two sets of changes to the curators' annotation, both pending curator confirmation. The first is manual corrections. The second is a full-text review of the papers that corrected or filled values (e.g. group sizes, clinical measures, periodontitis classification, systemic health status, study design, sequencing platform) and added the BugSigDB fields PerioSigDB lacked (statistical test, significance threshold, multiple-testing correction, LDA threshold, matching, confounders, diversity, signature source and description); every change is listed with its supporting quote in `output/llm_annotation/review_log.csv`. The review also proposes excluding 9 studies (14 signatures) whose signatures are not a health vs periodontitis comparison (e.g. rheumatoid arthritis groups, descriptive data without tests, a duplicate entry). They are marked in the `Review status` column and left out of every analysis in this report, including the precomputed consensus signatures (Studies 134, 144, 155, 450, 452, 1590, 1690, 1982 and 2025-PubMed-130).

Group 1 is the periodontitis group and Group 0 the comparison group. The comparison group is labelled "Health" in the figures, but eligibility criteria varied:

- Studies 298 and 153 include participants with gingivitis in Group 0.
- Studies 1752, 1818 and 1897 recruited adults aged 65 and over described as periodontitis-resistant.

::: {.callout-note}
## Terms used in this report

- **Study:** an individual published research study.
- **Signature:** a list of taxa reported as increased or decreased in one group compared with another. "Increased" and "decreased" are reported case–control differences, not changes over time.
- **Study unit:** a unique combination of study, condition, direction and body site group (BugSigDB analyses), so that a study with several similar signatures counts once.
- **Enrichment (literature analyses):** a genus is reported in a given direction by a larger share of a condition's studies than expected from other studies. It describes how often the genus is reported, not how much more abundant it is in participants.
- **Periodontitis-increased / -decreased genera:** the genera most consistently reported increased or decreased in PerioSigDB. Several health-associated oral taxa are in the decreased group, but a genus can contain species reported in both directions (e.g. *Porphyromonas gingivalis* increased, *P. catoniae* decreased).
- **FDR < 0.05:** p-values adjusted for the number of tests with the Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) method, at a false discovery rate of 5%. "Unadjusted p" is the p-value before this adjustment.
:::

The analyses use several sets of periodontitis taxa:

| Taxon set | Selection rule | Rank | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Top 20 genera per direction | the 20 genera per direction with the smallest binomial p-value (increased vs decreased PerioSigDB signatures); includes genera that do not pass FDR | genus | genus heatmaps, direction summary, assay and species checks, prevalence, co-occurrence |
| Consensus signatures (32 increased, 12 decreased taxa) | binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures, p < 0.05 | as reported (mostly species) | whole-signature similarity, taxon-by-taxon heatmaps |
| Genus consensus (16 and 9 genera) | the consensus signatures collapsed to genus | genus | Jaccard overlap, participant-level colorectal cancer analysis |
| Descriptive taxon sets (head and neck cancer, smoking) | reported by at least 3 studies, at least 75% in one direction; no statistical test | as reported | taxon-by-taxon heatmaps |

**Assay coverage:** about half of PerioSigDB signatures come from targeted PCR or DNA–DNA hybridization, which measure a predefined list of taxa. Reporting frequencies in this report therefore reflect both biological findings and which taxa the original assays could detect or were designed to measure. A signature does not distinguish a taxon that was measured and unchanged, measured but not reported, or not measured, so absence from a signature is not evidence that a taxon was absent or unchanged.

# Data availability

## Metadata completeness heatmap

```{r completeness}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 6.3
#| fig-cap: "Reporting of metadata across studies. Each column is a study, ordered by publication year (ticks: first study of each period); each row is a field. Group-level fields are shaded by whether they are reported for both groups, one group, or neither. Plaque counts as reported only when given as % of sites. Systemic health status is shaded when recorded, whether systemically healthy or not; systemic comorbidity is shaded only when participants are recorded as having a systemic condition (e.g. diabetes), so it is not a completeness measure. Statistical test, significance threshold and multiple-testing correction were added entirely by the full-text review. Green: cells raised by the full-text review of the papers (e.g. from neither or one group to both groups), not by the curators; dark and light green as for blue. The percentage after each field is the share of studies reporting it for both groups (group-level fields) or at all (study-level fields)."

# statistical fields: added to PerioSigDB by the full-text review (the curators did not record them), so
# reported by a study if any of its signatures has them, and never reported before the review
stat_fields <- c("Statistical test", "Significance threshold", "MHT correction")
stat_reported <- dat |>
  summarise(across(all_of(stat_fields), \(x) any(!is.na(x) & !(as.character(x) %in% c("", "NA")))), .by = Study) |>
  rename(`Multiple-testing correction` = `MHT correction`)

field_status <- function(st, review = TRUE) {
  stat_status <- stat_reported |>
    filter(Study %in% st$Study) |>
    mutate(across(-Study, \(x) x & review))
  study_fields <- tibble(
    Study = st$Study,
    `Profiling method` = st$method != "Other / not reported",
    `16S variable region` = !is.na(st$`16S variable region`),
    `Periodontitis classification` = st$classification != "Not specified",
    `Systemic health status` = !is.na(st$`Systemic condition`),
    `Systemic comorbidity recorded as present` = !is.na(st$`Systemic condition`) &
      !tolower(st$`Systemic condition`) %in% c("systemically healthy", systemic_no_disease),
    `Group 0 definition` = !is.na(st$`Group 0 definition`),
    `Group 1 definition` = !is.na(st$`Group 1 definition`)
  ) |>
    left_join(stat_status, by = "Study") |>
    pivot_longer(-Study, names_to = "field", values_to = "reported") |>
    mutate(status = ifelse(reported, "Reported", "Not reported"), type = "Study")

  # groups with a value; plaque only when measured as % sites (as in long)
  group_fields <- features |>
    mutate(label = as.character(label)) |>
    add_row(label = "Sample size", mean_col = "sample size") |>
    pmap_dfr(function(feature, label, mean_col, sd_col) {
      reported <- \(g) !is.na(st[[paste("Group", g, mean_col)]])
      tibble(
        Study = st$Study, field = as.character(label),
        groups = (reported(0) + reported(1)) * (label != "Plaque (% sites)" | st$`Plaque measure` %in% "% sites")
      )
    }) |>
    mutate(
      status = c("Neither group", "One group", "Both groups")[groups + 1],
      type = "Group"
    )

  bind_rows(group_fields, study_fields)
}

# values before the full-text review: its changes reverted (output/llm_annotation/review_log.csv)
review_changes <- read.csv("../../output/llm_annotation/review_log.csv") |>
  filter(action == "changed")
studies_pre <- studies
for (i in seq_len(nrow(review_changes))) {
  col <- review_changes$item[i]
  rows <- studies_pre$Study == review_changes$Study[i]
  value <- review_changes$curated[i]
  studies_pre[[col]][rows] <- if (is.numeric(studies_pre[[col]])) as.numeric(value) else value
}
studies_pre <- derive_fields(studies_pre)

status_rank <- c("Not reported" = 0, "Neither group" = 0, "One group" = 1, "Both groups" = 2, "Reported" = 1)

completeness <- field_status(studies) |>
  left_join(select(field_status(studies_pre, review = FALSE), Study, field, status_pre = status), by = c("Study", "field")) |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, Year), by = "Study") |>
  mutate(
    Study = fct_reorder(Study, Year, .fun = min),
    complete = status %in% c("Both groups", "Reported"),
    filled = status_rank[status] > status_rank[status_pre]
  ) |>
  mutate(field_label = paste0(field, " (", round(100 * mean(complete)), "%)"), .by = field)

field_order <- completeness |>
  summarise(pct = mean(complete), type = first(type), .by = field_label) |>
  arrange(type == "Study", pct) |>
  pull(field_label)

pal_status <- c(
  "Both groups" = "#2a78d6", "One group" = "#9ec5f4", "Neither group" = "#f0efec",
  "Reported" = "#256abf", "Not reported" = "#f0efec",
  # cells raised by the full-text review; shade shows both groups or one group, as for blue
  "Filled by review" = "#1a9e6e", "One group (review)" = "#a3dcc3", "Reported (review)" = "#178a60"
)

# year ticks: first study of each publication period
year_ticks <- studies |>
  arrange(Year) |>
  distinct(period, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(Study, Year)

completeness <- mutate(completeness, fill = case_when(
  !filled ~ status,
  status %in% c("Both groups") ~ "Filled by review",
  .default = paste(status, "(review)")
))

ggplot(completeness, aes(x = Study, y = factor(field_label, levels = field_order), fill = fill)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_status, breaks = c("Both groups", "One group", "Neither group", "Filled by review")) +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = year_ticks$Study, labels = year_ticks$Year) +
  labs(x = "Studies (ordered by publication year)", y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), panel.border = element_blank())
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each cell:** one study (column) × one field (row); all 119 studies. Columns ordered by publication year (1997–2025; ties in alphabetical order of study ID). Axis ticks label the first study of each period: 1997, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020.
- **Rows:** group-level fields (bottom block, sorted by completeness, lowest at bottom) then study-level fields (top block, same sorting). The % in each label is the share of the 119 studies that are dark blue in that row.
- **Group-level fields:** come from the `Group 0 …` and `Group 1 …` columns of the PerioSigDB sheet (`age mean`, `percent males`, `percent smokers`, `pocket depth mean (mm)`, `clinical attachment loss (mm)`, `bleeding on probing percent`, `plaque`, `suppuration percent`, `sample size`). A group counts as reported if its mean/percentage is non-missing; SDs are not considered. Group 0 is the comparison group, Group 1 periodontitis.
- **Plaque:** counted only when `Plaque measure` is "% sites" (40 studies have that measure); the 16 studies reporting a plaque index (e.g. Silness–Löe) count as "Neither group" even though a value is in the sheet.
- **Study-level fields:** profiling method is reported unless it falls in "Other / not reported" (method derived from `Sequencing type`: 16S, WMS → shotgun, PCR or 16S,PCR → PCR; otherwise `Sequencing platform` = DNA-DNA Hybridization; else other/not reported). Classification counts as reported unless "Periodontitis (type not specified)" (24 studies). Group definitions count as reported if non-empty, so the literal entry "ND" (9 Group 0, 2 Group 1 definitions) counts as reported.
- **Systemic rows:** `Systemic condition` non-missing → status shaded (100 studies: 92 "systemically healthy", 8 other entries); comorbidity row shaded only for the 3 entries naming a condition the participants have (not "non-diabetic", "HIV-negative" or "not restricted").
- **"One group" cells:** mostly missing comparison-group values for clinical measures (e.g. BOP: 5 studies with only the periodontitis group, 4 with only the comparison group); smokers lean the other way (2 comparison-only, 1 periodontitis-only).
- **Green cells (full-text review):** each cell's status is recomputed with the review's changes in `output/llm_annotation/review_log.csv` reverted to the curated values; a cell is green if its status is higher with the review (91 cells: 90 now reported for both groups or at study level, dark green; 1 for one group, light green, in the bleeding on probing row). Most are systemic health status (37) and periodontitis classification (16, from "type not specified" to a named type); the rest fill missing group values (e.g. bleeding on probing in 10 studies). Corrections to values that were already present, and the separate manual corrections, are not marked.
- **Statistical rows:** statistical test, significance threshold and multiple-testing correction were not in PerioSigDB before the full-text review, so every study reporting them is green (the 91 cells above exclude these rows). A study counts as reporting a field if any of its signatures has it; a multiple-testing correction recorded as not applied counts as reported. 2 studies have no statistical test recorded.
- **Example:** age is reported for both groups in 103 studies (87%), for one group in 2 (Studies 448, 1988), neither in 14.
- **Watch out:** study-level "Reported" uses a slightly darker blue (or green) than "Both groups", and light green (one group filled by review) is not in the legend. 16S variable region is a % of all 119 studies (16), not of 16S studies (16 of the 36 studies with sequencing type 16S or 16S,PCR).
:::

**Shows:** availability varies substantially across metadata fields, particularly for systemic health status and several clinical measures. Changes over time in the classification used are shown in "Periodontitis classification over time and by method".

**Caveat:** "Not reported" can also mean "not entered". Systemic health status was not extracted for about half the studies in the original overview sheet; the full-text review filled most of these, leaving 19 studies not recorded.

# Health vs periodontitis

## Paired study-level comparison

```{r paired-slopes}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Health (comparison group) vs periodontitis within each study. Small points: the group mean reported by each study; grey lines join the two groups of one study; large points: median of the group means across studies, for each group separately. n: studies reporting the measure for both groups; median difference: median across studies of the periodontitis minus health difference (not the difference between the two large points); p: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test across studies."

medians <- long |>
  semi_join(paired, by = c("Study", "feature")) |>
  summarise(median = median(mean), .by = c(label, group))

strip_labels <- paired_tests |>
  arrange(label) |>
  mutate(strip = paste0(label, "\nn = ", studies, ", median difference ", sprintf("%+.2g", diff), "\n", p_label)) |>
  mutate(strip = factor(strip, levels = strip)) |>
  select(label, strip)

long |>
  semi_join(paired, by = c("Study", "feature")) |>
  left_join(strip_labels, by = "label") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group, y = mean)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = Study), color = "grey60", alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(color = group), size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = left_join(medians, strip_labels, by = "label"),
            aes(y = median, group = 1), color = "grey15", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = left_join(medians, strip_labels, by = "label"),
             aes(y = median, fill = group), shape = 21, color = "white", size = 4, stroke = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~strip, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_group, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_group) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Data:** studies with a non-missing Group 0 and Group 1 value for the measure (same columns as in the completeness heatmap; plaque only when measured as % sites). Smokers: 45 studies with 0% in both groups (smokers excluded by design) are dropped, leaving 37 of 82. No other exclusions; e.g. Study 136 (all female) stays in males at 0% → 0%.
- **Small points/lines:** one study's reported group mean (or percentage); x position Health = Group 0 (comparison group), Periodontitis = Group 1. Free y axis per panel.
- **Large points:** median across the same studies of each group's values separately: age 37.4 vs 44.7 y; males 40.0 vs 41.7%; smokers 9.7 vs 28.8%; PD 2.0 vs 3.96 mm; CAL 1.15 vs 3.9 mm; BOP 7.7 vs 57.2%; plaque 21.4 vs 61.8%; suppuration 0 vs 3%.
- **Strip numbers:** n = studies with both groups; median difference = median of per-study (periodontitis − comparison) differences, printed to 2 significant figures (age +4.6, males +2, smokers +14, PD +2, CAL +2.5, BOP +45, plaque +37, suppuration +3).
- **Test:** paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test of Group 1 vs Group 0 values, two-sided, unit = study, normal approximation with continuity correction (`exact = FALSE`); zero differences are dropped. Unadjusted across the 8 measures; all are p < 0.001 except males (p = 0.019).
- **Direction counts (not shown):** periodontitis group higher in every study for PD (84/84), CAL (62), BOP (60), suppuration (21); plaque 37 higher, 1 lower; age 82 higher, 20 lower, 1 tie; males 54 / 34 / 11 ties; smokers 33 / 3 / 1.
- **Example:** Study 147 (2005, chronic periodontitis) reports age 37.5 → 47.2 y, males 53.3% → 38.5%, smokers 0% → 7.7%, PD 1.5 → 3.7 mm; it contributes one line to each of those four panels.
- **Watch out:** each study counts equally regardless of sample size; group values are study-reported means, so PD/CAL may be full-mouth or sampled-site values.
:::

**Shows:** the clinical measures separate the groups in nearly every study. The periodontitis group has the higher value in all 84 studies reporting probing depth, all 62 reporting attachment loss, all 60 reporting bleeding and 37 of 38 reporting plaque. The demographic measures are imbalanced rather than separating: periodontitis groups are older in 82 of 103 studies (median +4.6 years) and include more smokers in 33 of 37 (+14 points), so age and smoking travel with disease status across the corpus.

**Caveat:** each study counts equally, regardless of its sample size.

## PerioSigDB consensus taxa

The taxa that periodontitis studies report consistently in one direction, at the rank at which they were reported (mostly species). These consensus signatures are used in the analyses below and in the comparisons with other conditions in BugSigDB.

```{r consensus-taxa}
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| fig-cap: "PerioSigDB consensus taxa: taxa reported increased (left) or decreased (right) in periodontitis by more PerioSigDB signatures than in the other direction (exact binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures against 50%, unadjusted p < 0.05). Bars: signatures reporting the taxon increased (right) or decreased (left); faded: not significant after Benjamini–Hochberg correction across all taxa tested. Numbers: unadjusted p. Circles: participants (both groups) of the studies reporting the taxon in its consensus direction, each study counted once. Rows ordered by p within each direction."
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.R
consensus_data <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.rds")[c("consensus", "taxon_tests")]
rank_names <- c(g = "genus", f = "family", o = "order", c = "class", p = "phylum", k = "kingdom")

# terminal NCBI ID of each reported taxon, with its name and rank
sig_ids <- tibble(
  Study = dat$Study, direction = dat$`Abundance in Group 1`,
  id = map(dat$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`, \(x) paste0("NCBITaxon:", sub("^.*[|]", "", x))),
  full = dat$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`
) |>
  unnest(c(id, full))
consensus_names <- distinct(sig_ids, id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  transmute(id, rank = substr(sub("^.*[|]", "", full), 1, 1),
            name = gsub("_", " ", sub("^.*[|][a-z]__", "", full)),
            label = name)

consensus_participants <- sig_ids |>
  distinct(Study, direction, id) |>
  left_join(transmute(studies, Study, n = `Group 0 sample size` + `Group 1 sample size`), by = "Study") |>
  summarise(participants = sum(n, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(id, direction))

consensus_taxa <- tibble(
  id = unlist(consensus_data$consensus),
  direction = rep(names(consensus_data$consensus), lengths(consensus_data$consensus))
) |>
  left_join(mutate(consensus_data$taxon_tests, fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) |>
              select(id = ids, increased, decreased, p, fdr), by = "id") |>
  left_join(consensus_names, by = "id") |>
  left_join(consensus_participants, by = c("id", "direction")) |>
  arrange(p, desc(increased + decreased)) |>
  mutate(direction = factor(direction, levels = c("increased", "decreased"),
                            labels = c("Increased in periodontitis", "Decreased in periodontitis")),
         label = factor(label, levels = rev(unique(label))))

# one panel per direction, side by side; bars on the same scale, rows the same height
consensus_panel <- function(dir_label, title) {
  d <- filter(consensus_taxa, direction == dir_label) |> mutate(label = droplevels(label))
  bars <- d |>
    pivot_longer(c(increased, decreased), names_to = "sig_direction", values_to = "n") |>
    mutate(n = ifelse(sig_direction == "decreased", -n, n))
  max_n <- max(abs(c(consensus_taxa$increased, consensus_taxa$decreased)))
  ggplot(bars, aes(x = n, y = label)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = sig_direction, alpha = fdr < 0.05), width = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(data = d, aes(x = -max_n * 0.45, label = ifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))),
              hjust = 1, size = 2.1, color = "grey30") +
    geom_point(data = d, aes(x = max_n * 1.12, size = participants),
               shape = 21, fill = "grey65", color = "grey20", stroke = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6"),
                      labels = c(increased = "Increased", decreased = "Decreased"), name = "PerioSigDB\nsignatures") +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1, `FALSE` = 0.45),
                       labels = c(`TRUE` = "FDR < 0.05", `FALSE` = "p < 0.05"), name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 4.5, limits = c(0, max(consensus_taxa$participants, na.rm = TRUE)),
                    breaks = c(500, 2000, 5000), name = "Participants") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = abs, limits = c(-max_n * 0.62, max_n * 1.2), breaks = c(-25, 0, 25, 50, 75)) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Signatures", y = NULL) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic", size = 7.5),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 9.5, face = "bold"))
}
n_up <- sum(consensus_taxa$direction == "Increased in periodontitis")
n_down <- sum(consensus_taxa$direction == "Decreased in periodontitis")

# the decreased panel takes the height of its rows at the top of the right column, the legends the
# space below it, so the figure spans the full width without a legend column
wrap_plots(A = consensus_panel("Increased in periodontitis", "Increased in periodontitis"),
           B = consensus_panel("Decreased in periodontitis", "Decreased in periodontitis"),
           C = guide_area(), design = "AB\nAC") +
  plot_layout(heights = c(n_down, n_up - n_down), guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.direction = "vertical", legend.box = "vertical", legend.box.just = "left",
        legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7), legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Taxa:** each reported taxon is matched by its terminal NCBI ID, at the rank at which the study reported it, so a species and its genus are separate taxa. A study reporting the genus *Prevotella* and another reporting *Prevotella intermedia* count for different rows.
- **Test:** for each taxon, an exact binomial test of its increased vs decreased PerioSigDB signatures against 50%; consensus: unadjusted p < 0.05 (`r length(consensus_data$consensus$increased)` increased, `r length(consensus_data$consensus$decreased)` decreased of `r nrow(consensus_data$taxon_tests)` taxa tested). Faded bars do not pass Benjamini–Hochberg correction across all taxa tested.
- **Use:** these taxa are the consensus signatures of the similarity analyses and the participant-level figures below. The genus-level analyses compared with BugSigDB use the top 20 genera per direction instead (see the taxon set table above).
:::

## Participant characteristics of studies reporting the top consensus taxa

::::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" title="Show section"}

```{r consensus-taxa-characteristics}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8.5
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-group probing depth, age and share of males in the studies reporting each of the top 10 consensus taxa in its consensus direction (rows; red: increased, blue: decreased in periodontitis; each panel ordered by its median, highest at top). One point per study; boxes: median and interquartile range; whiskers: up to 1.5 × the interquartile range. Grey: all PerioSigDB studies with a value, for reference. Numbers at right: studies in each box. Consensus taxa: binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures, unadjusted p < 0.05."
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.R
consensus_tests <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.rds")[c("consensus", "taxon_tests")]

# each signature's taxa as terminal NCBI IDs with their names
sig_taxa <- tibble(
  Study = dat$Study, direction = dat$`Abundance in Group 1`,
  id = map(dat$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`, \(x) paste0("NCBITaxon:", sub("^.*[|]", "", x))),
  name = map(dat$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, \(x) sub("^.*[|][a-z]__", "", x))
) |>
  unnest(c(id, name))

top_consensus <- tibble(
  id = unlist(consensus_tests$consensus),
  direction = rep(names(consensus_tests$consensus), lengths(consensus_tests$consensus))
) |>
  left_join(select(consensus_tests$taxon_tests, id = ids, increased, decreased), by = "id") |>
  mutate(n_sigs = ifelse(direction == "increased", increased, decreased)) |>
  slice_max(n_sigs, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE, by = direction) |>
  left_join(distinct(sig_taxa, id, name), by = "id")

all_label <- "All PerioSigDB studies"
taxon_values <- filter(long, group == "Periodontitis", feature %in% c("pd", "age", "males")) |>
  select(Study, label, mean)

taxon_characteristics <- bind_rows(
  sig_taxa |>
    semi_join(top_consensus, by = c("id", "direction")) |>
    distinct(Study, direction, name) |>
    inner_join(taxon_values, by = "Study", relationship = "many-to-many"),
  map_dfr(c("increased", "decreased"), \(dir) mutate(taxon_values, direction = dir, name = all_label))
) |>
  mutate(
    name = factor(name, levels = c(all_label, rev(top_consensus$name))),
    direction = factor(direction, levels = c("increased", "decreased"),
                       labels = c("Increased in periodontitis", "Decreased in periodontitis")),
    label = factor(label, levels = c("Probing depth (mm)", "Age (years)", "Males (%)")),
    fill = case_when(name == all_label ~ "grey85", direction == "Increased in periodontitis" ~ "#e8a598",
                     .default = "#9fbbe0")
  )

# each panel has its own row order: taxa by median, highest at top, with all studies at the bottom
row_order <- taxon_characteristics |>
  summarise(median = median(mean), .by = c(direction, label, name)) |>
  mutate(row = paste(direction, label, name, sep = "|")) |>
  arrange(name != all_label, median)
taxon_characteristics <- mutate(taxon_characteristics, row = factor(paste(direction, label, name, sep = "|"),
                                                                    levels = row_order$row))

ggplot(taxon_characteristics, aes(mean, row)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = fill), outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6, linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_quasirandom(orientation = "y", size = 0.7, alpha = 0.5, width = 0.2) +
  geom_text(data = count(taxon_characteristics, direction, label, row), aes(x = Inf, label = n),
            hjust = 1.3, size = 2.6, color = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.12))) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) sub(".*[|]", "", x)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(direction, label), scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Taxa:** the PerioSigDB consensus, precomputed alongside the whole-signature similarity analysis. Taxa are matched by terminal NCBI ID at the reported rank (species and genus entries are separate). Per taxon: exact binomial test (two-sided, against 50%) of PerioSigDB signatures listing it increased vs decreased; consensus = p < 0.05, unadjusted, in the majority direction (32 increased, 12 decreased taxa).
- **Rows:** the 10 consensus taxa per direction with the most signatures in their consensus direction (no ties at the cut-off). Increased: *P. gingivalis* 73, *T. forsythia* 68, *T. denticola* 44, *P. intermedia* 37, *F. alocis* 31, *C. rectus* 25, *P. endodontalis* 23, *P. micra* 22, *F. nucleatum* 20, *[Eubacterium] saphenum* 19. Decreased: *S. sanguinis* 21, *R. dentocariosa* 16, *A. naeslundii* 14, *H. parainfluenzae* 14, *C. matruchotii* 12, *L. mirabilis* 11, *R. aeria* 9, *G. adiacens* 9, *G. haemolysans* 7, *C. durum* 7.
- **Signatures = studies here:** each study has at most one increased and one decreased signature, so these counts are also study counts.
- **Each point:** one study listing the taxon in the consensus direction, placed at its periodontitis-group (Group 1) value: `pocket depth mean (mm)`, `age mean`, `percent males`. Studies missing the value are dropped from that panel, so box n is below the signature count.
- **Grey reference row:** all PerioSigDB studies with a Group 1 value (PD 91, age 104, males 102), median PD 4.0 mm, age 44.8 y, males 42.3%. The same row is repeated in both direction panels.
- **Boxes:** median and IQR; whiskers to 1.5 × IQR; outliers not drawn separately (all studies shown as points). Numbers at right: studies in the box.
- **Example:** *P. gingivalis* (73 increased, 0 decreased signatures; p = 2.1e-22): 56 of its 73 studies report Group 1 PD, median 3.98 mm (IQR 3.44–5.91) vs 4.0 mm overall. *C. matruchotii* decreased: 8 studies with PD, median 6.4 mm; *R. aeria*: 6 studies, median 6.31 mm.
- **No test:** descriptive; the same study appears in many rows (e.g. 62 of the 73 *P. gingivalis* studies also list *T. forsythia*).
:::

**Shows:** for most of the top consensus taxa, the studies reporting them have periodontitis groups with probing depths, ages and shares of males similar to PerioSigDB as a whole, so these taxa are not reported only by studies of unusually severe disease or of particular age or sex groups. The exceptions are among the less-reported decreased taxa: the few studies reporting *Corynebacterium matruchotii* and *Rothia aeria* decreased have higher median probing depths than PerioSigDB overall.

**Caveat:** this is descriptive, with no test: the same studies appear in many rows, and rows with fewer than about 10 studies are uncertain. Probing depth is reported by fewer studies than age, and some studies report it for the sampled sites rather than the full mouth, which may raise values in studies that sampled the deepest pockets.

:::::

## Abundance of the top consensus taxa in individual participants

::::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" title="Show section"}

The figure above places each study at its group means. Five PerioSigDB 16S studies deposited their reads with participant annotations, so the same taxa can also be compared across individual sites. Two of them (Studies 484 and 1411) record the probing depth of the sampled site, shown here.

```{r participant-data}
# per-sample abundance of the top consensus species in the PerioSigDB studies with deposited reads and
# participant annotations (scripts/participant_data_1-download.R and participant_data_2-dada2.R);
# subgingival plaque of healthy and untreated periodontitis participants only
participant_samples <- read.csv("../../output/participant_data/sample_metadata.csv") |>
  filter(site == "subgingival plaque", status %in% c("healthy", "periodontitis")) |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(status == "healthy", "Health", "Periodontitis"))

participant_abundance <- read.csv("../../output/participant_data/taxon_abundance.csv") |>
  filter(rank == "species") |>
  transmute(Study, run_accession, id = paste0("NCBITaxon:", ncbi_taxon_id), abundance = 100 * relative_abundance) |>
  inner_join(select(top_consensus, id, direction, name), by = "id") |>
  inner_join(participant_samples, by = c("Study", "run_accession")) |>
  # a species never detected in a study is mostly one its 16S region cannot tell apart from relatives,
  # so it is left out of that study rather than counted as absent
  filter(any(abundance > 0), .by = c(Study, id)) |>
  mutate(name = factor(name, levels = top_consensus$name))

# probing depth of the sampled site: categories in Study 484 (as defined in the paper; no mm deposited);
# in Study 1411, the range of the participants' mean probing depths in each group
pd_levels <- c("Healthy", "≤ 3", "4–6", "≥ 7")
abundance_by_pd <- participant_abundance |>
  filter(Study %in% c("Study 484", "Study 1411")) |>
  mutate(category = case_when(
    status == "healthy" ~ pd_levels[1],
    pd_category == "shallow" ~ pd_levels[2],
    pd_category == "intermediate" ~ pd_levels[3],
    .default = pd_levels[4]
  )) |>
  mutate(category = if (first(Study) == "Study 1411") {
    paste0(min(pd_mm), "–", max(pd_mm))
  } else category, .by = c(Study, status)) |>
  mutate(category = fct_relevel(factor(category), pd_levels[pd_levels %in% category]))

# one column per study and consensus direction, one row per species; a species not detected in a
# study leaves an empty panel
plot_pd <- function(dir, study) {
  d <- filter(abundance_by_pd, direction == dir, Study == study) |>
    mutate(name = factor(name, levels = intersect(levels(name), abundance_by_pd$name[abundance_by_pd$direction == dir])),
           category = droplevels(category))
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(category, abundance)) +
    geom_boxplot(aes(fill = group), outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.7, linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_quasirandom(aes(color = group), width = 0.15, size = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
    labs(x = if (study == "Study 484") "Site probing depth (mm)" else "Mean probing depth (mm)") +
    theme(strip.text.y = if (study == "Study 484") element_blank() else
            element_text(face = "bold.italic", angle = 0, hjust = 0))
  p +
    scale_y_continuous(transform = scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 0.01, base = 10),
                       breaks = c(0, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 50), labels = \(x) format(x, drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal_group, guide = "none") +
    scale_color_manual(values = pal_group) +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(name), drop = FALSE) +
    labs(y = "Relative abundance (%)", title = paste0(str_to_sentence(dir), ": ", study)) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 11), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1)))
}
```

### By probing depth of the sampled site

```{r participant-pd}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-cap: "Relative abundance of the top consensus species in subgingival plaque, by the probing depth of the sampled site (one point per sample). Study 484: categories of site probing depth (no mm deposited); healthy participants' sites form one category, the others are sites of periodontitis participants; Study 1411: each participant's sites were pooled, so one box per group (healthy, periodontitis; shown by color), labelled with the range of the participants' mean probing depths. Boxes: median and interquartile range, whiskers up to 1.5 × the interquartile range. Empty panels: species not detected in that study. Pseudo-log scale, so samples without the species are shown at 0."
wrap_plots(
  plot_pd("increased", "Study 484"), plot_pd("increased", "Study 1411"),
  plot_pd("decreased", "Study 484"), plot_pd("decreased", "Study 1411"),
  nrow = 1, widths = c(4, 2, 4, 2)  # panel width per category, so boxes match across studies
) + plot_layout(guides = "collect", axis_titles = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "top")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Studies:** the figure uses Studies 484 and 1411, the two with probing depth per sample. They are among the five PerioSigDB 16S studies whose reads are public and whose samples are annotated with health status, age and sex (also used for the co-occurrence figures): 484 (V4, Illumina), 1411 (V1–V3, 454), 1141 (V3, Illumina), 191 (V3–V4, Illumina, reverse reads only) and 428 (V3–V4, Illumina). Other studies either deposited no reads, deposited only some groups (e.g. Study 639: healthy participants only) or have no per-sample annotations. Reads and annotations: `scripts/participant_data_1-download.R`; processing: `scripts/participant_data_2-dada2.R`; outputs in `output/participant_data/`.
- **Processing (precomputed):** each study run through DADA2 with settings for its read layout; genus from the HOMD 16S RefSeq (V16.03) by the naive Bayesian classifier, species by exact match to HOMD, then mapped to NCBI taxon IDs. An exact match to several species is left at genus rank, so species that a region cannot separate are not counted (e.g. *Campylobacter rectus* and *C. showae*, *Gemella haemolysans* and other *Gemella*); *[Eubacterium] saphenum* had no exact match in any study. These three of the 20 top consensus species have no panels.
- **Samples:** subgingival plaque only (supragingival plaque, tongue and feces samples in Studies 1141 and 428 excluded), and only healthy and untreated periodontitis participants (Study 191's treated samples excluded). Two runs could not be downloaded in a usable form (one each in Studies 1141 and 428).
- **Species not detected:** a species never detected in a study's subgingival samples is left out of that study, because this mostly reflects the region sequenced rather than absence (e.g. *Treponema denticola* in the V4 study 484; *Actinomyces naeslundii* is detected in three of the five studies).
- **Probing depth:** Study 484 sampled sites by probing depth, as shallow (≤ 3 mm), moderate (4–6 mm) or deep (≥ 7 mm) in its Methods, with several sites per participant (healthy 21 sites from 7 participants; periodontitis 26, 27 and 27 sites from 9). Study 1411 pooled sites per participant and recorded their mean probing depth in mm; the figure shows one box per group with the range of these means (healthy 13 participants at 1–2 mm; periodontitis 18 at 5–8 mm). Study 484 deposited only the categories. Sites of ≤ 3 mm in periodontitis participants come from Study 484 only.
- **Relative abundance:** reads of the species as % of the sample's reads after quality filtering and chimera removal; scales are not comparable across 16S regions in absolute terms.
- **No test:** descriptive; the studies differ in region, platform and population, and sites from the same participant are not independent.
:::

**Shows:** within periodontitis participants, the abundance of the consensus taxa follows the depth of the sampled site. In Study 484, shallow (≤ 3 mm) sites of periodontitis participants resemble healthy participants' sites for the decreased taxa (e.g. *Streptococcus sanguinis* median 1.2% vs 1.5% in health and 0.07% at 4–6 mm), and have intermediate levels of the increased taxa (*Porphyromonas gingivalis* 0.11% vs 0.04% in health and 4.6% at 4–6 mm). This is what Study 484 itself reported (shallow sites of periodontitis participants cluster with healthy sites, and health-associated taxa fall and *T. forsythia* and *F. alocis* rise with pocket depth); here it is shown for the PerioSigDB consensus species, with Study 1411 adding healthy and moderate-to-deep sites but no shallow sites of periodontitis participants.

**Caveat:** the comparison rests on two studies with 7–18 participants per group, using different 16S regions, and mostly on Study 484.

:::::

## Participant characteristics and clinical measures by periodontitis classification

::::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" title="Show section"}

```{r within-perio}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-group values across studies, by the periodontitis classification reported (one point per study). Bars are medians; numbers below are the studies in each panel. Smokers at 0% are mostly studies that excluded smokers."

within <- long |>
  filter(group == "Periodontitis", feature %in% c("age", "smokers", "pd", "cal", "bop")) |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, classification), by = "Study")

ggplot(within, aes(x = classification, y = mean, color = classification)) +
  geom_quasirandom(size = 1.8, width = 0.3, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.6, linewidth = 0.4, color = "grey15") +
  geom_text(data = count(within, label, classification), aes(y = -Inf, label = n), vjust = -0.5,
            size = 2.8, color = "grey35") +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_class) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each point:** one study's periodontitis-group (Group 1) mean or percentage; only Group 1 is used, so studies missing the comparison-group value are included (unlike the paired figure).
- **Data:** age, smokers, PD, CAL and BOP only (males, plaque, suppuration not shown). Smokers include 0% values (45 of 83 studies), i.e. no exclusion of smoker-free studies.
- **Classification:** from the `Periodontitis classification` column, shortened: Chronic, Chronic + aggressive (studies including both), Aggressive, Stage/grade (2017/2018 classification), Refractory, Not specified ("type not specified").
- **Bars:** median per classification. Medians (age / smokers / PD / CAL / BOP): Chronic 46.2 / 0 / 4.55 / 4.2 / 54.7; Chronic + aggressive 40.6 / 28.9 / 4.57 / 4.12 / 59.7; Aggressive 26.8 / 0 / 4.43 / 4.41 / 72; Stage/grade 43.3 / 0 / 3.59 / 3.7 / 68; Not specified 47.7 / 0 / 3.65 / 1.92 / 43.2.
- **Numbers below:** studies per box. Age: 49, 12, 8, 17, 1, 17 (Chronic → Not specified order); smokers 40, 8, 6, 16, 1, 12; PD 42, 8, 8, 16, 1, 16; CAL 32, 6, 7, 14, 1, 11; BOP 32, 6, 5, 11, 1, 10.
- **Example:** Refractory is one study (Study 1867): age 51, smokers 59%, PD 3.9 mm, CAL 4.2 mm, BOP 53%, so its "bar" is that single value. Aggressive age values range from 23.7 (Study 1085) to 39.4 (Study 1986).
- **No test:** descriptive only.
- **Watch out:** a smokers median of 0 (Chronic, Aggressive, Stage/grade, Not specified) reflects studies that excluded smokers, not low smoking among recruited patients.
:::

**Shows:** "periodontitis" does not describe the same patients in every study. Studies using the historical aggressive classification recruited much younger patients (median 26.8 years against 46.2 for chronic) with the most attachment loss (4.41 mm) and bleeding (72% of sites), while their probing depths match chronic studies (4.43 vs 4.55 mm). Stage/grade and unspecified studies span the widest range.

**Caveat:** some categories have few studies (e.g. refractory n = 1). Some studies report PD and CAL for the sampled sites rather than the full mouth. These values are not directly comparable and may be higher when sampling targets deeper or more affected sites.

:::::

## Trends over publication year

```{r trends}
# slope per decade of each periodontitis-group measure against publication year (no figure: only the
# smokers slope reaches p < 0.05, and it tracks exclusion criteria rather than the patients recruited)
trend_p <- within |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, Year), by = "Study") |>
  summarise(studies = n(), slope = 10 * coef(lm(mean ~ Year))[2],
            p = summary(lm(mean ~ Year))$coefficients["Year", 4], .by = label)
tv <- \(lab, col) trend_p[[col]][trend_p$label == lab]
tp <- \(lab) signif(tv(lab, "p"), 2)
```

Periodontitis groups changed little across three decades of publications. Per decade, reported age rises `r sprintf("%+.1f", tv("Age (years)", "slope"))` years (p = `r tp("Age (years)")`), bleeding on probing `r sprintf("%+.1f", tv("Bleeding on probing (% sites)", "slope"))` points (p = `r tp("Bleeding on probing (% sites)")`), clinical attachment loss `r sprintf("%+.1f", tv("Clinical attachment loss (mm)", "slope"))` mm (p = `r tp("Clinical attachment loss (mm)")`) and probing depth `r sprintf("%+.2f", tv("Probing depth (mm)", "slope"))` mm (p = `r tp("Probing depth (mm)")`); none of the four reaches p < 0.05. The share of smokers falls `r sprintf("%.1f", -tv("Smokers (%)", "slope"))` points per decade (p = `r tp("Smokers (%)")`), which tracks exclusion criteria rather than smoking among the patients recruited: many recent studies excluded smokers and report 0%.

Each slope is an unweighted least-squares fit over the studies reporting that measure for the periodontitis group (age `r tv("Age (years)", "studies")`, smokers `r tv("Smokers (%)", "studies")`, probing depth `r tv("Probing depth (mm)", "studies")`, attachment loss `r tv("Clinical attachment loss (mm)", "studies")`, bleeding on probing `r tv("Bleeding on probing (% sites)", "studies")`), unadjusted across the five measures, against publication year rather than recruitment year.

# Study characteristics

## Periodontitis classification over time and by method

```{r classification}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "(A) Periodontitis classification of studies by publication period (share of studies; counts in bars). (B) Number of studies by classification and profiling method."

pA <- studies |>
  count(period, classification) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), .by = period) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = prop, y = fct_rev(period), fill = classification)) +
  geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(prop > 0.06, n, "")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
            color = "white", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_class) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Studies", y = NULL, tag = "A") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

pB <- studies |>
  count(classification, method) |>
  complete(classification, method, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = method, y = fct_rev(classification), fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(n > 0, n, ""), color = n > 12), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f0efec", high = "#1c5cab", guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey15", `TRUE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, tag = "B") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

pA + pB + plot_layout(widths = c(1.2, 1))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Data:** all 119 studies, one each; classification from `Periodontitis classification` (shortened labels; "Not specified" = type not specified), period from `Year` (1995–2004, 2005–09, 2010–14, 2015–19, 2020–25).
- **A, each bar:** one period, studies = 100%; segments are classifications. Studies per period: 13, 27, 28, 22, 29.
- **A, numbers:** study counts, printed only for segments > 6% of the bar. Hidden: 2005–09 Chronic + aggressive (1) and Refractory (1); 2015–19 Aggressive (1).
- **A, counts by period (Chronic / Chronic + aggressive / Aggressive / Stage/grade / Refractory / Not specified):** 1995–2004 6/2/1/0/0/4; 2005–09 17/1/3/0/1/5; 2010–14 13/5/3/0/0/7; 2015–19 16/3/1/0/0/2; 2020–25 4/2/0/17/0/6.
- **B, each cell:** studies with that classification and profiling method; blank = 0; white text when > 12. Method from `Sequencing type` (16S; WMS → shotgun; PCR or 16S,PCR → PCR), else `Sequencing platform` = DNA-DNA Hybridization; otherwise "Other / not reported" (13 studies with no sequencing type and a platform other than hybridization or none, e.g. culture).
- **Example:** stage/grade studies are mostly 16S (12 of 17; 2 shotgun, 2 PCR, 1 other, none hybridization); chronic studies are mostly PCR (21 of 56) and hybridization (14).
- **Full-text review:** 16 studies curated as "type not specified" were assigned the classification their paper reports (12 chronic, 2 chronic and aggressive, 2 stage/grade), so "Not specified" fell from 40 to 24 studies; one study curated as aggressive was corrected to chronic.
- **No test.**
:::

**Shows:** the terminology used to classify periodontitis changed over time, from the chronic/aggressive categories of the 1999 classification to staging and grading (2017 World Workshop classification, published in 2018) in the most recent period. Studies are grouped by the classification terminology they report; stage/grade is a framework rather than a disease type directly interchangeable with chronic or aggressive periodontitis. Panel B shows which classifications each profiling method has studied.

**Caveat:** "Not specified" is still sizeable (24 studies). Many older studies define periodontitis only by PD/CAL thresholds.

## Systemic health status of participants

Most PerioSigDB studies compare systemically healthy groups: 92 of the 119 studies record their participants as systemically healthy and 19 record nothing. Five screened for one condition only or not at all (non-diabetic: Studies 1411, 1581 and 2044; HIV-negative: 2053; not restricted: 538). Three compare groups whose participants have a named condition: dyspepsia (Study 126), cardiovascular disease and diabetes in the periodontitis group only (766), and hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia and diabetes (2025-187, no full text to check). Those three are the candidates for a sensitivity analysis.

The full-text review changed this picture in two ways. Seven studies entered with a systemic condition (rheumatoid arthritis 129; COPD 515 and 2025-180; diabetes 734, 1411 and 2025-Embase-55; hypertension 2025-231) in fact took their signature from a pair of systemically healthy or non-diabetic groups, and 37 studies with no entry were filled from the paper. Two further rheumatoid arthritis studies (450, 2025-PubMed-130) are excluded altogether, because their signatures are not a health vs periodontitis comparison.

**Caveat:** "not recorded" means neither the overview sheet nor the paper states it, not that the participants were healthy. "Systemically healthy" is the authors' description, usually an exclusion criterion.

# Comparison with BugSigDB

```{r bugsigdb-load}
# BugSigDB export (cached by bugsigdbr; version date from its message or warning)
bsdb_version <- NA_character_
version_from <- function(cnd) {
  if (grepl("version from", conditionMessage(cnd))) bsdb_version <<- substr(trimws(sub(".*from ", "", conditionMessage(cnd))), 1, 10)
}
bsdb <- withCallingHandlers(
  bugsigdbr::importBugSigDB(),
  message = \(m) { version_from(m); invokeRestart("muffleMessage") },
  warning = \(w) { version_from(w); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") }
)
if (is.na(bsdb_version)) bsdb_version <- format(Sys.Date())

# body site group of each listed body site: the first matching pattern wins (so skin of the cheek is skin,
# the oropharynx upper airway); sites matching none are "other" (e.g. blood, milk, pancreas)
site_rules <- c(
  skin = "^skin|^cheek$|forehead|axilla|interdigital",
  eye = "conjunctiv|tear film|eyelid|meibum|ocular",
  oral = "plaque|saliva|mouth|oral cavity|oral opening|tongue|gingiv|buccal|lip$|cheek pouch",
  `upper airway` = "pharyn|throat|nasal|nose|upper respiratory|tonsil",
  `lower airway` = "lung|sputum|bronch|trachea",
  gastrointestinal = paste0("feces|colon|colorect|intestin|caecum|cecum|rectum|rectal|ileum|ileal|jejunum|duoden|",
                            "stomach|gastric|esophag|meconium|digestive|bile"),
  urogenital = "vagin|cervi|uter|endometri|ovary|fallopian|placenta|urine|urinary|urethra|genitalia|prostate|penis"
)
site_of <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(x)
  group <- rep("other", length(x))
  for (g in rev(names(site_rules))) group[grepl(site_rules[[g]], x, ignore.case = TRUE)] <- g
  group
}
# any of a signature's body sites is oral
is_oral <- function(sites) map_lgl(strsplit(sites, ","), \(x) any(site_of(x) == "oral"))

# BugSigDB without its periodontitis signatures (PerioSigDB is the reference for those)
bsdb_other <- filter(bsdb, !grepl("periodont", Condition, ignore.case = TRUE))

db_levels <- c("PerioSigDB", "BugSigDB")
pal_db <- setNames(c("#1baf7a", "#6250d6"), db_levels)

# genera of the taxa in a signature (taxa above genus rank are dropped)
genera <- function(x) unique(sub("^.*g__([^|]+).*$", "\\1", x[grepl("g__", x)]))

sig_genera <- function(d) {
  tibble(
    sig = seq_len(nrow(d)), Condition = d$Condition, `Body site` = d$`Body site`,
    direction = d$`Abundance in Group 1`, taxon = map(d$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, genera)
  ) |>
    unnest(taxon)
}
```

PerioSigDB uses BugSigDB's format, so its signatures can be compared with signatures from other microbiome studies. These analyses use the BugSigDB export of `r bsdb_version`, with `r n_distinct(bsdb$PMID)` studies and `r nrow(bsdb)` signatures across all conditions and body sites. BugSigDB's own periodontitis signatures (`r nrow(bsdb) - nrow(bsdb_other)`) are excluded throughout.

## Profiling methods and taxonomic resolution

```{r bsdb-methods}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| fig-cap: "(A) Profiling method of signatures (share of signatures). (B) Taxonomic rank of the taxa in signatures (share of taxon occurrences: a taxon listed in several signatures counts once per signature). BugSigDB includes all conditions and body sites except periodontitis."

method_of <- function(type, platform) {
  case_when(
    type == "16S" ~ "16S rRNA sequencing",
    type == "WMS" ~ "Shotgun metagenomics",
    type %in% c("PCR", "16S,PCR") ~ "PCR",
    platform == "DNA-DNA Hybridization" ~ "DNA-DNA hybridization",
    .default = "Other / not reported"
  ) |>
    factor(levels = method_levels)
}

methods_db <- bind_rows(
  dat |> transmute(db = "PerioSigDB", method = method_of(`Sequencing type`, `Sequencing platform`)),
  bsdb_other |> transmute(db = "BugSigDB", method = method_of(`Sequencing type`, `Sequencing platform`))
) |>
  count(db, method) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), db = factor(db, levels = rev(db_levels)), .by = db)

rank_names <- c(s = "Species", g = "Genus", f = "Family", o = "Order", c = "Class", p = "Phylum", k = "Kingdom")
pal_rank <- c(Species = "#184f95", Genus = "#3987e5", Family = "#86b6ef", Higher = "#cde2fb")

ranks_db <- bind_rows(
  tibble(db = "PerioSigDB", taxon = unlist(dat$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`)),
  tibble(db = "BugSigDB", taxon = unlist(bsdb_other$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`))
) |>
  mutate(
    rank = rank_names[substr(sub(".*[|]", "", taxon), 1, 1)],
    rank = factor(ifelse(rank %in% c("Species", "Genus", "Family"), rank, "Higher"), levels = names(pal_rank))
  ) |>
  count(db, rank) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), db = factor(db, levels = rev(db_levels)), .by = db)

stack_bar <- function(d, fill, pal, tag) {
  ggplot(d, aes(x = prop, y = db, fill = {{ fill }})) +
    geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(prop >= 0.06, scales::percent(prop, 1), "")),
              position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE), color = "white", size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, tag = tag) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
}

stack_bar(methods_db, method, pal_method, "A") +
  stack_bar(ranks_db, rank, pal_rank, "B") +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.3, 1))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Unit:** signatures, not studies. PerioSigDB: all 187 signatures (116 increased, 71 decreased; 68 studies contribute two). BugSigDB: 8,114 signatures from 1,371 studies, i.e. the cached bugsigdbr export minus the 49 signatures whose `Condition` contains "periodont"; all conditions, body sites, comparisons and directions.
- **A:** method per signature, derived from `Sequencing type` and `Sequencing platform` exactly as for PerioSigDB studies. PerioSigDB: 16S 33% (62), shotgun 9.1% (17), DNA-DNA hybridization 24% (45), PCR 24% (45; includes 6 signatures typed 16S,PCR), other/not reported 9.6% (18). BugSigDB: 16S 83% (6,715), shotgun 15% (1,196), PCR 1% (84), hybridization 2 signatures, other 1.4% (117; 18S 9, ITS 37, no type 71).
- **B:** rank of each taxon occurrence, from the last level prefix of its MetaPhlAn name (`s__`, `g__`, `f__`; order, class, phylum, kingdom pooled as "Higher"). PerioSigDB: species 89% (1,780), genus 8% (164), family 1.3%, higher 1.3%. BugSigDB: species 32% (20,813), genus 42% (27,494), family 13%, higher 13%.
- **Bar labels:** percentages shown only for segments ≥ 6%.
- **Example:** a *P. gingivalis* entry in 73 PerioSigDB signatures adds 73 species occurrences to B.
- **No test.**
:::

**Shows:** targeted PCR and checkerboard DNA–DNA hybridization together account for about half of PerioSigDB signatures, and most reported taxa are species. BugSigDB signatures come predominantly from sequencing studies and include a broader mix of taxonomic ranks, with genus the largest category. This is the main structural difference between the two databases, and it is why the comparison of taxa across conditions below works at genus level. Signature length follows the assay: the median PerioSigDB signature has 10 taxa for 16S, 9 for shotgun, 4 for hybridization and 3 for PCR, against 4, 5 and 2 in BugSigDB.

**Caveat:** targeted assays measure a predefined list of taxa, so in those studies a taxon missing from a signature may simply not have been measured (see "Assay coverage" above).

## Metadata captured by each database

```{r bsdb-fields}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Share of signatures with each field filled in, by database. PerioSigDB records participant and clinical characteristics; its statistical-method, matching and diversity fields were added by the full-text review. Case group: periodontitis in PerioSigDB, the condition in BugSigDB; control group: health in PerioSigDB. 16S variable region: share of 16S signatures only (not applicable to other methods). –: field not in the database."

filled <- function(x) {
  if (is.list(x)) return(lengths(x) > 0)
  !is.na(x) & !(as.character(x) %in% c("", "NA"))
}
field_share <- function(d, db, fields) {
  tibble(
    db = db, field = fields,
    share = map_dbl(fields, \(f) {
      if (!f %in% names(d)) return(NA_real_)
      # variable region applies to 16S signatures only
      keep <- if (f == "16S variable region") d$`Sequencing type` %in% c("16S", "16S,PCR") else TRUE
      mean(filled(d[[f]][keep]))
    })
  )
}

shared_fields <- c("Group 1 definition", "Group 0 sample size", "Group 1 sample size",
                   "Sequencing type", "16S variable region", "Sequencing platform", "Location of subjects")
bsdb_fields <- c("Statistical test", "Significance threshold", "MHT correction", "LDA Score above",
                 "Matched on", "Confounders controlled for", "Antibiotics exclusion", "Shannon", "Richness")
perio_fields <- c("Group 0 definition", "Periodontitis classification", "Systemic condition",
                  "Group 1 age mean", "Group 1 percent males", "Group 1 percent smokers",
                  "Group 1 pocket depth mean (mm)", "Group 1 clinical attachment loss (mm)",
                  "Group 1 bleeding on probing percent", "Group 1 plaque")
all_fields <- c(shared_fields, bsdb_fields, perio_fields)
# fields shared with BugSigDB name the case and control groups; PerioSigDB-only fields are periodontitis and health
field_label <- function(x) {
  ifelse(x %in% shared_fields,
         sub("^Group 0 (.)", "Control group \\L\\1", sub("^Group 1 (.)", "Case group \\L\\1", x, perl = TRUE), perl = TRUE),
         sub("^Group 0 ", "Health ", sub("^Group 1 ", "Periodontitis ", x)))
}

fields_db <- bind_rows(
  field_share(dat, "PerioSigDB", all_fields),
  field_share(bsdb_other, "BugSigDB", all_fields)
) |>
  mutate(
    # classification "not specified" counts as missing
    share = ifelse(db == "PerioSigDB" & field == "Periodontitis classification",
                   mean(dat$`Periodontitis classification` != "Periodontitis (type not specified)"), share),
    field_type = case_when(
      field %in% shared_fields ~ "Both databases",
      field %in% bsdb_fields ~ "BugSigDB fields",
      .default = "PerioSigDB only"
    ),
    field = factor(field_label(field), levels = rev(field_label(all_fields))),
    db = factor(db, levels = db_levels)
  )

ggplot(fields_db, aes(x = db, y = field)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = share, fill = db), shape = 21, color = "white", na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(is.na(share), "–", scales::percent(share, 1))),
            nudge_x = 0.22, hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "grey30") +
  facet_grid(field_type ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 7, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_db, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.4, 0.7))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each point:** share of signatures (PerioSigDB 187; BugSigDB 8,114, periodontitis excluded) with the field filled; area ∝ share, % printed beside it. "–" = column absent from that database.
- **Filled:** not NA, not "" and not the text "NA"; list fields filled if non-empty. "ND" counts as filled. PerioSigDB classification counts as missing when "type not specified" (79.1% filled).
- **Unit:** signatures, so PerioSigDB studies with two signatures count twice (shares differ slightly from the study-level completeness heatmap, e.g. age 88.8% here vs 87% both groups there).
- **Rows:** "Both databases" fields use BugSigDB names (Group 1 → case group, Group 0 → control group). "PerioSigDB only" clinical fields are Group 1 (periodontitis) values only; Group 0 definition shows as "Health definition".
- **16S variable region:** denominator is 16S signatures only (`Sequencing type` 16S or 16S,PCR): 68 in PerioSigDB (44.1% filled), 6,715 in BugSigDB (92.7%).
- **Plaque here:** any non-missing `Group 1 plaque` (indices included), unlike the heatmap, which counts % sites only.
- **Example:** sequencing type is filled for 66.3% of PerioSigDB vs 99.1% of BugSigDB signatures; the 45 hybridization signatures account for most of the PerioSigDB gap. `Shannon` (PerioSigDB 26.2%, BugSigDB 61.7%) counts "unchanged" entries as filled.
- **PerioSigDB statistical fields:** from the full-text review, not the curators (see "Data version" above); `Antibiotics exclusion` was not extracted.
- **No test.**
:::

**Shows:** PerioSigDB adds participant and clinical characteristics for which BugSigDB does not currently include dedicated fields. With the fields added by the full-text review, PerioSigDB now also records the statistical test (98% of signatures), significance threshold (93%) and multiple-testing correction (96%) about as often as BugSigDB; matching, confounders and diversity are reported less often than in BugSigDB, partly because many PerioSigDB studies used targeted assays without diversity measures. A full import would still need curator confirmation of these fields and validation against BugSigDB's schema and vocabularies.

**Caveats:**

- A filled field is not necessarily a complete one (e.g. "Matched on" can list only some of the variables).
- PerioSigDB's lower sequencing type completeness is mostly checkerboard hybridization, which has no sequencing type in BugSigDB's vocabulary.

## PerioSigDB taxa across other conditions

```{r bsdb-conditions-data}
# genera with the most consistent direction in PerioSigDB: exact binomial test of increased vs
# decreased signatures against 50% (as for taxa in the main report), then how often the top 20
# in each direction appear in BugSigDB signatures of the same direction for each other condition
n_sig_dir <- table(dat$`Abundance in Group 1`)

perio_tests <- sig_genera(dat) |>
  count(taxon, direction) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    signatures = increased + decreased,
    p = map2_dbl(increased, signatures, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
    fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
    direction = case_when(increased > decreased ~ "increased", decreased > increased ~ "decreased")
  )

perio_genera <- perio_tests |>
  filter(!is.na(direction)) |>
  arrange(p, desc(signatures)) |>
  slice_head(n = 20, by = direction) |>
  mutate(
    significance = case_when(
      fdr < 0.05 ~ "FDR < 0.05",
      p < 0.05 ~ "p < 0.05 (not FDR)",
      .default = "Not significant"
    ) |>
      factor(levels = c("FDR < 0.05", "p < 0.05 (not FDR)", "Not significant"))
  )

# participants (both groups) of the PerioSigDB studies reporting each genus in its periodontitis
# direction, each study counted once
perio_participants <- sig_genera(dat) |>
  mutate(Study = dat$Study[sig]) |>
  distinct(Study, taxon, direction) |>
  left_join(transmute(studies, Study, n = `Group 0 sample size` + `Group 1 sample size`), by = "Study") |>
  summarise(participants = sum(n, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(taxon, direction))
perio_genera <- left_join(perio_genera, perio_participants, by = c("taxon", "direction"))

# body site group of each signature (signatures listing sites in several groups are "mixed")
site_group <- function(sites) {
  map_chr(strsplit(sites, ","), function(x) {
    groups <- unique(site_of(x))
    if (length(groups) == 1) groups else "mixed"
  })
}

# disease (or exposure) vs control comparisons only: Group 0 is a control group and Group 1 is not.
# This drops body site, time point, treatment arm, diet and reversed comparisons, which BugSigDB
# also files under the study's condition
control_names <- paste0("control|healthy|\\bhealth\\b|normal|\\bnon[- ]?|without|negative|unaffected|",
                        "\\bHC\\b|\\bNC\\b|cognitively (intact|unimpaired)|^no\\b|-free\\b|peritumo|adjacent|benign")
# BugSigDB condition labels that name the same condition (different ontology terms), merged
condition_synonyms <- c(
  "Colorectal carcinoma" = "Colorectal cancer", "Colorectal adenocarcinoma" = "Colorectal cancer",
  "Colon carcinoma" = "Colorectal cancer",
  "Major depressive disorder" = "Unipolar depression",
  "Human immunodeficiency virus" = "HIV infection",
  "Eczema" = "Atopic eczema",
  "Autism" = "Autism spectrum disorder",
  "Breast carcinoma" = "Breast cancer",
  "Esophageal carcinoma" = "Esophageal cancer",
  "Human papillomavirus" = "Human papilloma virus infection",
  "Gastric adenocarcinoma" = "Gastric cancer",
  "Prostate carcinoma" = "Prostate cancer",
  "Psoriasis vulgaris" = "Psoriasis",
  "Autoimmune type 1 diabetes" = "Type I diabetes mellitus",
  "SARS-CoV-2-related disease" = "COVID-19",
  "Constipation" = "Chronic constipation",
  # all oral, pharyngeal or laryngeal cancers
  "Squamous cell carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer", "Oral squamous cell carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer",
  "Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer", "Oral cavity carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer",
  "Head and neck carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer"
)

# human disease-vs-control comparisons only (PerioSigDB is human), excluding meta-analyses, which
# re-analyse cohorts that are also in BugSigDB as primary studies
bsdb_cc <- bsdb_other |>
  filter(`Host species` == "Homo sapiens",
         !grepl("meta-analysis", `Study design`),
         grepl(control_names, `Group 0 name`, ignore.case = TRUE),
         !grepl(control_names, `Group 1 name`, ignore.case = TRUE),
         `Abundance in Group 1` %in% c("increased", "decreased")) |>
  mutate(Condition = coalesce(condition_synonyms[Condition], Condition))

# count each study once per condition, direction and body site group: the units below are
# study-level, and a genus is in a unit if it is in any of the study's signatures in that unit
bsdb_cc_sigs <- tibble(
  sig = seq_len(nrow(bsdb_cc)), bsdb_id = bsdb_cc$`BSDB ID`, Study = bsdb_cc$Study,
  Condition = bsdb_cc$Condition, direction = bsdb_cc$`Abundance in Group 1`,
  oral = is_oral(bsdb_cc$`Body site`),
  site_group = site_group(bsdb_cc$`Body site`)
) |>
  mutate(unit = as.integer(factor(paste(Study, Condition, direction, site_group, sep = "|"))))

bsdb_sigs <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  summarise(oral = any(oral), .by = c(unit, Study, Condition, direction, site_group)) |>
  rename(sig = unit)

bsdb_genera <- sig_genera(bsdb_cc) |>
  left_join(select(bsdb_cc_sigs, sig, unit), by = "sig") |>
  distinct(sig = unit, direction, taxon)

# direction of the periodontitis genera in each condition (genera reported by >= 3 of its studies)
genus_agreement_by <- function(by = "Condition") bsdb_genera |>
  filter(taxon %in% perio_genera$taxon) |>
  distinct(sig, taxon, direction) |>
  left_join(select(bsdb_sigs, sig, all_of(by)), by = "sig") |>
  count(across(all_of(c(by, "taxon", "direction")))) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  left_join(select(perio_genera, taxon, perio = direction), by = "taxon") |>
  mutate(n = increased + decreased, same = ifelse(perio == "increased", increased, decreased)) |>
  filter(n >= 3)
genus_agreement <- genus_agreement_by()

# a genus agrees with periodontitis in a condition if at least two thirds of the condition's reports of it
# are in the periodontitis direction, and goes the opposite way if at most one third are; in between
# (e.g. 2 of 4) it counts as neither, i.e. against both directions
agree_cut <- 2 / 3

agreement_summary <- function(ga, by = "Condition") ga |>
  # each genus counts once
  summarise(genera = n(), agree = sum(same / n >= agree_cut), against = sum(same / n <= 1 - agree_cut),
            share = mean(same / n), .by = all_of(c(by, "perio"))) |>
  filter(genera >= 3) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = perio, values_from = c(genera, agree, against, share)) |>
  filter(!is.na(share_increased), !is.na(share_decreased)) |>
  mutate(genera = genera_increased + genera_decreased, agree = agree_increased + agree_decreased,
         # share of each genus group's genera with a clear direction (mixed genera left out) that agree
         informative_increased = agree_increased + against_increased,
         informative_decreased = agree_decreased + against_decreased,
         frac_increased = ifelse(informative_increased > 0, agree_increased / informative_increased, 0.5),
         frac_decreased = ifelse(informative_decreased > 0, agree_decreased / informative_decreased, 0.5),
         label = Condition,
         informative = informative_increased + informative_decreased,
         p = map2_dbl(agree, informative, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n)$p.value))
agreement_map <- agreement_summary(genus_agreement)
# the same within each body site group of a condition (for the body site arrows of the agreement map)
agreement_map_site <- agreement_summary(genus_agreement_by(c("Condition", "site_group")), c("Condition", "site_group"))


# left panel: PerioSigDB signatures with the genus increased (right) and decreased (left), and
# participants in the studies reporting it in its periodontitis direction (circles)
perio_panel <- function(top, genus_levels, details = TRUE, labels_right = FALSE) {
  perio_counts <- top |>
    select(taxon, increased, decreased, significance) |>
    pivot_longer(c(increased, decreased), names_to = "sig_direction", values_to = "n") |>
    mutate(n = ifelse(sig_direction == "decreased", -n, n))

  max_n <- max(abs(perio_counts$n))
  p <- ggplot(perio_counts, aes(x = n, y = factor(taxon, levels = genus_levels))) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = sig_direction, alpha = significance), width = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3)
  # without details (combined figure): no FDR values or participant circles, genus names on either side
  if (!details) {
    return(p +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6"),
                        labels = c(increased = "Increased", decreased = "Decreased"),
                        name = "PerioSigDB\nsignatures") +
      scale_alpha_manual(values = c("FDR < 0.05" = 1, "p < 0.05 (not FDR)" = 0.6, "Not significant" = 0.25),
                         labels = c("FDR < 0.05" = "FDR < 0.05", "p < 0.05 (not FDR)" = "p < 0.05",
                                    "Not significant" = "Not significant"),
                         drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
      scale_x_continuous(labels = abs, breaks = pretty(c(-max_n, max_n), 3)) +
      scale_y_discrete(position = if (labels_right) "right" else "left") +
      labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
      guides(fill = "none", alpha = "none") +
```
