```{r bsdb-conditions-data}
      theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic")))
  }
  p +
    geom_text(data = distinct(top, taxon, fdr),
              aes(x = -max_n * 1.05, label = ifelse(fdr < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", fdr))),
              hjust = 1, size = 2.5, color = "grey30") +
    geom_point(data = distinct(top, taxon, participants), aes(x = max_n * 1.35, size = participants),
               shape = 21, fill = "grey65", color = "grey20", stroke = 0.3) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 6.5, limits = c(0, max(perio_genera$participants)), breaks = c(500, 2000, 5000),
                    name = "Participants") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6"),
                      labels = c(increased = "Increased", decreased = "Decreased"), name = NULL) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c("FDR < 0.05" = 1, "p < 0.05 (not FDR)" = 0.6, "Not significant" = 0.25),
                       drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = abs, breaks = scales::breaks_extended()(c(-max_n, max_n)),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0.35, 0.25))) +
    labs(x = "PerioSigDB signatures\n(left: FDR; circles: participants)", y = NULL) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1, ncol = 1), alpha = guide_legend(order = 2, ncol = 1),
           size = guide_legend(order = 3, ncol = 1)) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"),
          legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical", legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"))
}

# top bar: share of each column's signatures from oral body sites
oral_panel <- function(columns, axis_right = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(columns, aes(x = col, y = oral)) +
    geom_col(fill = "grey60", width = 0.7) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, breaks = c(0, 1), limits = c(0, 1),
                       position = if (axis_right) "right" else "left") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Oral sites") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
  # columns split into blocks (direction heatmaps): one panel per block, as in the heatmap
  if ("block" %in% names(columns)) {
    p <- p + facet_grid(. ~ block, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
      theme(strip.text = element_blank(), strip.background = element_blank(),
            panel.spacing.x = unit(0.3, "cm"))
  }
  p
}

# one-sided test of a genus being in a condition's signatures more often than in other conditions'
# signatures from the same body site group; strata without both are uninformative and dropped
site_matched_p <- function(condition, genus, sigs, hits) {
  d <- sigs |>
    mutate(in_condition = Condition == condition, has_genus = sig %in% hits$sig[hits$taxon == genus])
  informative <- d |>
    summarise(ok = any(in_condition) & any(!in_condition), .by = site_group) |>
    filter(ok) |>
    pull(site_group)
  if (!length(informative)) return(NA_real_)
  d <- filter(d, site_group %in% informative)
  tab <- table(factor(d$in_condition, c(TRUE, FALSE)), factor(d$has_genus, c(TRUE, FALSE)),
               factor(d$site_group))
  if (dim(tab)[3] == 1) {
    fisher.test(tab[, , 1], alternative = "greater")$p.value
  } else {
    mantelhaen.test(tab, exact = TRUE, alternative = "greater")$p.value
  }
}

# observed and expected share of a condition's signatures with each genus, where expected is the
# share in other conditions' signatures from the same body site group, weighted by the condition's
# own site mix; only site groups with signatures from both are used (as in site_matched_p)
site_expected <- function(sigs, hits) {
  by_group <- count(sigs, Condition, site_group, name = "n")
  hits_by_group <- hits |>
    left_join(select(sigs, sig, Condition, site_group), by = "sig") |>
    count(Condition, site_group, taxon, name = "h")
  totals <- count(sigs, site_group, name = "N")
  hit_totals <- count(hits_by_group, site_group, taxon, wt = h, name = "H")

  tidyr::expand_grid(by_group, taxon = unique(hits$taxon)) |>
    left_join(hits_by_group, by = c("Condition", "site_group", "taxon")) |>
    left_join(totals, by = "site_group") |>
    left_join(hit_totals, by = c("site_group", "taxon")) |>
    mutate(h = coalesce(h, 0L), H = coalesce(H, 0L)) |>
    filter(N > n) |>
    summarise(observed = sum(h) / sum(n), expected = sum(n * (H - h) / (N - n)) / sum(n),
              .by = c(Condition, taxon))
}

# match_site = TRUE compares each condition with other signatures from the same body site group
# (exact Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by site group) instead of all other signatures
# enrichment of each genus in each condition's signatures, vs all other BugSigDB signatures of this
# direction (one-sided Fisher's exact test) or vs other signatures from the same body site group
# (match_site), BH-adjusted across all genus x condition tests; cached as it is used twice
enrichment_cache <- new.env()
enrichment_table <- function(dir, min_sigs = 5, match_site = FALSE) {
  key <- paste(dir, min_sigs, match_site)
  if (!is.null(enrichment_cache[[key]])) return(enrichment_cache[[key]])
  top <- filter(perio_genera, direction == dir)
  sigs <- filter(bsdb_sigs, direction == dir)
  hits <- bsdb_genera |>
    filter(direction == dir, taxon %in% top$taxon) |>
    distinct(sig, taxon)
  condition_sizes <- sigs |>
    summarise(signatures = n(), oral = mean(oral), .by = Condition) |>
    filter(signatures >= min_sigs)
  genus_totals <- count(hits, taxon, name = "with_genus")
  enrichment_cache[[key]] <- hits |>
    left_join(select(sigs, sig, Condition), by = "sig") |>
    count(Condition, taxon, name = "n") |>
    right_join(tidyr::expand_grid(Condition = condition_sizes$Condition, taxon = top$taxon),
               by = c("Condition", "taxon")) |>
    left_join(condition_sizes, by = "Condition") |>
    left_join(genus_totals, by = "taxon") |>
    mutate(
      n = coalesce(n, 0L), with_genus = coalesce(with_genus, 0L),
      share = n / signatures,
      p = if (match_site) {
        map2_dbl(Condition, taxon, site_matched_p, sigs = sigs, hits = hits)
      } else {
        pmap_dbl(list(n, signatures, with_genus), function(a, n_cond, n_genus) {
          fisher.test(matrix(c(a, n_cond - a, n_genus - a, nrow(sigs) - n_cond - n_genus + a), 2),
                      alternative = "greater")$p.value
        })
      },
      fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
    )
  enrichment_cache[[key]]
}

condition_heatmap <- function(dir, min_sigs = 5, match_site = FALSE) {
  top <- filter(perio_genera, direction == dir)
  sigs <- filter(bsdb_sigs, direction == dir)
  hits <- bsdb_genera |>
    filter(direction == dir, taxon %in% top$taxon) |>
    distinct(sig, taxon)
  genus_totals <- count(hits, taxon, name = "with_genus")
  enrichment <- enrichment_table(dir, min_sigs, match_site)

  # conditions of the shared set, ordered by most significantly enriched genera (ties: combined p-value)
  conditions <- enrichment |>
    filter(Condition %in% figure_conditions(enrichment)) |>
    summarise(n_enriched = sum(fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), score = sum(-log10(p), na.rm = TRUE),
              .by = c(Condition, signatures, oral)) |>
    arrange(desc(n_enriched), desc(score))

  # first column: all BugSigDB signatures of this direction (baseline)
  columns <- bind_rows(
    tibble(Condition = "All BugSigDB", signatures = nrow(sigs), oral = mean(sigs$oral)),
    select(conditions, Condition, signatures, oral)
  ) |>
    mutate(col = paste0(Condition, " (", signatures, ")"), col = factor(col, levels = col))

  baseline <- tibble(taxon = top$taxon) |>
    left_join(genus_totals, by = "taxon") |>
    transmute(Condition = "All BugSigDB", taxon, share = coalesce(with_genus, 0L) / nrow(sigs), fdr = NA_real_)

  genus_levels <- rev(top$taxon)
  high <- if (dir == "increased") "#c2410c" else "#1c5cab"

  if (match_site) {
    # site-matched: colour and label are observed / expected (no unmatched baseline column)
    columns <- filter(columns, Condition != "All BugSigDB") |> mutate(col = droplevels(col))
    shares <- filter(enrichment, Condition %in% conditions$Condition) |>
      select(Condition, taxon, n, fdr) |>
      left_join(site_expected(sigs, hits), by = c("Condition", "taxon")) |>
      left_join(select(columns, Condition, col), by = "Condition") |>
      mutate(
        enriched = !is.na(fdr) & fdr < 0.05,
        # ratios from a single study are unstable, so only cells with at least 2 studies are shaded
        ratio = ifelse(coalesce(expected, 0) > 0 & n >= 2, observed / expected, NA),
        value = ifelse(is.na(ratio), 0, log2(pmax(ratio, 1))),
        label = ifelse(!is.na(ratio) & (enriched | ratio >= 2),
                       ifelse(ratio < 10, sprintf("%.1f", ratio), sprintf("%.0f", ratio)), "")
      )
    fill_scale <- scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f0efec", high = high, limits = c(0, 4), oob = scales::squish,
                                      breaks = 0:4, labels = paste0("×", 2^(0:4)), na.value = "white",
                                      name = "Observed /\nexpected")
    dark <- quote(value > 2.5)
  } else {
    shares <- bind_rows(baseline, filter(enrichment, Condition %in% conditions$Condition)) |>
      select(Condition, taxon, share, fdr) |>
      left_join(select(columns, Condition, col), by = "Condition") |>
      mutate(enriched = !is.na(fdr) & fdr < 0.05, value = share,
             label = ifelse(enriched | share >= 0.1, round(100 * share), ""))
    fill_scale <- scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f0efec", high = high, labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, NA),
                                      name = "BugSigDB\nstudies")
    dark <- quote(value > 0.45)
  }

  p_heat <- ggplot(shares, aes(x = col, y = factor(taxon, levels = genus_levels), fill = value)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(shares, enriched), color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.7, width = 0.9, height = 0.85) +
    (if (!match_site) geom_vline(xintercept = 1.5, color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.6)) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label, color = !!dark, fontface = ifelse(enriched, "bold", "plain")), size = 2.7) +
    fill_scale +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey20", `TRUE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
          plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey30", hjust = 0))

  (plot_spacer() + oral_panel(columns) + perio_panel(top, genus_levels) + p_heat) +
    plot_layout(ncol = 2, widths = c(1.8, 6), heights = c(1, 7))
}

# direction of each genus within each BugSigDB condition: exact binomial test of signatures
# reporting it increased vs decreased against 50% (the same test as for PerioSigDB),
# BH-adjusted across all genus x condition tests
# direction of each genus within each BugSigDB condition: exact binomial test of signatures
# reporting it in the same vs the opposite direction as periodontitis
count_directions <- function(d, ...) {
  d |>
    count(..., taxon, direction) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
    (\(x) mutate(x, increased = if ("increased" %in% names(x)) increased else 0L,
                  decreased = if ("decreased" %in% names(x)) decreased else 0L))()
}
direction_test <- function(d, dir) {
  d |>
    mutate(
      n = increased + decreased,
      same = if (dir == "increased") increased else decreased,
      share_same = same / n,
      p = map2_dbl(same, n, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
      fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
    )
}
# body site subsets shown as extra columns of the direction heatmap: conditions whose position in the
# direction summary changes most when restricted to one body site group
site_subsets <- tribble(
  ~Condition,             ~site_group,        ~subset,
  "COVID-19",             "gastrointestinal", "COVID-19 (gut)",
  "Rheumatoid arthritis", "oral",             "Rheumatoid arthritis (mouth)"
)
# BugSigDB study units, with the units of each body site subset added again under the subset's name
sigs_with_subsets <- function() {
  bind_rows(bsdb_sigs,
            inner_join(bsdb_sigs, site_subsets, by = c("Condition", "site_group")) |>
              mutate(Condition = subset) |> select(-subset))
}
direction_hits <- function(dir, subsets = FALSE) {
  bsdb_genera |>
    filter(taxon %in% perio_genera$taxon[perio_genera$direction == dir]) |>
    distinct(sig, taxon) |>
    left_join(select(if (subsets) sigs_with_subsets() else bsdb_sigs, sig, Condition, direction), by = "sig",
              relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    filter(direction %in% c("increased", "decreased"))
}
direction_tests <- function(dir, min_sigs = 5) {
  sizes <- sigs_with_subsets() |> count(Condition, name = "signatures") |> filter(signatures >= min_sigs)
  tests <- direction_hits(dir, subsets = TRUE) |>
    filter(Condition %in% sizes$Condition) |>
    count_directions(Condition) |>
    direction_test(dir)
  # FDR of the conditions as before (body site subsets not part of their family); the subsets'
  # FDR adjusted together with all conditions
  is_subset <- tests$Condition %in% site_subsets$subset
  tests$fdr[!is_subset] <- p.adjust(tests$p[!is_subset], method = "BH")
  tests
}

# per condition and genus group: genera reported by at least min_reports of the condition's studies
# (agreement counts), how many agree with periodontitis (at least agree_cut of their reports in the
# periodontitis direction) and how many go the opposite way (at most 1 - agree_cut); genera in between
# (mixed) have no clear direction and are left out, as in a sign test; informative = agree + against
direction_agreement <- function(dir, min_sigs = 5, min_reports = 3) {
  direction_tests(dir, min_sigs) |>
    filter(n >= min_reports) |>
    summarise(genera = n(), agree = sum(same / n >= agree_cut), against = sum(same / n <= 1 - agree_cut),
              .by = Condition) |>
    mutate(informative = agree + against, mixed = genera - informative) |>
    filter(informative > 0) |>
    mutate(p = map2_dbl(agree, informative, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n)$p.value), direction = dir)
}

# one genus group of the direction heatmap, for the given columns
# legend key for mixed cells: a black-outlined box with the cells' diagonal hatching
draw_key_hatch <- function(data, params, size) {
  offsets <- c(-0.5, -0.25, 0, 0.25, 0.5)
  x0 <- pmax(0, offsets); x1 <- pmin(1, 1 + offsets)
  grid::grobTree(
    grid::segmentsGrob(x0 = x0, y0 = x0 - offsets, x1 = x1, y1 = x1 - offsets,
                       gp = grid::gpar(col = "grey45", lwd = 0.8)),
    grid::rectGrob(gp = grid::gpar(col = "black", fill = NA, lwd = 1))
  )
}

direction_heat_panel <- function(dir, columns, min_sigs = 5, show_x = TRUE, neutral = FALSE) {
  top <- filter(perio_genera, direction == dir)
  tests <- direction_tests(dir, min_sigs)
  baseline <- direction_hits(dir) |>
    count_directions() |>
    direction_test(dir) |>
    mutate(Condition = "All BugSigDB")

  cells <- bind_rows(baseline, filter(tests, Condition %in% columns$Condition)) |>
    right_join(tidyr::expand_grid(Condition = columns$Condition, taxon = top$taxon),
               by = c("Condition", "taxon")) |>
    left_join(select(columns, Condition, col, block), by = "Condition") |>
    mutate(
      significant = !is.na(fdr) & fdr < 0.05,
      # too few signatures to show a direction
      few = !is.na(n) & n < 3,
      # colour: share reported in the genus group's periodontitis direction (increased: orange, decreased: blue)
      # neutral (combined figure): share reported increased for both genus groups, one key
      share_plot = ifelse(few, NA, if (neutral && dir == "decreased") 1 - share_same else share_same),
      label = ifelse(!is.na(n) & !few, paste0(same, "/", n), ""),
      # mixed: neither direction reaches agree_cut, so the genus is left out of the condition's count
      mixed = Condition != "All BugSigDB" & !is.na(n) & n >= 3 & same / n < agree_cut & same / n > 1 - agree_cut
    )

  # hatching for mixed cells: diagonal lines in numeric panel positions (columns are numbered within
  # each panel, rows from the bottom)
  hatch_offsets <- tibble(c = c(-0.6, -0.3, 0, 0.3, 0.6))
  hatch <- cells |>
    mutate(xi = dense_rank(as.integer(col)), .by = block) |>
    mutate(yi = match(taxon, rev(top$taxon))) |>
    filter(mixed) |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(hatch_offsets) |>
    mutate(h = 0.45,
           x0 = pmax(-h, -h + c), y0 = x0 - c, x1 = pmin(h, h + c), y1 = x1 - c,
           x = xi + x0, y = yi + y0, xend = xi + x1, yend = yi + y1)

  # line next to All BugSigDB (after it, or before it when the columns are mirrored)
  all_pos <- columns |>
    mutate(pos = dense_rank(as.integer(col)), n_block = n(), .by = block) |>
    filter(Condition == "All BugSigDB") |>
    mutate(xintercept = ifelse(pos == 1, 1.5, pos - 0.5))
  fill_scale <- if (neutral) {
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#1c5cab", mid = "#f0efec", high = "#c2410c", midpoint = 0.5, limits = c(0, 1),
                         breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), labels = c("All decreased", "Half", "All increased"),
                         na.value = "white", name = "Studies reporting\nthe genus")
  } else {
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = if (dir == "increased") "#1c5cab" else "#c2410c", mid = "#f0efec",
                         high = if (dir == "increased") "#c2410c" else "#1c5cab", midpoint = 0.5,
                         limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent, na.value = "white",
                         name = paste0("Share of studies\nreporting it ", dir))
  }

  ggplot(cells, aes(x = col, y = factor(taxon, levels = rev(top$taxon)), fill = share_plot)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(cells, few), fill = "grey85", color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(cells, significant), color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.7, width = 0.9, height = 0.85) +
    geom_segment(data = hatch, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend, linetype = "Mixed (left out)"),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey55", linewidth = 0.3, key_glyph = draw_key_hatch) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = "solid", name = NULL) +
    geom_vline(data = select(all_pos, block, xintercept), aes(xintercept = xintercept),
               color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.6) +
    # conditions going the opposite way in a separate panel
    facet_grid(. ~ block, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    geom_text(aes(label = label, fontface = ifelse(significant, "bold", "plain")), size = 2.4, color = "grey15") +
    fill_scale +
    guides(fill = guide_colourbar(order = 1), linetype = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = if (show_x) element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1) else element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.x = if (show_x) element_line() else element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_blank(), strip.background = element_blank(),
          panel.spacing.x = unit(0.3, "cm"),
          legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9))
}

# conditions shown in a direction heatmap: at least min_genera genera with a clear direction, of which
# at least min_agree agree with periodontitis or at least min_agree go the opposite way
direction_conditions <- function(dir, min_sigs = 5, min_reports = 3, min_genera = 4, min_agree = agree_cut) {
  direction_agreement(dir, min_sigs, min_reports) |>
    filter(informative >= min_genera, agree / informative >= min_agree | against / informative >= min_agree) |>
    mutate(agreeing = agree / informative >= min_agree, k = ifelse(agreeing, agree, against))
}

# one genus group per figure: unlike the other figures (shared core set), each shows the tested
# conditions with at least min_genera genera reported by at least min_reports studies of which at least
# min_agree have more than half of their reports in the periodontitis direction (agreeing, first) or at
# least min_agree in the opposite direction (opposite, after a dashed line), each block ordered by the
# sign test (two-sided against half, as in the next figure), smallest p first. Cells keep the width of
# a figure with n_ref columns, so the heatmap is narrower rather than stretched.
direction_heatmap <- function(dir, min_sigs = 5, min_reports = 3, min_genera = 4, min_agree = agree_cut, n_ref = 13,
                              columns_only = FALSE) {
  condition_sizes <- sigs_with_subsets() |>
    summarise(signatures = n(), oral = mean(oral), .by = Condition)
  shown <- direction_conditions(dir, min_sigs, min_reports, min_genera, min_agree)
  # body site subsets are always shown, in the panel of the direction most of their genera take
  forced <- direction_agreement(dir, min_sigs, min_reports) |>
    filter(Condition %in% site_subsets$subset, !Condition %in% shown$Condition) |>
    mutate(agreeing = agree >= against, k = ifelse(agreeing, agree, against))
  conditions <- bind_rows(shown, forced) |>
    arrange(desc(agreeing), p, desc(k / informative)) |>
    left_join(condition_sizes, by = "Condition")
  columns <- bind_rows(
    tibble(Condition = "All BugSigDB", signatures = nrow(bsdb_sigs), oral = mean(bsdb_sigs$oral)),
    select(conditions, Condition, signatures, oral, agree, against, informative, mixed, agreeing)
  ) |>
    # label: genera agreeing (left panel) or going the opposite way (right panel) / genera with a clear
    # direction (mixed genera are hatched in the cells)
    mutate(col = ifelse(is.na(informative), "All BugSigDB",
                        paste0(Condition, " (", ifelse(agreeing, agree, against), "/", informative, ")")),
           col = factor(col, levels = col),
           # All BugSigDB and agreeing conditions in one panel, opposite conditions in another
           block = factor(ifelse(agreeing %in% FALSE, "opposite", "same"), levels = c("same", "opposite")),
           block = droplevels(block))

  if (columns_only) return(columns)
  top <- filter(perio_genera, direction == dir)
  k <- min(nrow(columns) / n_ref, 1)
  (plot_spacer() + oral_panel(columns) + plot_spacer() +
     perio_panel(top, rev(top$taxon)) + direction_heat_panel(dir, columns, min_sigs) + plot_spacer()) +
    plot_layout(ncol = 3, widths = c(1.8, 6 * k, max(6 * (1 - k), 0.01)), heights = c(1, 7))
}

# both genus groups in one figure: periodontitis-increased genera and their heatmap on the left,
# periodontitis-decreased on the right, each with the genus names and PerioSigDB bars on its left,
# separated by a vertical line; one colour key (share reported increased) for both
direction_heatmap_combined <- function(min_sigs = 5) {
  cols_inc <- direction_heatmap("increased", columns_only = TRUE)
  cols_dec <- direction_heatmap("decreased", columns_only = TRUE)
  top_inc <- filter(perio_genera, direction == "increased")
  top_dec <- filter(perio_genera, direction == "decreased")
  separator <- ggplot() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
    theme_void()
  # title over each half, left-aligned with the genus names (full area, including the axis-label space)
  title <- function(text) {
    wrap_elements(full = grid::textGrob(text, x = 0, hjust = 0,
                                        gp = grid::gpar(fontface = "bold", fontsize = 10.5)))
  }
  no_y <- theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), axis.title.y = element_blank())
  wrap_plots(
    A = title("Periodontitis-increased genera"), B = title("Periodontitis-decreased genera"),
    C = oral_panel(cols_inc), D = oral_panel(cols_dec) + no_y,
    E = perio_panel(top_inc, rev(top_inc$taxon), details = FALSE),
    F = direction_heat_panel("increased", cols_inc, min_sigs, neutral = TRUE),
    S = separator,
    H = perio_panel(top_dec, rev(top_dec$taxon), details = FALSE),
    G = direction_heat_panel("decreased", cols_dec, min_sigs, neutral = TRUE),
    design = "AASBB\n#CS#D\nEFSHG"
  ) +
    plot_layout(widths = c(1.4, nrow(cols_inc) + 0.4, 0.4, 1.4, nrow(cols_dec) + 0.4),
                heights = c(0.25, 1, 7), guides = "collect") &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

# whole-signature similarity (see "Whole-signature similarity to periodontitis")
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.R (takes ~20 minutes)
semsim <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.rds")
# Lin similarity of each BugSigDB taxon to the consensus taxa, with taxon lineages
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_taxon_similarity.R
taxon_sim <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_taxon_similarity.rds")

# similarity of a set of BugSigDB study units to a PerioSigDB consensus, compared with the units of all *other*
# conditions (periodontitis studies are not in bsdb_cc): one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann-Whitney) test,
# more similar than the background. Shown rank of a unit: share of background units it is more similar than
# (ties count half), so a set's mean rank is U / (n_x * n_y) (0.5 = typical).
# scores: one row per unit and periodontitis consensus (perio), with unit, Condition, direction, site_group, sim.
# Sets, each needing >= min_units units of the BugSigDB direction:
#   all:      all of a condition's units, vs all other units of the direction
#   site_all: a condition's units from one body site group, vs all other units of the direction
#   site:     the same, vs other units of the direction from that site group; only where that site group has
#             >= min_bg_units such units from >= min_bg_conditions other conditions (a proper background)
# BH within each kind of set and each BugSigDB direction x consensus column.
similarity_tests <- function(scores, min_units = 5, min_bg_units = 20, min_bg_conditions = 10) {
  unit_info <- distinct(scores, unit, Condition, direction, site_group)
  sim <- pivot_wider(select(scores, unit, perio, sim), names_from = perio, values_from = sim)
  sim_of <- \(u, pr) sim[[pr]][match(u, sim$unit)]
  rank_vs <- \(x, y) vapply(x, \(v) mean(y < v) + 0.5 * mean(y == v), numeric(1))
  background <- \(cond, dir, kind, s) with(unit_info, unit[direction == dir & Condition != cond &
                                                             (kind != "site" | site_group == s)])
  sets <- bind_rows(mutate(unit_info, kind = "all", site = NA_character_),
                    mutate(unit_info, kind = "site_all", site = site_group),
                    mutate(unit_info, kind = "site", site = site_group)) |>
    filter(n() >= min_units, .by = c(kind, Condition, site, direction)) |>
    nest(units = c(unit, site_group), .by = c(kind, Condition, site, direction)) |>
    mutate(bg = pmap(list(Condition, direction, kind, site), background),
           bg_conditions = map_int(bg, \(b) n_distinct(unit_info$Condition[match(b, unit_info$unit)]))) |>
    filter(kind != "site" | (lengths(bg) >= min_bg_units & bg_conditions >= min_bg_conditions))
  res <- cross_join(sets, tibble(perio = c("increased", "decreased"))) |>
    mutate(x = map2(units, perio, \(u, pr) sim_of(u$unit, pr)),
           y = map2(bg, perio, sim_of),
           ranks = map2(x, y, rank_vs),
           studies = lengths(x), background = lengths(y),
           mean_rank = map_dbl(ranks, mean),
           ci = map_dbl(ranks, \(r) 1.96 * sd(r) / sqrt(length(r))),
           p = map2_dbl(x, y, \(x, y) wilcox.test(x, y, alternative = "greater", exact = FALSE)$p.value)) |>
    mutate(fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"), .by = c(kind, direction, perio))
  list(stats = select(res, kind, Condition, site, direction, perio, studies, background, bg_conditions,
                      mean_rank, ci, p, fdr),
       units = res |> mutate(units = map2(units, ranks, \(u, r) mutate(u, rank = r))) |>
         select(kind, Condition, site, direction, perio, units) |> unnest(units))
}

# mean best-match similarity of each study unit to the two consensus signatures, over its signatures with
# at least 5 taxa (as in the BugSigDB paper): smaller ones give extreme, noisy similarities
semsim_scores <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  filter(lengths(bsdb_cc$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`[sig]) >= 5) |>
  inner_join(semsim$similarity, by = c("bsdb_id" = "BSDB ID")) |>
  summarise(increased = mean(sim_increased), decreased = mean(sim_decreased),
            .by = c(unit, Condition, direction, site_group)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(increased, decreased), names_to = "perio", values_to = "sim")
semsim_tests <- similarity_tests(semsim_scores)

# conditions shown: those with enough data in both directions (at least 3 periodontitis genera
# reported by at least 3 studies in each) in every figure, plus, in each figure, any condition with
# p < 0.05 in that figure's own tests; each figure orders them by its own criterion
base_conditions <- agreement_map$Condition
figure_conditions <- function(tests) union(base_conditions, tests$Condition[!is.na(tests$p) & tests$p < 0.05])
```

In which other conditions does the microbiome literature (BugSigDB) report the taxa that PerioSigDB links to periodontitis? BugSigDB is restricted to human disease-vs-control comparisons, excluding meta-analyses (`r nrow(bsdb_cc)` signatures from `r n_distinct(bsdb_cc$Study)` studies), and each study counts once per condition, direction and body site group. Body site groups: oral (mouth, saliva, dental plaque, tongue, gums, inner cheek, lip), upper airway (throat, pharynx including the oropharynx, nose), lower airway, gastrointestinal, urogenital, skin, eye and other (e.g. blood, milk); signatures listing sites from several groups are mixed. Condition labels that name the same condition are merged (e.g. colorectal carcinoma into colorectal cancer; oral, pharyngeal and laryngeal cancers into head and neck cancer).

Which conditions can be compared at all depends on how many studies BugSigDB holds for each, and the clinically nearest conditions do not qualify: it has 2 gingivitis study units per direction and 1 each for peri-implantitis, dental caries and halitosis, against the 5 any test here requires. "The condition most like periodontitis" therefore means the most like it among conditions with enough studies, which are mostly gut conditions and cancers.

The enrichment heatmaps show the same `r length(base_conditions)` core conditions, those with at least 3 periodontitis genera reported by at least 3 studies in each direction, plus any other condition with unadjusted p < 0.05 in that figure's own tests. The direction heatmap instead shows, for each direction, the conditions whose reports agree most with periodontitis; the direction summary shows these conditions, and the whole-signature similarity figures show the conditions with unadjusted p < 0.05 in any of their own tests.

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to read the genus heatmaps

- **Rows:** the top 20 periodontitis-increased or -decreased genera (see the taxon set table above), most significant at top. Not all of them pass FDR in PerioSigDB.
- **Left panel:** PerioSigDB signatures reporting the genus decreased (bars to the left) or increased (bars to the right), with the FDR of a binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures against 50%. Bar shading: FDR < 0.05, unadjusted p < 0.05, or neither. Circles: total participants (periodontitis and comparison groups) in the PerioSigDB studies reporting the genus in its periodontitis direction, each study counted once; this shows how many participants support each genus, which the number of signatures does not.
- **Columns:** BugSigDB conditions; in brackets, the number of the condition's studies (study units) of the direction shown, i.e. studies with any signature of that direction, not only those reporting the displayed genera.
- **Top bar:** share of the condition's studies from oral sites.
- **Outlined cells with bold numbers:** FDR < 0.05 for the test named in each caption, adjusted across all genera and all conditions tested, including conditions not shown. The All BugSigDB column is not tested in the enrichment heatmaps; in the direction heatmap it is adjusted separately, across its 20 genera.
- **Empty cells:** not reported, or too few studies to show a value (each caption gives the minimum). A study reporting a genus in both directions (e.g. different species of it, or different comparisons) counts once in each direction.
:::

### Do the targeted panels create these genera?

Half of PerioSigDB comes from checkerboard DNA–DNA hybridization and PCR, which only measure the taxa on a fixed panel. Those panels were designed around the taxa already suspected in periodontitis, so they could manufacture the genus sets above. Here the same counts are split by assay.

```{r assay-genera}
#| fig-width: 12.5
#| fig-height: 8.8
#| fig-cap: "How much of the evidence for each genus comes from targeted assays, and whether they agree with sequencing. Rows: the 20 genera per direction of the heatmaps, in the same order. Left: PerioSigDB signatures reporting the genus, by profiling method. Right: the share of those reports that are in the genus's periodontitis direction, for sequencing signatures (16S and shotgun) and targeted signatures (PCR and checkerboard hybridization) separately; a point is drawn where that assay has at least 3 signatures reporting the genus, and point area is the number of signatures. Dashed line: half the reports, i.e. no direction. Signatures with no method recorded are in the left panel only."
assay_of <- \(m) case_when(m %in% c("16S rRNA sequencing", "Shotgun metagenomics") ~ "Sequencing",
                           m %in% c("PCR", "DNA-DNA hybridization") ~ "Targeted",
                           .default = "Other / not reported")
sig_assay <- tibble(sig = seq_len(nrow(dat)),
                    method = method_of(dat$`Sequencing type`, dat$`Sequencing platform`)) |>
  mutate(assay = assay_of(method))
genus_assay <- sig_genera(dat) |> left_join(sig_assay, by = "sig")

assay_levels <- rev(perio_genera$taxon)
dir_label <- c(increased = "Increased in periodontitis", decreased = "Decreased in periodontitis")

# left: signatures per genus, split by profiling method
evidence <- genus_assay |>
  filter(taxon %in% perio_genera$taxon) |>
  distinct(sig, taxon, method) |>
  count(taxon, method) |>
  left_join(select(perio_genera, taxon, direction), by = "taxon") |>
  mutate(taxon = factor(taxon, levels = assay_levels),
         direction = factor(dir_label[direction], levels = dir_label))

p_evidence <- ggplot(evidence, aes(n, taxon, fill = method)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_method, name = NULL) +
  facet_grid(direction ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "PerioSigDB signatures reporting the genus", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"), strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

# right: share of reports in the periodontitis direction, sequencing vs targeted
assay_direction <- genus_assay |>
  filter(taxon %in% perio_genera$taxon, assay != "Other / not reported") |>
  count_directions(assay) |>
  left_join(select(perio_genera, taxon, perio = direction), by = "taxon") |>
  mutate(n = increased + decreased, same = ifelse(perio == "increased", increased, decreased),
         share = ifelse(n >= 3, same / n, NA)) |>
  # every genus gets a row in both assays, so that the rows line up with the left panel
  right_join(tidyr::expand_grid(select(perio_genera, taxon, perio = direction),
                                assay = c("Sequencing", "Targeted")),
             by = c("taxon", "assay", "perio")) |>
  mutate(taxon = factor(taxon, levels = assay_levels),
         direction = factor(dir_label[perio], levels = dir_label))
p_assay <- ggplot(assay_direction, aes(share, taxon)) +
  # a genus with no point in either assay would otherwise be dropped from the axis and re-added at the
  # top, shifting the rows out of line with the left panel
  geom_blank(data = \(d) mutate(d, share = 0.5)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  # line joining the two assays of a genus, where both are shown (a geom_segment with y and yend on a
  # discrete axis retrains the scale and reorders the rows, so the panels would stop lining up)
  geom_line(data = \(d) filter(d, !is.na(share)), aes(group = taxon), orientation = "y",
            color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = assay, size = n), shape = 21, color = "grey20", stroke = 0.3, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Sequencing = "#2a78d6", Targeted = "#d55181"), name = NULL) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 5, breaks = c(5, 20, 40), name = "Signatures") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  facet_grid(direction ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Reports in the genus's periodontitis direction", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), strip.text = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1), size = guide_legend(order = 2))

p_evidence + p_assay + plot_layout(widths = c(1.25, 1)) & theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r assay-values}
# the top 20 per direction rebuilt from sequencing signatures only, to compare with the heatmap rows
seq_tests <- genus_assay |>
  filter(assay == "Sequencing") |>
  count_directions() |>
  mutate(signatures = increased + decreased,
         p = map2_dbl(increased, signatures, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
         fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
         direction = case_when(increased > decreased ~ "increased", decreased > increased ~ "decreased"))
seq_top <- seq_tests |>
  filter(!is.na(direction)) |>
  arrange(p, desc(signatures)) |>
  slice_head(n = 20, by = direction)
seq_shared <- \(dir) length(intersect(perio_genera$taxon[perio_genera$direction == dir],
                                      seq_top$taxon[seq_top$direction == dir]))
seq_only <- \(dir) setdiff(seq_top$taxon[seq_top$direction == dir], perio_genera$taxon)
panel_only <- \(dir) setdiff(perio_genera$taxon[perio_genera$direction == dir], seq_top$taxon)
# share of a genus's reports in its periodontitis direction, within one assay
ad <- \(g, a) with(filter(assay_direction, taxon == g, assay == a), sprintf("%d of %d", same, n))
# share of a genus's signatures from targeted assays
targeted_share <- genus_assay |>
  filter(taxon %in% perio_genera$taxon) |>
  distinct(sig, taxon, assay) |>
  count(taxon, assay) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n), .by = taxon) |>
  filter(assay == "Targeted")
ts <- \(g) scales::percent(targeted_share$share[targeted_share$taxon == g], 1)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Assay groups:** sequencing = 16S (62 signatures) and shotgun (17); targeted = PCR (45) and checkerboard DNA–DNA hybridization (45); 18 signatures have no method recorded and are left out of the right panel.
- **Left panel:** signatures, not studies, and a genus counts once per signature, so the bars match the left panel of the genus heatmaps.
- **Right panel:** of the signatures that report the genus at all, the share listing it in the direction the heatmaps assign to it. A genus with fewer than 3 signatures in an assay gets no point, which is why some rows show one point or none.
- **Sequencing-only check:** repeating the binomial test on sequencing signatures alone keeps `r seq_shared("increased")` of the 20 periodontitis-increased genera and `r seq_shared("decreased")` of the 20 decreased genera in the top 20. Dropped: `r paste0("*", panel_only("increased"), "*", collapse = ", ")` (increased) and `r paste0("*", panel_only("decreased"), "*", collapse = ", ")` (decreased). Added: `r paste0("*", seq_only("increased"), "*", collapse = ", ")` and `r paste0("*", seq_only("decreased"), "*", collapse = ", ")`.
- **Test:** none in the figure. The sequencing-only counts above use the same exact binomial test against 50%, BH-adjusted across all `r nrow(seq_tests)` genera that sequencing studies report; `r sum(seq_tests$fdr < 0.05)` pass FDR < 0.05, against `r sum(perio_tests$fdr < 0.05)` for all signatures.
- **Watch out:** the two assay groups are not independent samples of the same studies, because studies chose their method. Sequencing studies are also more recent: 16S or shotgun is the method of `r scales::percent(mean(assay_of(studies$method[studies$Year >= 2015]) == "Sequencing"), 1)` of studies published from 2015 on, against `r scales::percent(mean(assay_of(studies$method[studies$Year < 2015]) == "Sequencing"), 1)` before.
:::

**Shows:** the panels supply about half the evidence for the classic periodontal pathogens (*Tannerella* `r ts("Tannerella")` of its signatures from targeted assays, *Porphyromonas* `r ts("Porphyromonas")`, *Treponema* `r ts("Treponema")`, *Prevotella* `r ts("Prevotella")`) but they do not create them: sequencing studies alone put `r seq_shared("increased")` of the 20 increased and `r seq_shared("decreased")` of the 20 decreased genera back in the top 20, and the two assay types agree on direction for almost every genus. Two genera depend on the panels. *Aggregatibacter* is reported increased by `r ad("Aggregatibacter", "Targeted")` targeted signatures but only `r ad("Aggregatibacter", "Sequencing")` sequencing ones, and *Campylobacter* by `r ad("Campylobacter", "Targeted")` against `r ad("Campylobacter", "Sequencing")`; both are standard checkerboard targets, and both leave the top 20 when sequencing studies are used alone. The genera that only sequencing reports (*Anaeroglobus*, *Johnsonella*, *Metamycoplasma*, *Pseudoramibacter*, and *Oribacterium* and *Propionibacterium* among the decreased) carry the opposite bias: panels could not have found them.

**Caveat:** this compares assays, not the same studies measured two ways. No PerioSigDB study reports both, so a difference between the two columns can also reflect the populations, sites and years those studies covered.

### Periodontitis-associated genera reported more often in other conditions

*Is the genus reported more often in this condition than in others?*

```{r bsdb-conditions-increased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-increased genera and how often other conditions report them increased (BugSigDB). Columns: all of BugSigDB, then each condition, ordered by number of enriched genera (ties: sum of −log10 p). Cells: share of the condition's studies reporting the genus increased (numbers, in %, shown when at least 10% or enriched); empty: not reported. Outlined: one-sided Fisher's exact test of the share of the condition's studies with the genus vs the share of all other BugSigDB studies of this direction."
condition_heatmap("increased")
```

```{r bsdb-conditions-decreased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-decreased genera and how often other conditions report them decreased (BugSigDB). Columns: all of BugSigDB, then each condition, ordered by number of enriched genera (ties: sum of −log10 p). Cells: share of the condition's studies reporting the genus decreased (numbers, in %, shown when at least 10% or enriched); empty: not reported. Outlined: one-sided Fisher's exact test of the share of the condition's studies with the genus vs the share of all other BugSigDB studies of this direction."
condition_heatmap("decreased")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Question:** is the genus listed in this condition's signatures of the same direction more often than in the rest of BugSigDB? It tests how often the genus is reported, not its direction. A condition reporting it in the opposite direction is not counted here (see the direction figures).
- **PerioSigDB rows:** each PerioSigDB taxon is reduced to its MetaPhlAn `g__` genus; taxa above genus rank are dropped, and a genus counts once per signature. For each of the 172 genera, an exact binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures against 50% is run, BH-adjusted across all 172 (the FDR in the left panel). Genera with equal counts in both directions have no direction and are left out. The top 20 per direction are ranked by p, with ties broken by more signatures. Rows 15–20 (from *Anaeroglobus* down) of the increased set and rows 6–20 (from *Neisseria* down) of the decreased set have FDR ≥ 0.05.
- **Left panel:** bar lengths are PerioSigDB signatures, not studies (187 signatures from 119 studies; one study can contribute several). For example, *Porphyromonas* has 77 increased and 10 decreased, FDR 3e-12.
- **Participant circles:** total Group 0 + Group 1 size of each PerioSigDB study reporting the genus in its periodontitis direction, each study counted once. The circle area is proportional to this total, on one scale shared by all genus figures (largest: *Porphyromonas* increased, 7,467).
- **BugSigDB data:** non-periodontitis BugSigDB signatures from human studies, excluding meta-analyses and keeping only increased or decreased signatures. A signature is kept only if its Group 0 name matches a control pattern (control, healthy, normal, non-, without, negative, HC, adjacent, benign, …) and its Group 1 name does not. This keeps 3,208 of 6,355 signatures from 867 studies. Synonymous condition labels are merged (e.g. colorectal carcinoma, colorectal adenocarcinoma and colon carcinoma become colorectal cancer; oral, oral squamous cell and head and neck carcinomas become head and neck cancer).
- **Study unit:** one BugSigDB study × condition × direction × body site group, giving 1,892 units: 974 increased and 918 decreased. A genus is in a unit if any of the unit's signatures lists it at genus or species rank. Units whose signatures list no genus still count in the denominators.
- **Each cell:** the share of the condition's units of this direction that contain the genus. For example, *Fusobacterium* in colorectal cancer is 54% = 29 of 54 increased colorectal cancer units.
- **All BugSigDB column:** units of this direction from all conditions, including small ones and the condition itself; for example, *Fusobacterium* is in 125 of 974 (13%). This column is not tested.
- **Brackets and top bar:** the number of the condition's units of this direction. The top bar is the share of those units with any oral body site (e.g. colorectal cancer 9%, smoking 88%, increased).
- **Conditions tested:** the 40 conditions with ≥ 5 units of the direction. Shown are 12 core conditions plus any with unadjusted p < 0.05: 17 columns for increased (adds HPV infection, response to transplant, cervical glandular intraepithelial neoplasia, diarrhoea, multiple sclerosis) and 17 for decreased (adds dry eye syndrome, atopic eczema, chronic kidney disease, response to immunochemotherapy, chronic fatigue syndrome).
- **Test:** a one-sided Fisher's exact test on a 2×2 table: the condition's units with and without the genus vs all other units of this direction with and without it. The BH correction covers all 800 genus × condition tests per direction, including conditions not shown.
- **Example:** colorectal cancer × *Fusobacterium* is 29 of 54 (54%) vs 96 of 920 other increased units (10%), OR 9.9, p = 8e-14, FDR = 2e-11. Rheumatoid arthritis × *Treponema* is 5 of 13 vs 27 of 961 (3%), FDR = 0.005. Head and neck cancer × *Rothia* (decreased) is 7 of 15 vs 49 of 903 (5%), FDR = 0.004.
- **All FDR < 0.05 cells:** for increased, colorectal cancer × *Peptostreptococcus*, *Parvimonas*, *Fusobacterium* and *Porphyromonas*, plus rheumatoid arthritis × *Treponema*. For decreased, head and neck cancer × *Rothia* and *Actinomyces*, smoking × *Gemella*, *Capnocytophaga* and *Lautropia*, and COVID-19 × *Neisseria*.
- **Watch out:** there is no adjustment for body site (oral genera are enriched in any oral condition; see the next figure) or for signature length (long signatures include more genera by chance). Small conditions with 5–15 units give large shares from few studies.
:::

**Shows:** colorectal cancer studies disproportionately report increases in *Porphyromonas*, *Parvimonas*, *Peptostreptococcus* and *Fusobacterium*. Oral conditions also appear enriched: rheumatoid arthritis for increases in *Treponema*, and, among the periodontitis-decreased genera, head and neck cancer (*Actinomyces*, *Rothia*), smoking (*Capnocytophaga*, *Gemella*, *Lautropia*) and COVID-19 (*Neisseria*). These oral genera are common in any oral sample, so the next section compares conditions within body site groups.

### Enrichment compared within body site groups

Here each condition is compared only with studies from the same broad body site groups. "Oral" is broad: it includes saliva, tongue and other oral sites as well as plaque.

```{r bsdb-site-increased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-increased genera and how often other conditions report them increased (BugSigDB), compared within body site groups. Columns ordered by number of enriched genera (ties: sum of −log10 p). Cells: share of the condition's studies reporting the genus increased divided by the share expected from other conditions' studies from the same body site groups, weighted by the condition's own site mix. Shaded only with at least 2 studies reporting the genus; empty: not reported, 1 study, or no expected value. Numbers shown when ×2 or more or enriched; large ratios from 2–3 studies are uncertain unless outlined. Outlined: one-sided exact Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test of the condition's studies with the genus vs other conditions' studies, stratified by body site group (oral, upper airway, lower airway, gastrointestinal, urogenital, skin, eye, other, mixed)."
condition_heatmap("increased", match_site = TRUE)
```

```{r bsdb-site-decreased}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-decreased genera and how often other conditions report them decreased (BugSigDB), compared within body site groups. Columns ordered by number of enriched genera (ties: sum of −log10 p). Cells: share of the condition's studies reporting the genus decreased divided by the share expected from other conditions' studies from the same body site groups, weighted by the condition's own site mix. Shaded only with at least 2 studies reporting the genus; empty: not reported, 1 study, or no expected value. Numbers shown when ×2 or more or enriched; large ratios from 2–3 studies are uncertain unless outlined. Outlined: one-sided exact Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test of the condition's studies with the genus vs other conditions' studies, stratified by body site group (oral, upper airway, lower airway, gastrointestinal, urogenital, skin, eye, other, mixed)."
condition_heatmap("decreased", match_site = TRUE)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Data:** the same as the previous figure: the same units, genera and 40 tested conditions. The only change is that each condition is compared with other conditions' units from the same body site group. There is no All BugSigDB column.
- **Body site group:** each unit has one group (oral, upper airway, lower airway, gastrointestinal, urogenital, skin, eye, other), or "mixed" if its signatures' sites span several groups. Of all 1,892 units, 1,249 are gastrointestinal and 260 oral. The top bar still shows the share of units with any oral site.
- **Each cell (observed / expected):** observed is the condition's share of units with the genus. Expected averages, over the condition's site groups and weighted by its number of units in each, the share of other conditions' units in that group with the genus. Groups where the condition is the only one are skipped.
- **Example:** colorectal cancer × *Fusobacterium* is observed 54% (29/54) vs expected 8.6% (gastrointestinal: 28 of 48 colorectal cancer units vs 42 of 583 other units; oral: 1 of 5 vs 28 of 133), giving ×6.3. Other colorectal cancer ratios: *Parvimonas* ×13, *Peptostreptococcus* ×12, *Porphyromonas* ×6.6.
- **Shading rules:** a cell is shaded only if ≥ 2 of the condition's units have the genus (e.g. colorectal cancer × *Pseudoramibacter*, 1 unit at ×2.8, is blank). The colour is log2(ratio) capped at ×16. Ratios below 1 get the palest colour, so depletion is not shown. Numbers appear when ×2 or more, or when outlined.
- **Test:** a one-sided exact Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel test. It uses 2×2 tables (condition vs other × genus present vs absent) stratified by site group and tests a common odds ratio > 1. Strata without units from both the condition and others are dropped; with a single informative stratum, it is a one-sided Fisher's test. BH covers all 800 genus × condition tests per direction.
- **Result:** only colorectal cancer × *Peptostreptococcus*, *Parvimonas*, *Fusobacterium* and *Porphyromonas* have FDR < 0.05 (e.g. *Fusobacterium* p = 3e-15, FDR = 8e-13). No decreased cell passes.
- **What changed:** rheumatoid arthritis × *Treponema* is ×4.2 (5 of 8 oral rheumatoid arthritis units vs 19 of 130 other oral units), p = 0.005, FDR = 0.39. Smoking × *Gemella* is ×5.0, p = 0.001, FDR = 0.53. Head and neck cancer × *Rothia* is ×2.3, p = 0.02, FDR = 1. COVID-19 × *Neisseria* is ×2.7, p = 0.01, FDR = 1. These ratios stay high but are no longer significant once compared with other oral (or upper airway) studies.
- **Conditions shown:** the 12 core conditions plus any with p < 0.05 in this test. For increased, that adds response to transplant, treatment outcome measurement, diarrhoea and multiple sclerosis. For decreased, it adds atopic eczema, chronic fatigue syndrome, chronic kidney disease, psoriasis, response to immunochemotherapy, schizophrenia, type I diabetes and unipolar depression.
- **Watch out:** "oral" lumps plaque, saliva, tongue and mucosa, so plaque-specific genera can still look enriched in oral conditions sampled from plaque. Large ratios from 2–3 units are imprecise. The number of other units in a stratum can be small (e.g. 14–16 in eye or lower airway).
:::

**Shows:** only colorectal cancer survives body-site stratification, with the same four genera. Every oral-condition enrichment falls below FDR < 0.05 once it is compared with other oral studies, so sampling site accounts for much of the unstratified overlap. The ratios themselves stay high (rheumatoid arthritis × *Treponema* ×4.2, smoking × *Gemella* ×5.0), so this is a power problem as much as a confounding one: rheumatoid arthritis and smoking contribute 13 studies each to those tests, against 54 for colorectal cancer.

### Direction of periodontitis-associated genera within each condition

*When the condition reports the genus, is it in the same direction as in periodontitis?*

```{r bsdb-direction-combined}
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-associated genera and the direction other conditions report them in (BugSigDB). Left: the 20 periodontitis-increased genera; right: the 20 periodontitis-decreased genera, each with its names on the left and the PerioSigDB signatures reporting the genus decreased (bars to the left) or increased (bars to the right), coloured and shaded as in the consensus taxa figure (binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures; faded: not significant after Benjamini–Hochberg correction; palest: unadjusted p ≥ 0.05). Columns on each side: all of BugSigDB (next to the genus names), then the conditions with at least 4 of these genera reported by at least 3 of their studies with a clear direction, of which at least two thirds agree with periodontitis (first panel) or at least two thirds go the opposite way (second panel); each panel ordered by a two-sided sign test of that count against half, smallest p first. COVID-19 (gut) and rheumatoid arthritis (mouth): the same condition restricted to studies of one body site group, shown in both genus groups even where they do not meet these criteria (rheumatoid arthritis (mouth), decreased genera: 3 genera with a clear direction). In brackets: the number of genera agreeing or going the opposite way out of the genera with a clear direction. Cells: studies reporting the genus in its periodontitis direction (increased on the left, decreased on the right) / all studies reporting it; colour: from orange (all increased) to blue (all decreased). Grey: 1–2 studies; white: not reported. Hatched: mixed (3 or more studies, between one and two thirds of them in the periodontitis direction, e.g. 2 of 4), left out of the count in brackets. Outlined: two-sided binomial test of the cell's studies against 50% (FDR < 0.05), so an outlined cell can be significant in either direction. Top bars: share of the column's studies from oral sites."
direction_heatmap_combined()
```


::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Question:** among the condition's units that report the genus in either direction, what share report it in the periodontitis direction? It ignores how often the genus is reported relative to other conditions (see the enrichment figures).
- **Each cell:** "same / n", where n is the condition's units reporting the genus increased plus units reporting it decreased. The colour is the share in the periodontitis direction. For example, colorectal cancer × *Fusobacterium* is 29/34 (29 increased, 5 decreased).
- **Counting:** units are the same as in the enrichment figures (study × condition × direction × body site group). A study listing the genus in both an increased and a decreased signature counts once in each. This happens for 88 study × condition × genus combinations among the periodontitis-increased genera.
- **Grey and white cells:** grey means 1–2 units, with no share or label shown. These cells are still tested and can never reach p < 0.05. White means not reported.
- **Brackets:** of the genera with n ≥ 3 (cells with a label) and a clear direction, how many agree with periodontitis (left panel: at least two thirds of the units report the genus in the periodontitis direction) or go the opposite way (right panel: at most one third do), out of the genera with a clear direction. Genera without one ("mixed", e.g. 2/4 or 4/7) are hatched and left out.
- **Conditions and order:** a condition is shown if it has at least 4 genera with n ≥ 3 and a clear direction, and at least two thirds of them agree with periodontitis (left panel) or at least two thirds go the opposite way (right, outlined panel), the same threshold as for a single genus. Each panel is ordered by a two-sided sign test of that count against half of the genera, smallest p first. Cells keep the width of a 12-condition figure, so the figure is narrower rather than stretched. An earlier version ordered by the mean share per genus, which ranked conditions with only 2–3 such genera too high (e.g. obesity: *Prevotella* 5/11, *Fusobacterium* 5/7 and *Aggregatibacter* 3/3 averaged 72%), and counted any genus with more than half of its reports in one direction, so that genera split 50:50 decided whether a condition looked opposite (e.g. dry eye syndrome).
- **Conditions tested:** the conditions with ≥ 5 units across both directions (67 for increased, 66 for decreased, since only conditions reporting at least one of the genera have tests). Unlike the other figures, these do not show the 12 core conditions. A condition can appear in one figure and not the other, or agree in one and go the opposite way in the other (e.g. colorectal cancer), which the next figure shows for both genus groups together.
- **Test:** a two-sided exact binomial test of same vs opposite direction against 50%, BH-adjusted across all genus × condition tests per genus group (442 increased, 471 decreased), including conditions not shown.
- **All BugSigDB column:** pools all 1,892 units from every condition, including small ones. It has its own BH correction across its 20 genera, so its outlines are not part of the condition family. Increased genera: *Fusobacterium* 125/189 (FDR 7e-5), *Parvimonas* 64/82, *Peptostreptococcus* 71/92, *Porphyromonas* 91/149 and *Selenomonas* 45/67 lean increased. Decreased genera: *Haemophilus* 130/204 lean decreased (FDR 0.001), while *Streptococcus* 144/384, *Actinomyces* 58/158 and *Gemella* 40/108 lean increased, the opposite of periodontitis.
- **Significant condition cells:** only colorectal cancer: *Peptostreptococcus* 25/25 (FDR 3e-5), *Parvimonas* 22/22 (1e-4), *Porphyromonas* 20/21 (0.003) and *Fusobacterium* 29/34 (0.004), all in the periodontitis direction. *Gemella* is 0/15 decreased, i.e. 15 of 15 increased (FDR 0.03), the opposite direction.
- **Example of a non-significant cell:** head and neck cancer × *Rothia* is 7/8 decreased (p = 0.07, FDR = 1). Small n per cell gives little power after correction across ~450 tests.
- **Watch out:** a share near 50% can mean genuinely mixed reports or very few reports, so read it together with n. The direction of a genus in a unit comes from genus or species entries, so different species of one genus can push opposite ways.
:::

**Shows:** colorectal cancer is the only condition with genera whose direction differs significantly from 50% after BH correction: *Peptostreptococcus* (25/25 studies increased), *Parvimonas* (22/22), *Porphyromonas* (20/21) and *Fusobacterium* (29/34), all in the same direction as periodontitis. Its *Gemella*, decreased in periodontitis, is significant in the opposite direction (15/15 studies increased). The next figure summarises both directions for every condition.

#### Conditions with similar directions of association across periodontitis-associated genera

Each condition is summarised over all the periodontitis-associated genera its studies report, averaged over genera so that each genus counts once. This shows the direction of reports only: not how often the genera are reported compared with other conditions (see the enrichment heatmaps for that), and not whether the genera change together within participants.

```{r bsdb-agreement-map}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-cap: "Direction of the periodontitis-associated genera in each BugSigDB condition. Genera counted: those among the 20 per direction in the genus heatmaps reported by at least 3 of the condition's studies. A genus agrees with periodontitis if at least two thirds of these studies report it in the periodontitis direction and goes the opposite way if at most one third do; genera in between (e.g. 2 of 4 studies) have no clear direction and are left out, as in the direction heatmap. x: share of the periodontitis-increased genera with a clear direction that agree (reported increased); y: the same for the periodontitis-decreased genera (reported decreased). Conditions: those shown in either direction heatmap. Point size: number of genera counted. Shape: one per condition with body site points here or in the similarity overview (the same in both), circle otherwise. Colour: the body site group of at least two thirds of the condition's study units (grey: mixed). Shaded: same direction as periodontitis for both genus groups. Arrows: from all of a condition's studies to those of one body site group (labelled with the condition and site, in the condition's shape), for conditions whose position moves by at least 25 percentage points when restricted to that site (site groups with at least 3 genera with a clear direction in each genus group). COVID-19 and RA are mixed (no site group has two thirds of their units). CRC: colorectal cancer; GC: gastric cancer; HNC: head and neck cancer; PD: Parkinson's disease; RA: rheumatoid arthritis."
# arrows on the 50% lines, pointing outward from the centre, labelled in light grey at their tips
centre_arrow <- arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"), angle = 25, type = "open")
h_arrows <- tibble(xend = c(1.035, -0.035), label = c("Taxa increased\nin condition include\nperio-increased genera",
                                                      "Taxa decreased\nin condition include\nperio-increased genera"),
                   hjust = c(1, 0))
v_arrows <- tibble(yend = c(1.065, -0.065), label = c("Taxa decreased in condition include perio-decreased genera",
                                                      "Taxa increased in condition include perio-decreased genera"),
                   ly = c(1.085, -0.085), vjust = c(0, 1))

# only the conditions shown in the direction heatmap (either genus group)
heatmap_conditions <- union(direction_conditions("increased")$Condition, direction_conditions("decreased")$Condition)
# body site: a condition whose position moves by at least 0.25 when restricted to one body site group
# (with at least 3 genera with a clear direction in each genus group) also gets a point per such site
# group, with an arrow from all of its studies to those of the site
site_names <- c(oral = "mouth", gastrointestinal = "gut", "upper airway" = "airway", "lower airway" = "lung",
                urogenital = "urogenital", skin = "skin", eye = "eye", other = "other", mixed = "mixed sites")
site_points <- agreement_map_site |>
  filter(Condition %in% heatmap_conditions, informative_increased >= 3, informative_decreased >= 3) |>
  left_join(select(agreement_map, Condition, all_x = frac_increased, all_y = frac_decreased), by = "Condition") |>
  filter(any(sqrt((frac_increased - all_x)^2 + (frac_decreased - all_y)^2) >= 0.25), .by = Condition) |>
  mutate(label = paste0(Condition, " (", site_names[site_group], ")"), site = TRUE) |>
  select(-all_x, -all_y)
site_split_conditions <- unique(site_points$Condition)
# one filled shape per condition with body site points in this figure or the similarity overview, used in both (rheumatoid arthritis
# and head and neck cancer sit close together there: square and triangle keep them apart)
split_shapes <- c("Rheumatoid arthritis" = 22, "Colorectal cancer" = 23, "Head and neck cancer" = 24, "COVID-19" = 25)
site_colours <- c(mouth = "#1b9e77", gut = "#a6761d", airway = "#7570b3", other = "grey45")
unit_site_colours <- c(mouth = "#1b9e77", gut = "#a6761d", airway = "#7570b3", lung = "#e7298a",
                       urogenital = "#66a61e", skin = "#e6ab02", eye = "#1f78b4", other = "grey55",
                       "mixed sites" = "grey30")
# shared with the similarity overview: point colour (the body site group of at least two thirds of the
# units, else mixed) and common abbreviations for the point labels (spelled out in the captions)
ov_mixed <- "mixed (no site ≥ 2/3)"
ov_site_colours <- c(unit_site_colours[names(unit_site_colours) != "mixed sites"], setNames("grey60", ov_mixed))
ov_abbreviations <- c("Alzheimer's disease" = "AD", "Autism spectrum disorder" = "ASD", "Colorectal cancer" = "CRC",
                      "Dry eye syndrome" = "Dry eye", "Gastric cancer" = "GC", "Head and neck cancer" = "HNC",
                      "HIV infection" = "HIV", "Parkinson's disease" = "PD", "Rheumatoid arthritis" = "RA",
                      "Schizophrenia" = "SCZ", "Smoking behavior" = "Smoking", "Type I diabetes mellitus" = "T1D",
                      "Ulcerative colitis" = "UC", "Unipolar depression" = "MDD")
ov_abbrev <- \(x) coalesce(unname(ov_abbreviations[x]), x)
main_site_of <- \(site_group, share) ifelse(share >= 2/3, coalesce(site_names[as.character(site_group)], "other"), ov_mixed)
# main body site of all of a condition's study units (both directions)
condition_main_site <- bsdb_sigs |>
  count(Condition, site_group) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n), .by = Condition) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = Condition) |>
  transmute(Condition, main_site = main_site_of(site_group, share))
agreement_plot <- agreement_map |>
  filter(Condition %in% heatmap_conditions) |>
  mutate(site = FALSE) |>
  left_join(condition_main_site, by = "Condition") |>
  # body site points first, so that at tied coordinates they sit on the side their arrow comes from
  (\(d) bind_rows(mutate(site_points, main_site = main_site_of(site_group, rep(1, n()))), d))() |>
  # conditions at identical coordinates are spread slightly sideways so that both are visible
  mutate(plot_x = frac_increased + (row_number() - (n() + 1) / 2) * 0.035, .by = c(frac_increased, frac_decreased)) |>
  mutate(main_site = factor(main_site, levels = names(ov_site_colours)),
         # main point: the condition's abbreviation; body site points: the condition and the site
         label = ifelse(site, paste(ov_abbrev(Condition), site_names[site_group]), ov_abbrev(Condition)),
         # conditions with body site points here or in the similarity overview get their own filled shape (square,
         # diamond, triangles), with or without arrows; others a circle
         shape = coalesce(unname(split_shapes[Condition]), 21))
# arrows from a condition (all studies) to its body site points, shortened to stop short of the points
site_arrows <- inner_join(filter(agreement_plot, !site) |> select(Condition, x = plot_x, y = frac_decreased),
                          filter(agreement_plot, site) |> select(Condition, xend = plot_x, yend = frac_decreased),
                          by = "Condition") |>
  mutate(d = sqrt((xend - x)^2 + (yend - y)^2), gap = pmin(0.1, d * 0.35),
         x0 = x + (xend - x) * 0.05 / d, y0 = y + (yend - y) * 0.05 / d,
         x1 = xend - (xend - x) * gap / d, y1 = yend - (yend - y) * gap / d)
# label data: the points, plus unlabelled points along the arrows (so that labels are pushed off them);
# points on or just below the 50% line get their labels below, away from the grey arrow labels
map_labels <- bind_rows(
  agreement_plot |> transmute(plot_x, frac_decreased, label, point_size = 8 * sqrt(genera / max(genera)),
                              text_size = ifelse(site, 2.9, 3.1), face = ifelse(site, "italic", "plain"),
                              text_col = ifelse(site, "grey40", "grey15"),
                              ny = ifelse(abs(frac_decreased - 0.5) < 0.1, -0.08, 0)),
  site_arrows |> mutate(n = pmax(2, ceiling(d / 0.03))) |>
    reframe(t = seq(0.15, 0.85, length.out = n), .by = c(x0, y0, x1, y1, n)) |>
    transmute(plot_x = x0 + (x1 - x0) * t, frac_decreased = y0 + (y1 - y0) * t, label = "", point_size = 1,
              text_size = 2.9, face = "plain", text_col = "grey40", ny = 0))

p_map <- ggplot(agreement_plot, aes(plot_x, frac_decreased)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = 1, ymin = 0.5, ymax = 1, fill = "grey94") +
  # dashed lines, with solid heads at the tips (a dashed arrow draws a broken head)
  geom_segment(data = h_arrows, aes(x = 0.5, xend = xend, y = 0.5, yend = 0.5), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_segment(data = v_arrows, aes(x = 0.5, xend = 0.5, y = 0.5, yend = yend), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_segment(data = h_arrows, aes(x = xend - sign(xend - 0.5) * 0.001, xend = xend, y = 0.5, yend = 0.5),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey60", arrow = centre_arrow, linejoin = "mitre") +
  geom_segment(data = v_arrows, aes(x = 0.5, xend = 0.5, y = yend - sign(yend - 0.5) * 0.001, yend = yend),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey60", arrow = centre_arrow, linejoin = "mitre") +
  geom_text(data = h_arrows, aes(x = xend, y = 0.52, label = label, hjust = hjust), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            vjust = 0, size = 2.7, color = "grey55", lineheight = 0.9) +
  geom_text(data = v_arrows, aes(x = 0.5, y = ly, label = label, vjust = vjust), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            size = 2.7, color = "grey55") +
  # body site arrows, above the shading
  geom_segment(data = site_arrows, aes(x = x0, y = y0, xend = x1, yend = y1), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               color = "grey35", linewidth = 0.5, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), angle = 25, type = "open")) +
  geom_point(aes(size = genera, fill = main_site, shape = shape), color = "grey15", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_point(aes(size = genera, shape = shape), color = "grey15", fill = NA) +
  scale_shape_identity() +
  # (text size and face set per label outside aes, so that they do not share the point size scale)
  geom_label_repel(data = map_labels, aes(label = label, point.size = point_size),
                   size = map_labels$text_size, fontface = map_labels$face, color = map_labels$text_col,
                   fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.75), linewidth = 0, label.padding = unit(0.08, "lines"),
                   nudge_y = map_labels$ny, seed = 1, min.segment.length = 0, box.padding = 0.4,
                   point.padding = 0.1, force = 4, segment.color = "grey50", segment.size = 0.3,
                   max.overlaps = Inf, max.iter = 20000, ylim = c(-0.02, 1.02)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 8, name = "Genera counted") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ov_site_colours, name = "Main body site", drop = TRUE,
                    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, size = 4, alpha = 1))) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25)) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(-0.05, 1.05), ylim = c(-0.13, 1.13), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Share of periodontitis-increased genera reported increased in the condition",
       y = "Share of periodontitis-decreased genera reported decreased in the condition") +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_text(size = 9))

p_map
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each point:** one BugSigDB condition. Its x and y are the agreeing genera out of the genera with a clear direction, i.e. the bracketed counts of the increased and decreased halves of the direction heatmap (for a condition shown there). Conditions with identical values are drawn slightly apart sideways.
- **x:** of the periodontitis-increased genera (top 20) reported by ≥ 3 of the condition's units, those with a clear direction: agreeing (at least two thirds of the units report the genus increased) or opposite (at most one third do). x is agreeing ÷ (agreeing + opposite). Genera in between (e.g. 2 of 4 units increased) are left out, as in the direction heatmap. A group with no genus with a clear direction is placed at 50%.
- **y:** the same for the periodontitis-decreased genera, with agreeing meaning reported decreased by at least two thirds of the units.
- **Inclusion:** the conditions shown in either direction heatmap, which all have ≥ 3 such genera in each direction. Other conditions of the core set (HIV infection, obesity, ulcerative colitis, type 2 diabetes, Alzheimer's disease) meet neither heatmap's criteria and are not shown.
- **Point size:** genera counted (reported by ≥ 3 units), both directions combined and including those without a clear direction.
- **Colour:** the body site group of at least two thirds of the condition's study units (both directions), as in the similarity overview; grey (mixed) otherwise. A body site point takes the colour of its site.
- **Sign test (text only):** a two-sided exact binomial test of the agreeing genera, pooled over both genus groups, against half of the genera with a clear direction. Genera without a clear direction are left out. No correction across conditions.
- **Example (colorectal cancer):** x = 10 of 10 (100%): *Aggregatibacter* 4/4, *Campylobacter* 8/9, *Dialister* 9/12, *Fusobacterium* 29/34, *Mogibacterium* 5/6, *Parvimonas* 22/22, *Peptostreptococcus* 25/25, *Porphyromonas* 20/21, *Prevotella* 15/20 and *Selenomonas* 8/9 are all reported increased by at least two thirds of studies. y = 1 of 5 (20%): *Haemophilus* (7/10) agrees; *Bacillus* 1/3, *Corynebacterium* 1/6, *Gemella* 0/15 and *Granulicatella* 0/4 go the opposite way; *Actinomyces* 5/11, *Neisseria* 4/8, *Rothia* 2/5 and *Streptococcus* 10/24 have no clear direction and are left out.
- **Other values:** the counts for the conditions discussed are given in the text below the figure.
- **Watch out:** this shows direction only, not frequency or enrichment. A genus counts as agreeing whether its reports are 4/7 or 25/25, and most rest on 3–10 units. With few genera the axes are coarse (e.g. 2 of 3 = 67%), so check point size and the direction heatmap. An earlier version plotted the mean share per genus, which let a single 3/3 genus dominate a condition with few genera.
:::

```{r bsdb-agreement-values}
am <- \(cond, col) agreement_map[[col]][agreement_map$Condition == cond]
# "agreeing of counted" genera in one genus group
ag <- \(cond, dir) {
  mixed <- am(cond, paste0("genera_", dir)) - am(cond, paste0("informative_", dir))
  paste0(am(cond, paste0("agree_", dir)), " of ", am(cond, paste0("informative_", dir)),
         if (mixed > 0) paste0(" (", mixed, " mixed)") else "")
}
```

**Shows:** three patterns. Sign tests across genera are unadjusted for the number of conditions.

- **Same direction as periodontitis for both genus groups (top right):** head and neck cancer (`r ag("Head and neck cancer", "increased")` periodontitis-increased genera agree (reported increased by at least two thirds of studies) and `r ag("Head and neck cancer", "decreased")` periodontitis-decreased genera agree; `r am("Head and neck cancer", "agree")` of `r am("Head and neck cancer", "informative")` genera with a clear direction overall, sign test p = `r signif(am("Head and neck cancer", "p"), 1)`). Smoking agrees for the periodontitis-decreased genera (`r ag("Smoking behavior", "decreased")`) but not for the periodontitis-increased genera (`r ag("Smoking behavior", "increased")`; overall p = `r signif(am("Smoking behavior", "p"), 1)`). *Haemophilus*, *Neisseria* and *Corynebacterium* are decreased in both; also *Rothia* and *Actinomyces* in head and neck cancer, *Gemella* and *Lautropia* in smoking. Both are sampled mostly in the mouth, and smoking is a periodontitis risk factor.
- **Both genus groups reported increased (bottom right):** colorectal cancer, gastric cancer and rheumatoid arthritis report most periodontitis-increased genera increased (colorectal cancer `r ag("Colorectal cancer", "increased")`) but few periodontitis-decreased genera decreased (colorectal cancer `r ag("Colorectal cancer", "decreased")`; e.g. *Gemella* increased in 15 of 15 colorectal cancer studies). The two groups pull in opposite directions, so none of these is significant overall. The whole-signature similarity analyses below do not flag colorectal cancer's increased signatures overall as resembling the periodontitis-decreased signature, because they score whole signatures, in which these genera are a small part; only its few mouth studies do. For ulcerative colitis and COVID-19 gut studies they do. This pattern is compatible with increased representation of oral-associated genera in gastrointestinal disease, but does not establish their source or route of transfer.
- **Opposite to periodontitis (left):** COVID-19 (`r ag("COVID-19", "increased")` and `r ag("COVID-19", "decreased")`; `r am("COVID-19", "agree")` of `r am("COVID-19", "informative")` genera with a clear direction overall, p = `r signif(am("COVID-19", "p"), 1)`) reports the periodontitis-increased genera mostly decreased, and so, less clearly, does Parkinson's disease (`r ag("Parkinson's disease", "increased")` and `r ag("Parkinson's disease", "decreased")`).

### Whole-signature similarity to periodontitis

Compares whole signatures using taxa at their reported ranks (mostly species, with some genera and higher ranks), without collapsing to genus.

- **PerioSigDB consensus:** taxa more often increased (`r length(semsim$consensus$increased)`) or decreased (`r length(semsim$consensus$decreased)`) in periodontitis signatures (binomial test, unadjusted p < 0.05).
