- **Similarity:** semantic similarity on the NCBI taxonomy (best-match average of Lin similarity, as in BugSigDB's tools), for BugSigDB signatures with at least 5 taxa (smaller ones give extreme scores).

```{r bsdb-semantic-c}
# one row of the similarity tests, and a short text summary of it
sv_row <- function(cond, dir, perio = dir, kind = "all", site = NA) {
  st <- semsim_tests$stats
  st[st$Condition == cond & st$direction == dir & st$perio == perio & st$kind == kind &
       (if (is.na(site)) is.na(st$site) else !is.na(st$site) & st$site == site), ]
}
sv <- function(...) {
  r <- sv_row(...)
  sprintf("mean rank %.2f, p = %s, FDR = %s", r$mean_rank, signif(r$p, 1), signif(r$fdr, 1))
}
sim_set_label <- \(cond, kind, site) case_when(
  kind == "all" ~ cond,
  kind == "site_all" ~ paste0(cond, " (", site_names[site], ")"),
  .default = paste0(cond, " (", site_names[site], " vs ", site_names[site], ")"))

# conditions shown in both similarity figures: unadjusted p < 0.05 in any of their tests
sim_conditions <- unique(semsim_tests$stats$Condition[semsim_tests$stats$p < 0.05])

comparison_levels <- c("Perio increased\nvs BugSigDB increased", "Perio decreased\nvs BugSigDB decreased",
                       "Perio increased\nvs BugSigDB decreased", "Perio decreased\nvs BugSigDB increased")
label_comparison <- \(d) mutate(d, comparison = factor(sprintf("Perio %s\nvs BugSigDB %s", perio, direction),
                                                       levels = comparison_levels),
                                opposite = perio != direction)

# rows of the boxed figure: per condition, all of its units vs all other conditions first, then by p (same-
# direction columns) its units from each site group vs the same site group (where a proper background) and
# vs all of BugSigDB (only where p < 0.05 in some column and not the same units as the first row)
sim_rows <- function(res, conditions) {
  all_n <- filter(res$stats, kind == "all") |> select(Condition, direction, perio, all_n = studies)
  site_all_keep <- res$stats |>
    filter(kind == "site_all") |>
    left_join(all_n, by = c("Condition", "direction", "perio")) |>
    summarise(keep = any(p < 0.05) & !all(studies == all_n, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(Condition, site)) |>
    filter(keep)
  stats <- res$stats |>
    filter(Condition %in% conditions, kind != "site_all" | paste(Condition, site) %in% paste(site_all_keep$Condition, site_all_keep$site))
  cond_order <- stats |> filter(direction == perio) |> summarise(p = min(p), .by = Condition) |> arrange(p) |> pull(Condition)
  gap <- 0.6
  rows <- stats |>
    summarise(p_same = suppressWarnings(min(p[direction == perio])), .by = c(Condition, kind, site)) |>
    mutate(Condition = factor(Condition, levels = cond_order)) |>
    arrange(Condition, kind != "all", p_same) |>
    mutate(pos = -(row_number() + (as.integer(Condition) - 1) * gap),
           label = case_when(kind == "all" ~ as.character(Condition),
                             kind == "site_all" ~ paste0("   ", site_names[site], " studies (vs all BugSigDB)"),
                             .default = paste0("   ", site_names[site], " studies (vs ", site_names[site], ")")),
           Condition = as.character(Condition))
  list(rows = rows, stats = stats)
}

similarity_boxes <- function(res, conditions) {
  r <- sim_rows(res, conditions)
  rows <- r$rows
  keys <- c("Condition", "kind", "site")
  boxes <- rows |> summarise(ymin = min(pos) - 0.45, ymax = max(pos) + 0.45, .by = Condition)
  stats <- r$stats |> inner_join(select(rows, all_of(keys), pos), by = keys) |> label_comparison() |>
    mutate(significance = case_when(fdr < 0.05 ~ "FDR < 0.05", p < 0.05 ~ "p < 0.05", .default = "Not significant") |>
             factor(levels = c("FDR < 0.05", "p < 0.05", "Not significant")))
  units <- res$units |> inner_join(select(rows, all_of(keys), pos), by = keys) |> label_comparison() |>
    mutate(point_colour = factor(coalesce(site_names[site_group], "other"), levels = names(unit_site_colours)))
  shade <- distinct(stats, comparison, opposite) |> filter(opposite)

  ggplot(stats, aes(y = pos)) +
    geom_rect(data = shade, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              fill = "grey95") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, color = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_rect(data = boxes, aes(xmin = -0.03, xmax = 1.03, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_quasirandom(data = units, aes(x = rank, color = point_colour), orientation = "y", width = 0.3,
                     size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = mean_rank - ci, xmax = mean_rank + ci), width = 0, linewidth = 0.7,
                  color = "grey10", orientation = "y") +
    geom_point(aes(x = mean_rank, fill = significance), shape = 21, size = 3, color = "grey10", stroke = 0.7) +
    scale_color_manual(values = unit_site_colours, name = "Body site") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("FDR < 0.05" = "grey10", "p < 0.05" = "grey60", "Not significant" = "white"),
                      name = "Mean", drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = rows$pos, labels = rows$label, expand = expansion(add = 0.3)) +
    # coordinate limits, not scale limits, so that bars reaching past 1 are clipped rather than dropped
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.03, 1.03), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
    facet_grid(. ~ comparison) +
    labs(x = "Similarity (share of other conditions' study units of the same direction it is more similar than; 0.5 = typical)",
         y = NULL) +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), legend.position = "top",
          panel.spacing.x = unit(0.8, "lines"), panel.border = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0, face = ifelse(rows$kind == "all", "bold", "plain")))
}
```

```{r bsdb-semantic-boxes}
#| fig-width: 13.5
#| fig-height: !expr 1.4 + 0.36 * (nrow(sim_rows(semsim_tests, sim_conditions)$rows) + 0.6 * length(sim_conditions))
#| fig-cap: "Similarity of BugSigDB signatures to the PerioSigDB consensus signatures, for all of a condition's study units and by body site group. Each study unit's mean best-match average Lin similarity is ranked against the study units of all other conditions with the same BugSigDB direction (the share of them it is more similar than; 0.5 = typical). Boxes: one condition each. First row (bold): all of its study units, compared with all other conditions. Then, ordered by p: its study units from one body site group, compared only with other conditions' units from the same site group (\"vs gut\", \"vs mouth\"; only where that site group has at least 20 such units from at least 10 other conditions in the direction, which excludes airway and eye) or with all other conditions (\"vs all BugSigDB\"; shown only where p < 0.05 in some column and the condition has units from more than one site group). Columns: similarity to the periodontitis-increased or -decreased consensus, for BugSigDB signatures of the same direction (white) or the opposite direction (shaded). Conditions: those with unadjusted p < 0.05 in any row and column, ordered by their smallest p in the two same-direction columns, most significant at top. Small points: study units, coloured by body site group; large point and bar: mean and 95% confidence interval. Large point black: FDR < 0.05; grey: unadjusted p < 0.05; one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test of the units' similarities against those of the other conditions (BH within each column, separately for the three kinds of row). A row has no point in a column with fewer than 5 study units of that direction. Left of 0.5: less similar than typical; the test is one-sided, so this side is not tested."
similarity_boxes(semsim_tests, sim_conditions)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **PerioSigDB consensus signatures:** taxa at their reported rank (species and genera are separate taxa; not collapsed). A taxon is in the consensus if it has more increased than decreased PerioSigDB signatures (or vice versa) with an exact binomial p < 0.05, unadjusted. This gives 32 increased and 12 decreased taxa. Precomputed in a separate step, together with the similarity scores below.
- **Similarity of one BugSigDB signature:** Lin similarity on the NCBI taxonomy, based on how specific the taxa's most specific shared ancestor is. Information content is computed from descendant counts. The best-match average works in both directions: each consensus taxon is matched to its most similar taxon in the signature, those best scores are averaged, the same is done from the signature side, and the two averages are averaged. Partial credit therefore goes to relatives, e.g. a BugSigDB genus vs a PerioSigDB species of it.
- **Signatures used:** the same disease-vs-control signatures as the heatmaps, with ≥ 5 NCBI taxa (1,751 of 3,208). Taxa missing from the ontology are dropped. A unit's score is the mean over its signatures, giving 646 increased and 584 decreased units. Periodontitis studies are not in BugSigDB here.
- **Background:** the study units of all *other* conditions with the same BugSigDB direction, so a condition is never compared with itself. For the "vs" rows, only those from the same body site group. A site group is used as a background only with ≥ 20 such units from ≥ 10 other conditions in that direction: gut (366–416 units from 156 conditions), mouth (77–88 from 52–55) and urogenital (26–52 from 24–36). Upper airway (7–11 other units, as COVID-19 is 15 of its 22 decreased units), eye, skin, lung and other groups are too small.
- **Test:** one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann–Whitney) test, normal approximation, of the set's similarities against the background's: is the set more similar than the other conditions? Sets need ≥ 5 study units of the direction (`r n_distinct(semsim_tests$stats$Condition[semsim_tests$stats$kind == "all" & semsim_tests$stats$direction == "increased"])` conditions with increased and `r n_distinct(semsim_tests$stats$Condition[semsim_tests$stats$kind == "all" & semsim_tests$stats$direction == "decreased"])` with decreased units for the first rows). BH runs within each column, separately for the three kinds of row (all units, within site group, site group vs all BugSigDB). The bar is the mean rank ± 1.96 SD/√n, a normal approximation and not a bootstrap.
- **Rank shown:** the share of background units the unit is more similar than (ties half), which equals the rank-sum effect size on average. The ranks are used because raw scores vary little (median 0.41 among all increased units vs 0.48 for colorectal cancer).
- **Columns:** BugSigDB direction × consensus. The white columns pair same directions (the main test). The shaded columns pair opposite directions, e.g. "Perio decreased vs BugSigDB increased", which asks whether a condition's increased taxa resemble periodontitis-depleted (health-associated) taxa.
- **Example:** colorectal cancer increased vs periodontitis-increased: all `r sv_row("Colorectal cancer", "increased")$studies` units, `r sv("Colorectal cancer", "increased")`; its `r sv_row("Colorectal cancer", "increased", kind = "site", site = "gastrointestinal")$studies` gut units vs other gut units, `r sv("Colorectal cancer", "increased", kind = "site", site = "gastrointestinal")`.
- **Watch out:** a site group compared with all of BugSigDB (mostly gut studies) can look periodontitis-like because of its site alone; the "vs" row of the same site corrects for this where there is one. The score covers the whole signature, so a few shared genera (e.g. colorectal cancer *Gemella*) barely move it. Many tests are run (4 columns × about 30 conditions, plus their site groups), so expect some unadjusted hits by chance.
:::

**Shows:** colorectal cancer is the only condition whose similarity holds within its own body site: its increased signatures resemble the periodontitis-increased consensus compared with all other conditions (`r sv("Colorectal cancer", "increased")`) and with other gut studies only (`r sv("Colorectal cancer", "increased", kind = "site", site = "gastrointestinal")`). Its few mouth studies instead report increased taxa resembling the periodontitis-decreased consensus (`r sv("Colorectal cancer", "increased", "decreased", kind = "site_all", site = "oral")`). Head and neck cancer's decreased signatures resemble the periodontitis-decreased consensus (`r sv("Head and neck cancer", "decreased")`), less so compared with other mouth studies only (`r sv("Head and neck cancer", "decreased", kind = "site", site = "oral")`). The decreased signatures of smoking (`r sv("Smoking behavior", "decreased")`) and of COVID-19 airway studies (`r sv("COVID-19", "decreased", kind = "site_all", site = "upper airway")`), and the signatures of rheumatoid arthritis mouth studies, resemble periodontitis compared with all of BugSigDB, which is mostly gut studies. Compared with other mouth studies, smoking is typical (`r sv("Smoking behavior", "decreased", kind = "site", site = "oral")`), and there are too few other airway studies to compare COVID-19 with. In the shaded columns, the increased signatures of COVID-19 and ulcerative colitis gut studies resemble the periodontitis-decreased consensus compared with other gut studies (`r sv("COVID-19", "increased", "decreased", kind = "site", site = "gastrointestinal")` and `r sv("Ulcerative colitis", "increased", "decreased", kind = "site", site = "gastrointestinal")`), the "both genus groups reported increased" pattern of the direction summary above.

```{r bsdb-jaccard}
# the same tests with the BugSigDB paper's other measure: Jaccard overlap of genera
consensus_genera <- map(semsim$consensus, \(ids) {
  known <- unique(c(sig_genera(dat)$taxon, bsdb_genera$taxon))
  # NCBI disambiguates some genus names (e.g. "Rothia <high G+C Gram-positive bacteria>"); drop the qualifier
  # so that they match the MetaPhlAn genus names used everywhere else
  strip_homonym <- \(x) sub(" <[^>]+>", "", x)
  unique(na.omit(map_chr(strsplit(taxon_sim$lineage[ids], "|", fixed = TRUE), \(l) {
    l <- strip_homonym(l)
    hit <- which(l %in% known)
    if (length(hit)) l[max(hit)] else NA
  })))
})
jaccard <- \(a, b) length(intersect(a, b)) / length(union(a, b))
jaccard_units <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  filter(lengths(bsdb_cc$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`[sig]) >= 5) |>
  inner_join(summarise(sig_genera(bsdb_cc), g = list(unique(taxon)), .by = sig), by = "sig") |>
  mutate(up = map_dbl(g, jaccard, consensus_genera$increased), down = map_dbl(g, jaccard, consensus_genera$decreased)) |>
  summarise(increased = mean(up), decreased = mean(down), .by = c(unit, Condition, direction, site_group)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(increased, decreased), names_to = "perio", values_to = "sim")
# the same tests as for semantic similarity: all of a condition's units vs all other conditions ("all"), and
# its units from one site group vs other conditions' units from the same site group ("site")
jaccard_res <- similarity_tests(jaccard_units)$stats
jaccard_tests <- list(all = filter(jaccard_res, kind == "all"), site = filter(jaccard_res, kind == "site"))
jt <- \(version, cond, dir, site = "gastrointestinal") with(
  filter(jaccard_tests[[version]], Condition == cond, direction == dir, perio == dir,
         version == "all" | site == !!site),
  format(signif(fdr, 1), scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE))
# same-direction results with FDR < 0.05, e.g. "colorectal cancer (gut) increased, FDR 1e-14"
jaccard_list <- function(version, drop = character(0)) {
  d <- filter(jaccard_tests[[version]], fdr < 0.05, perio == direction, !Condition %in% drop) |> arrange(fdr)
  paste0(d$Condition, if (version == "site") paste0(" (", site_names[d$site], ")") else "", " ", d$direction,
         " (FDR ", signif(d$fdr, 1), ")", collapse = "; ")
}
jaccard_hits <- \(version) with(filter(jaccard_tests[[version]], fdr < 0.05, perio == direction),
                                paste0(Condition, " (", direction, ")", collapse = ", "))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Details
- **No figure:** the numbers appear in the text below the chunk and in "Agreement across approaches".
- **Consensus genera:** each consensus taxon is mapped to the deepest name in its NCBI lineage that is a genus seen in PerioSigDB or BugSigDB; taxa above genus are dropped. This gives 16 increased genera, all among the heatmap's top 20, and 9 decreased genera: *Streptococcus*, *Gemella*, *Actinomyces*, *Rothia*, *Corynebacterium*, *Granulicatella*, *Lautropia*, *Neisseria* and *Haemophilus*. *Streptococcus* comes from *S. sanguinis* (decreased) only. These are the same genus sets as the participant-level colorectal cancer analysis.
- **Score:** Jaccard = shared genera / all genera in either set, between a signature's genera (MetaPhlAn `g__`) and each consensus genus set. The score is averaged over a unit's signatures, using signatures with ≥ 5 taxa; signatures with no genus-level taxa are dropped.
- **Test:** the same as for semantic similarity: a one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test of a condition's units against those of all other conditions of the same direction, or of its units from one body site group against other conditions' units from that site group (gut, mouth or urogenital), ≥ 5 units, BH within each direction × consensus pair.
- **Same-direction results with FDR < 0.05, all units:** `r jaccard_list("all")`.
- **Within body site groups:** `r jaccard_list("site")`.
- **Why it differs from semantic similarity:** Jaccard counts only exact genus matches and is reduced by long signatures. It ignores related genera, which semantic similarity partly credits, and taxon rank, since everything is collapsed to genus.
:::

**A second similarity measure:** the BugSigDB paper also used Jaccard overlap of genera. With the periodontitis consensus collapsed to genus (`r lengths(consensus_genera)[["increased"]]` and `r lengths(consensus_genera)[["decreased"]]` genera), colorectal cancer's increased signatures are again the most periodontitis-like (FDR = `r jt("all", "Colorectal cancer", "increased")`; `r jt("site", "Colorectal cancer", "increased")` within body site groups). The two measures do not fully agree, though: across all study units, Jaccard overlap also flags `r jaccard_list("all", drop = "Colorectal cancer")` after correction, and within body site groups `r jaccard_list("site", drop = "Colorectal cancer")` (see "Agreement across approaches" for a side-by-side comparison). Jaccard overlap counts only exact genus matches, whereas semantic similarity also credits related taxa, so conclusions for conditions other than colorectal cancer depend partly on the measure used.

The next figure condenses the per-condition similarity figure above into one point per condition: in which direction the condition reports each periodontitis consensus, judged by whether its increased or its decreased signatures resemble it more. The axes match the direction summary above.

```{r bsdb-semantic-overview}
#| fig-width: 10.5
#| fig-height: 8.2
#| fig-cap: "Overview of the whole-signature similarity of BugSigDB conditions to the PerioSigDB consensus signatures: in which direction each condition reports each periodontitis consensus. Similarity is the mean rank of the condition's study units among the study units of all other conditions with the same BugSigDB direction (the share of them each unit is more similar than; 0.5 = typical), as in the per-condition similarity figure above, and only the excess above 0.5 counts (a rank below 0.5 means not similar, and adds nothing). x: for the periodontitis-increased consensus, excess similarity of the condition's increased signatures minus that of its decreased signatures (right: the condition reports these taxa increased; left: decreased). y: the same for the periodontitis-decreased consensus, its decreased minus its increased signatures (up: the condition reports these taxa decreased; down: increased). The quadrants read as in the direction summary: top right (shaded), same direction as periodontitis; bottom right, both consensus signatures resemble the condition's increased taxa; top left, both resemble its decreased taxa. Points: all of a condition's study units, compared with all other conditions. Points: shown only with unadjusted p < 0.05 in at least one of their four comparisons; a condition whose all-units point has none is shown by its significant site points instead, labelled with its name (e.g. autism spectrum disorder: its gut studies compared with other gut studies). Arrows: to the condition's study units from one body site group (same shape as the condition, for conditions with more than one point; labelled with the condition and site), compared with all other conditions (e.g. \"RA mouth (vs all)\") or only with other conditions' study units from the same site group (e.g. \"RA mouth (vs mouth)\"), where any of the four mean ranks of the per-condition similarity figure above changes by at least 0.15; where a site group's two comparisons nearly coincide (within 0.1), only the within-site one is shown. Rheumatoid arthritis has no all-units point (no comparison with p < 0.05), so its arrow runs from its mouth studies compared with all other conditions to the same studies compared with other mouth studies. A direction with fewer than 5 study units is not tested and counts as 0 in both differences. Point size: study units (both directions). Colour: the body site group of at least two thirds of the set's study units (grey: mixed). Shaded: same direction as periodontitis for both. AD: Alzheimer's disease; ASD: autism spectrum disorder; CRC: colorectal cancer; GC: gastric cancer; HNC: head and neck cancer; MDD: unipolar (major) depression; RA: rheumatoid arthritis; SCZ: schizophrenia; T1D: type 1 diabetes; UC: ulcerative colitis."
# columns of the per-condition similarity figure above, by BugSigDB direction . periodontitis consensus
ov_cols <- c("increased.increased" = "inc_same", "increased.decreased" = "inc_opp",
             "decreased.decreased" = "dec_same", "decreased.increased" = "dec_opp")
ov_sets <- semsim_tests$stats |>
  filter(Condition %in% sim_conditions) |>
  mutate(col = ov_cols[paste(direction, perio, sep = ".")]) |>
  select(kind, Condition, site, col, mean_rank, p, studies) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = c(mean_rank, p, studies))
ov_base <- filter(ov_sets, kind == "all")
ov_min_p <- \(d) pmin(d$p_inc_same, d$p_inc_opp, d$p_dec_same, d$p_dec_opp, na.rm = TRUE)
# conditions whose all-units point has no comparison with p < 0.05: their significant site points stand in for it
weak_conditions <- ov_base$Condition[ov_min_p(ov_base) >= 0.05]
# body site sets: kept where any of the four mean ranks moves by at least 0.15 from all of the condition's units,
# or where they are significant and the condition's all-units point is not
ov_change <- ov_sets |>
  filter(kind != "all") |>
  inner_join(select(ov_base, Condition, starts_with("mean_rank")), by = "Condition", suffix = c("", "_all")) |>
  mutate(change = pmax(abs(mean_rank_inc_same - mean_rank_inc_same_all), abs(mean_rank_inc_opp - mean_rank_inc_opp_all),
                       abs(mean_rank_dec_same - mean_rank_dec_same_all), abs(mean_rank_dec_opp - mean_rank_dec_opp_all),
                       na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  filter(change >= 0.15 | (Condition %in% weak_conditions & ov_min_p(pick(everything())) < 0.05)) |>
  select(all_of(names(ov_sets)))
# excess similarity above typical (0.5); below typical counts as 0, and so does a missing comparison
excess <- \(r) pmax(coalesce(r, 0.5) - 0.5, 0)
ov <- bind_rows(ov_change, ov_base) |>
  # x: the periodontitis-increased consensus, resembled by the condition's increased minus its decreased signatures;
  # y: the periodontitis-decreased consensus, resembled by its decreased minus its increased signatures
  # (organised by periodontitis consensus, like the axes of the direction summary)
  mutate(px = excess(mean_rank_inc_same) - excess(mean_rank_dec_opp),
         py = excess(mean_rank_dec_same) - excess(mean_rank_inc_opp),
         units = coalesce(studies_inc_same, 0L) + coalesce(studies_dec_same, 0L),
         # main point: the condition's name; body site points: the site and comparison (shape shows the condition)
         label = case_when(kind == "all" ~ ov_abbrev(Condition), kind == "site_all" ~ paste(site_names[site], "(vs all)"),
                           .default = paste0(site_names[site], " (vs ", site_names[site], ")"))) |>
  # colour: the body site group of at least two thirds of the set's study units (both directions), else mixed
  left_join(semsim_tests$units |> distinct(kind, Condition, site, unit, site_group) |>
              count(kind, Condition, site, site_group) |>
              mutate(share = n / sum(n), .by = c(kind, Condition, site)) |>
              slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = c(kind, Condition, site)) |>
              transmute(kind, Condition, site,
                        main_site = ifelse(share >= 2/3, coalesce(site_names[site_group], "other"), ov_mixed)),
            by = c("kind", "Condition", "site")) |>
  mutate(main_site = factor(main_site, levels = names(ov_site_colours)))
# clean-up: (1) where a site group's "vs all" and "vs the same site" points nearly coincide (within 0.1), keep
# only the within-site one (the fairer comparison); (2) drop points with no p < 0.05 in any of their four tests
# (conditions left with no point drop out; the per-condition similarity figure above shows them all)
ov <- ov |>
  mutate(twin_d = {
    w <- sqrt(outer(px, px, "-")^2 + outer(py, py, "-")^2)
    same <- outer(paste(Condition, site), paste(Condition, site), "==") & outer(kind, kind, "!=") & kind != "all"
    w[!same] <- Inf
    apply(w, 1, min)
  }) |>
  filter(!(kind == "site_all" & twin_d < 0.1)) |>
  filter(pmin(p_inc_same, p_inc_opp, p_dec_same, p_dec_opp, na.rm = TRUE) < 0.05) |>
  # site points carry the condition's name too; without its all-units point, the condition's first site point is
  # drawn as its main label (plain, not italic)
  mutate(named = kind == "all" | (!any(kind == "all") & row_number() == which.max(kind == "site_all")),
         label = ifelse(kind != "all", paste0(ov_abbrev(Condition), " ", label), label), .by = Condition) |>
  mutate(kind = factor(kind, levels = c("all", "site_all", "site"))) |>
  arrange(Condition, kind) |>
  mutate(kind = as.character(kind))
# conditions with two or more points (joined by arrows) get their own filled shape (square, diamond, triangles),
# others a circle
split_conditions <- ov |> count(Condition) |> filter(n >= 2) |> pull(Condition)
# (the shapes of the direction summary, where the condition has one there)
ov_shapes <- split_shapes[names(split_shapes) %in% split_conditions]
ov_shapes <- c(ov_shapes, setNames(setdiff(c(22, 23, 24, 25), ov_shapes)[seq_along(setdiff(split_conditions, names(ov_shapes)))],
                                   setdiff(split_conditions, names(ov_shapes))))
ov <- mutate(ov, shape = coalesce(unname(split_shapes[Condition]), unname(ov_shapes[Condition]), 21))
# arrows from all of a condition's units to each of its site points; without an all-units point, from the site's
# "vs all" point to its "vs the same site" point
ov_from <- ov |> filter(kind == "all" | (kind == "site_all" & !any(kind == "all")), .by = Condition) |>
  select(Condition, from_kind = kind, from_site = site, x = px, y = py)
ov_arrows <- inner_join(ov_from, select(ov, Condition, kind, site, xend = px, yend = py), by = "Condition",
                        relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(kind != "all", !(kind == from_kind & coalesce(site == from_site, FALSE))) |>
  mutate(d = sqrt((xend - x)^2 + (yend - y)^2)) |>
  filter(d > 0.01) |>
  mutate(gap = pmin(0.025, d * 0.35), x0 = x + (xend - x) * pmin(0.015, d * 0.2) / d,
         y0 = y + (yend - y) * pmin(0.015, d * 0.2) / d,
         x1 = xend - (xend - x) * gap / d, y1 = yend - (yend - y) * gap / d)

# arrows on the 0 lines, pointing outward from the centre, labelled in light grey at their tips (as in the
# direction summary)
ov_h_arrows <- tibble(xend = c(0.49, -0.49), hjust = c(1, 0),
                      label = c("Taxa increased in condition\nresemble perio-increased taxa",
                                "Taxa decreased in condition\nresemble perio-increased taxa"))
ov_v_arrows <- tibble(yend = c(0.405, -0.445), ly = c(0.413, -0.453), vjust = c(0, 1),
                      label = c("Taxa decreased in condition resemble perio-decreased taxa",
                                "Taxa increased in condition resemble perio-decreased taxa"))

# label data: the points, plus unlabelled points along the arrows (so that labels are pushed off them)
ov_labels <- bind_rows(
  ov |> mutate(point_size = 8 * sqrt(units / max(units)),
               text_size = ifelse(named, 3, 2.6), face = ifelse(named, "plain", "italic"),
               text_col = ifelse(named, "grey15", "grey40"),
               # (COVID-19's gut point overlaps UC: its label goes to the left, UC's below; the RA and HNC within-mouth
               # labels go to the right of their points, away from the arrows)
               ny = case_when(py == 0 ~ 0.05, Condition == "COVID-19" & kind != "all" & site == "gastrointestinal" ~ 0,
                              Condition == "COVID-19" ~ -0.02,
                              Condition == "Ulcerative colitis" ~ -0.05,
                              Condition == "Colorectal cancer" & kind == "site" ~ -0.03,
                              .default = 0),
               nx = case_when(Condition == "COVID-19" & kind != "all" & site == "gastrointestinal" ~ -0.14,
                              Condition == "Ulcerative colitis" ~ 0,
                              Condition == "Colorectal cancer" & kind == "site" ~ 0.06,
                              Condition == "Colorectal cancer" & kind == "site_all" ~ 0.09,
                              Condition %in% c("Rheumatoid arthritis", "Head and neck cancer") & kind == "site" ~ 0.1,
                              kind != "all" ~ 0,
                              Condition == "COVID-19" ~ 0.09, Condition == "Head and neck cancer" ~ 0.06,
                              .default = 0)),
  ov_arrows |> mutate(n = pmax(2, ceiling(d / 0.015))) |>
    reframe(t = seq(0.15, 0.85, length.out = n), .by = c(x0, y0, x1, y1, n)) |>
    transmute(px = x0 + (x1 - x0) * t, py = y0 + (y1 - y0) * t, label = "", point_size = 1,
              text_size = 2.6, face = "plain", text_col = "grey40", nx = 0, ny = 0)) |>
  select(px, py, label, point_size, text_size, face, text_col, nx, ny)

p_ov <- ggplot(ov, aes(px, py)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 0.5, ymin = 0, ymax = 0.395, fill = "grey94") +
  # dashed lines, with solid heads at the tips (a dashed arrow draws a broken head)
  geom_segment(data = ov_h_arrows, aes(x = 0, xend = xend, y = 0, yend = 0), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_segment(data = ov_v_arrows, aes(x = 0, xend = 0, y = 0, yend = yend), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_segment(data = ov_h_arrows, aes(x = xend - sign(xend) * 0.0005, xend = xend, y = 0, yend = 0),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey60", arrow = centre_arrow, linejoin = "mitre") +
  geom_segment(data = ov_v_arrows, aes(x = 0, xend = 0, y = yend - sign(yend) * 0.0005, yend = yend),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey60", arrow = centre_arrow, linejoin = "mitre") +
  # (below the line: points on the line, with no decreased signatures to test, get their labels above it)
  geom_text(data = ov_h_arrows, aes(x = xend, y = -0.012, label = label, hjust = hjust), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            vjust = 1, size = 2.7, color = "grey55", lineheight = 0.9) +
  geom_text(data = ov_v_arrows, aes(x = 0, y = ly, label = label, vjust = vjust), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            size = 2.7, color = "grey55") +
  geom_segment(data = ov_arrows, aes(x = x0, y = y0, xend = x1, yend = y1), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               color = "grey35", linewidth = 0.5, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), angle = 25, type = "open")) +
  geom_point(aes(size = units, fill = main_site, shape = shape), color = "grey15", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_point(aes(size = units, shape = shape), color = "grey15", fill = NA) +
  scale_shape_identity() +
  # (text size and face set per label outside aes, so that they do not share the point size scale; unlabelled
  # points along the arrows keep labels off them; a white backing keeps lines from running through the text)
  geom_label_repel(data = ov_labels, aes(label = label, point.size = point_size),
                   size = ov_labels$text_size, fontface = ov_labels$face, color = ov_labels$text_col,
                   fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.75), linewidth = 0, label.padding = unit(0.08, "lines"),
                   seed = 3, min.segment.length = 0, lineheight = 0.9,
                   box.padding = 0.4, point.padding = 0.1, force = 6, force_pull = 0.3,
                   segment.color = "grey50", segment.size = 0.3, max.overlaps = Inf, max.iter = 20000,
                   xlim = c(-0.36, 0.36), ylim = c(-0.42, 0.38), nudge_x = ov_labels$nx, nudge_y = ov_labels$ny) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 8, name = "Study units") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ov_site_colours, name = "Main body site", drop = TRUE,
                    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, size = 4, alpha = 1))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 0.4, 0.2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 0.4, 0.2)) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(-0.5, 0.5), ylim = c(-0.48, 0.44), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Perio-increased consensus\n(increased minus decreased signature similarity)",
       y = "Perio-decreased consensus\n(decreased minus increased signature similarity)") +
  theme(legend.title = element_text(size = 9))
p_ov + theme(legend.justification = c(0, 1))
```

```{r paper-figure-6}
#| include: false
# paper Figure 6: the direction summary (A) and the similarity overview (B) side by side, with a single body site
# legend (B's, which covers every site group in A)
fig7 <- (p_map + guides(fill = "none")) + p_ov +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") & theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20))
ggsave("doc_figures/Figure 6.png", fig7, width = 18, height = 8.8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each point:** a set of BugSigDB study units, placed by the four mean ranks of the per-condition similarity figure above. x = max(0, column 1 − 0.5) − max(0, column 3 − 0.5): the periodontitis-increased consensus compared with the condition's increased and its decreased signatures. y = max(0, column 2 − 0.5) − max(0, column 4 − 0.5): the periodontitis-decreased consensus compared with its decreased and its increased signatures. Ranks below 0.5 count as 0, so a point moves only for signatures more similar than typical.
- **Reading:** right/top: the condition reports the periodontitis-increased/decreased taxa in the periodontitis direction; left/bottom: in the opposite direction (e.g. its increased signatures resemble the taxa depleted in periodontitis). Near 0: neither, or both directions equally. The quadrants match the direction summary: bottom right, both consensus signatures resemble the condition's increased taxa; top left, its decreased taxa.
- **Points:** labelled with a condition alone: all of its units. Labelled with a condition and a site, in the condition's shape (circle for conditions with a single point): the condition's units from that body site group, compared with all other conditions ("RA mouth (vs all)") or only with other conditions' units from that site group ("RA mouth (vs mouth)").
- **Arrows:** drawn for a site set when any of its four mean ranks differs by at least 0.15 from that of all of the condition's units.
- **Left out to reduce clutter:** a site group's comparison with all other conditions when it lies within 0.1 of the within-site comparison of the same studies, and any point with no comparison at unadjusted p < 0.05 (e.g. all of rheumatoid arthritis' units). A condition whose all-units point is left out this way is shown by its significant site points instead (rheumatoid arthritis: its mouth studies; autism spectrum disorder, schizophrenia, type 1 diabetes and unipolar depression: their gut studies compared with other gut studies). All points are in the per-condition similarity figure above.
- **Rank:** the share of other conditions' study units of the same direction (and site group, for "vs" sets) that the unit is more similar than, ties counting half. The mean over a set's units equals the Mann–Whitney U statistic divided by the product of the two group sizes.
- **Colour:** the body site group of at least two thirds of the set's study units, counting both directions (all of colorectal cancer: 88% gut; its mouth studies: mouth; Alzheimer's disease: 68% gut); grey when no site group reaches two thirds (COVID-19 45% gut, rheumatoid arthritis 61% mouth).
- **Watch out:** the comparisons are relative to the background, so a site set compared with all of BugSigDB (mostly gut studies) can look periodontitis-like because of its site alone (mouth and airway studies share oral taxa). Compare its point with the "vs" point of the same site, where there is one.
:::

### Species behind the genera shared with colorectal cancer

Colorectal cancer reports ten of the periodontitis-increased genera increased (direction summary above). Agreement at genus level does not mean the same organisms: a genus can be increased in both through different species. This figure compares the species each database names within those ten genera.

```{r crc-genus-species}
#| fig-width: 9.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| fig-cap: "Which species carry the genera increased in both periodontitis and colorectal cancer. Genera: the periodontitis-increased genera of the heatmaps that at least two thirds of the colorectal cancer study units reporting them (at least 3) report increased, as in the direction summary. Bars: the species named in increased reports within each genus, as shares of those reports: PerioSigDB signatures (left) and BugSigDB colorectal cancer study units (middle); the number of reports is at the right of each bar. Colour: periodontitis's three most reported species of the genus (each with at least 10% of its reports and 2 signatures), the same species in both bars; grey: any other species. A colorectal cancer bar in grey therefore names species that periodontitis studies do not. Right: overlap of the two species mixes (sum over species of the smaller share; 100% = same mix, 0% = no species in common). Genera ordered by overlap. Reports naming only the genus, or an unnamed species (sp., oral taxon, uncultured), are left out."
# the genera increased in periodontitis that colorectal cancer also reports increased (by at least two thirds
# of the >= 3 study units reporting them), as in the direction summary
crc_genera <- genus_agreement |>
  filter(Condition == "Colorectal cancer", perio == "increased", n >= 3, same / n >= 2/3) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  pull(taxon)
# entries named at genus or species rank within some genera; unnamed placeholders (sp., oral taxon, uncultured)
# are left out
named_entries <- \(names, genera) tibble(i = rep(seq_along(names), lengths(names)), name = unlist(names)) |>
  mutate(genus = ifelse(grepl("g__", name), sub("^.*g__([^|]+).*$", "\\1", name), NA),
         species = ifelse(grepl("[|]s__", name), gsub("_", " ", sub("^.*s__([^|]+).*$", "\\1", name)), NA)) |>
  filter(genus %in% genera, !grepl("[|]t__", name),
         is.na(species) | !grepl(" sp[.]| oral |uncultured|genomosp", species)) |>
  mutate(label = coalesce(species, "(genus level)"))
# PerioSigDB signatures and colorectal cancer study units naming each taxon, by direction
crc_units <- filter(bsdb_cc_sigs, Condition == "Colorectal cancer")
crc_species <- bind_rows(
  named_entries(dat$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, crc_genera) |>
    transmute(source = "PerioSigDB signatures", id = i, direction = dat$`Abundance in Group 1`[i], genus, label),
  named_entries(bsdb_cc$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`[crc_units$sig], crc_genera) |>
    transmute(source = "Colorectal cancer study units (BugSigDB)", id = crc_units$unit[i],
              direction = crc_units$direction[i], genus, label)) |>
  distinct() |>
  count(source, genus, label, direction)
# species-level reports in the shared (increased) direction, as shares within each genus and source
crc_mix <- crc_species |>
  filter(direction == "increased", label != "(genus level)") |>
  mutate(source = ifelse(source == "PerioSigDB signatures", "perio", "crc")) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n), total = sum(n), .by = c(source, genus))
# overlap of the two species distributions: sum over species of the smaller share (1 = same mix, 0 = no species shared)
crc_overlap <- crc_mix |>
  select(genus, label, source, share) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = share, values_fill = 0) |>
  summarise(overlap = sum(pmin(perio, crc)), .by = genus)
# colour: periodontitis's three most reported species of each genus; every other species is grey
crc_top <- crc_mix |>
  filter(source == "perio") |>
  arrange(desc(n), label) |>
  mutate(top = row_number(), .by = genus) |>
  filter(top <= 3, share >= 0.1, n >= 2) |>
  select(genus, label, top)
genus_order <- crc_overlap |> arrange(overlap) |> pull(genus)
mix_plot <- crc_mix |>
  left_join(crc_top, by = c("genus", "label")) |>
  mutate(tone = ifelse(is.na(top), "other", paste0("top", top)),
         source = factor(source, levels = c("perio", "crc"),
                         labels = c("PerioSigDB signatures", "Colorectal cancer study units")),
         genus = factor(genus, levels = genus_order),
         epithet = sub("^\\S+ ", "", label)) |>
  # segments: periodontitis's top species first, in order, then the rest by size
  arrange(genus, source, tone == "other", top, desc(n)) |>
  mutate(end = cumsum(share), start = end - share, .by = c(genus, source))
tones <- c(top1 = "#b5401a", top2 = "#e8703f", top3 = "#f4b08f", other = "grey72")
p_mix <- ggplot(mix_plot, aes(y = genus)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = as.integer(genus) - 0.38, ymax = as.integer(genus) + 0.38,
                fill = tone), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  # species names inside segments wide enough to hold them
  geom_text(data = \(d) filter(d, share >= 0.16), aes(x = (start + end) / 2, label = epithet,
                                                      colour = tone %in% c("top1", "top2")),
            size = 2.6, fontface = "italic") +
  geom_text(data = \(d) distinct(d, genus, source, total), aes(x = 1.02, label = total),
            hjust = 0, size = 2.6, colour = "grey35") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tones, breaks = c("top1", "top2", "top3", "other"),
                    labels = c("Periodontitis's main species", "2nd", "3rd", "Other species"),
                    name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey15"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), expand = expansion(add = c(0, 0.08))) +
  facet_wrap(~source) +
  labs(x = "Share of species-level reports (increased); right: number of reports", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"), panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "top",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
p_overlap <- crc_overlap |>
  mutate(genus = factor(genus, levels = genus_order)) |>
  ggplot(aes(overlap, genus)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = overlap, yend = genus), colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 2, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~"Overlap") +
  labs(x = "Shared species mix", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
p_mix + p_overlap + plot_layout(widths = c(4, 1))
```

```{r crc-genus-species-values}
# colorectal cancer reports, classed by the PerioSigDB direction of the taxon they name
crc_perio_side <- crc_species |>
  filter(source == "PerioSigDB signatures") |>
  summarise(p_inc = sum(n[direction == "increased"]), p_dec = sum(n[direction == "decreased"]), .by = c(genus, label))
crc_named <- crc_species |>
  filter(source != "PerioSigDB signatures") |>
  left_join(crc_perio_side, by = c("genus", "label")) |>
  mutate(across(c(p_inc, p_dec), \(x) coalesce(x, 0L)),
         class = case_when(label == "(genus level)" ~ "genus", p_inc > p_dec ~ "perio increased",
                           p_dec > p_inc ~ "perio decreased", p_inc + p_dec == 0 ~ "absent", .default = "split"))
# colorectal cancer reports in one direction, of some classes (all classes if none given)
cn <- \(dir, cls = unique(crc_named$class)) sum(crc_named$n[crc_named$direction == dir & crc_named$class %in% cls])
# reports naming one taxon increased: colorectal cancer study units or PerioSigDB signatures
cu <- \(lab, src = "Colorectal cancer study units (BugSigDB)")
  sum(crc_species$n[crc_species$label == lab & crc_species$source == src & crc_species$direction == "increased"])
ps <- \(lab) cu(lab, "PerioSigDB signatures")
# overlap of a genus's two species mixes, as a percentage
ovl <- \(g) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * crc_overlap$overlap[crc_overlap$genus == g])
# body site group of the colorectal cancer study units naming these genera
crc_sites <- named_entries(bsdb_cc$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`[crc_units$sig], crc_genera) |>
  transmute(unit = crc_units$unit[i], site = crc_units$site_group[i]) |>
  distinct()
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Counting:** a PerioSigDB signature or a colorectal cancer study unit counts once per species and direction; a report naming two species of a genus counts for both. Only increased reports are shown. Decreased reports of these species are rare in both databases (see the text).
- **Colorectal cancer study units:** study × direction × body site group, as in the other BugSigDB figures. Most are gut (stool or tissue); `r sum(crc_sites$site == "oral")` of the `r nrow(crc_sites)` units naming these genera are from the mouth.
- **Names as given:** *F. animalis*, *F. polymorphum* and *F. vincentii* were subspecies of *F. nucleatum* and are kept as named, as is *F. nucleatum* subsp. *nucleatum*.
- **Small numbers:** the colorectal cancer bars rest on `r min(crc_mix$total[crc_mix$source == "crc"])`–`r max(crc_mix$total[crc_mix$source == "crc"])` reports, and *Mogibacterium*'s on one, so its 0% overlap means little. No test.
- **Overlap:** 1 minus the Bray–Curtis dissimilarity of the two species mixes. It is 100% when both name the same single species (*Parvimonas*), whatever the numbers.
:::

**Shows:** colorectal cancer studies mostly name these genera without a species: `r cn("increased", "genus")` of their `r cn("increased")` increased reports. Where they name a species, it is usually one PerioSigDB reports increased (`r cn("increased", "perio increased")` of `r cn("increased") - cn("increased", "genus")`): the species it names most are *F. nucleatum* (`r cu("Fusobacterium nucleatum")` study units; `r ps("Fusobacterium nucleatum")` PerioSigDB signatures increased), *Parvimonas micra* (`r cu("Parvimonas micra")`; `r ps("Parvimonas micra")`), *Peptostreptococcus stomatis* (`r cu("Peptostreptococcus stomatis")`; `r ps("Peptostreptococcus stomatis")`) and *Prevotella intermedia* (`r cu("Prevotella intermedia")`; `r ps("Prevotella intermedia")`). No species that PerioSigDB reports increased is reported decreased by more than one colorectal cancer study unit.

The species mixes match closely for *Parvimonas* (`r ovl("Parvimonas")` overlap), *Prevotella* (`r ovl("Prevotella")`) and *Peptostreptococcus* (`r ovl("Peptostreptococcus")`), and least for *Porphyromonas* (`r ovl("Porphyromonas")`) and *Aggregatibacter* (`r ovl("Aggregatibacter")`), which agree only at genus level. *Porphyromonas* in periodontitis is *P. gingivalis* (`r ps("Porphyromonas gingivalis")` signatures) and *P. endodontalis* (`r ps("Porphyromonas endodontalis")`); colorectal cancer studies name *P. asaccharolytica* (`r cu("Porphyromonas asaccharolytica")`) and *P. uenonis* (`r cu("Porphyromonas uenonis")`) at least as often as *P. gingivalis* (`r cu("Porphyromonas gingivalis")`), and PerioSigDB names each in one signature. *Aggregatibacter* in periodontitis is *A. actinomycetemcomitans* (`r ps("Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans")` signatures increased); no colorectal cancer study names it. *Peptostreptococcus anaerobius* (`r cu("Peptostreptococcus anaerobius")` colorectal cancer study units) and the gut *Campylobacter* species (*C. hominis*, *C. jejuni*, *C. ureolyticus*) are likewise colorectal cancer's own.

As far as the named species show, the overlap between the two conditions rests on a handful of oral species, led by *F. nucleatum*, *P. micra*, *P. stomatis* and *P. intermedia*, not on every shared genus.

### Exact taxon overlap and taxonomic similarity between periodontitis and colorectal cancer

Colorectal cancer's consensus signatures, built as for PerioSigDB, compared taxon by taxon with both PerioSigDB consensus signatures. Most cells show taxonomic relatives rather than exact matches.

```{r bsdb-crc-consensus}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 10.5
#| fig-cap: "Lin similarity (higher = more closely related; 1 = same taxon, outlined) between the PerioSigDB consensus taxa (rows; red: increased, blue: decreased in periodontitis; binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures, unadjusted p < 0.05) and the colorectal cancer consensus taxa (binomial test of increased vs decreased studies, unadjusted p < 0.05) (columns). Brackets: PerioSigDB signatures (rows) or colorectal cancer studies (columns) reporting the taxon increased / decreased. The top-left and bottom-right blocks are the same direction as periodontitis. Rows: ordered by NCBI taxonomic lineage within each direction. Top strip: similarity of the column taxon's best match among the periodontitis-increased taxa minus that among the periodontitis-decreased taxa (red: more like increased, blue: more like decreased; full colour at a difference of 0.7 or more). Columns: grouped by family; families ordered by their mean difference and taxa within a family by their own, red to blue for colorectal cancer's increased taxa and blue to red for its decreased taxa."

terminal_id <- function(x) paste0("NCBITaxon:", unique(sub("^.*[|]", "", x)))

perio_consensus <- tibble(
  id = unlist(semsim$consensus),
  perio_direction = rep(names(semsim$consensus), lengths(semsim$consensus))
) |>
  left_join(select(semsim$taxon_tests, id = ids, perio_up = increased, perio_down = decreased), by = "id") |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", taxon_sim$names[id], perio_up, perio_down))

crc_consensus <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  filter(Condition == "Colorectal cancer") |>
  mutate(taxon = map(bsdb_cc$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`[sig], terminal_id)) |>
  unnest(taxon) |>
  distinct(Study, direction, taxon) |>
  count(taxon, direction) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    n = increased + decreased,
    p = map2_dbl(increased, n, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
    direction = ifelse(increased > decreased, "increased", "decreased")
  ) |>
  filter(p < 0.05, taxon %in% rownames(taxon_sim$sim)) |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", sub(" <[^>]+>", "", taxon_sim$names[taxon]), increased, decreased))

# taxa reported by at least min_studies of a condition's studies, at least min_share of them in one direction
consistent_taxa <- function(cond, min_studies = 3, min_share = 0.75) {
  bsdb_cc_sigs |>
    filter(Condition == cond) |>
    mutate(taxon = map(bsdb_cc$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`[sig], terminal_id)) |>
    unnest(taxon) |>
    distinct(Study, direction, taxon) |>
    count(taxon, direction) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
    (\(x) mutate(x, increased = if ("increased" %in% names(x)) increased else 0L,
                  decreased = if ("decreased" %in% names(x)) decreased else 0L))() |>
    mutate(n = increased + decreased, direction = ifelse(increased > decreased, "increased", "decreased")) |>
    filter(n >= min_studies, pmax(increased, decreased) / n >= min_share, taxon %in% rownames(taxon_sim$sim)) |>
    mutate(label = sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", sub(" <[^>]+>", "", taxon_sim$names[taxon]), increased, decreased))
}

# heatmap of Lin similarity: PerioSigDB consensus taxa (rows) vs a condition's taxa (columns), with a
# strip showing the difference between each column taxon's best match among the periodontitis-
# increased and the periodontitis-decreased taxa (red: more like increased, blue: more like decreased,
# pale: like both or neither); within each block, columns are grouped by family (keeping relatives
# together), families ordered by their mean difference and taxa within a family by their own, red to
# blue for the condition's increased taxa and blue to red for its decreased taxa
taxon_family <- function(ids) {
  map_chr(strsplit(taxon_sim$lineage[ids], "|", fixed = TRUE), \(l) {
    fam <- grep("aceae$", l, value = TRUE)
    if (length(fam)) fam[1] else tail(l, 1)
  })
}
order_block <- function(ids, weights) {
  tibble(id = ids, w = weights, family = taxon_family(ids)) |>
    mutate(family_w = mean(w), .by = family) |>
    arrange(family_w, family, w) |>
    pull(id)
}
both_directions_heatmap <- function(cond, taxa) {
  shade <- \(x, col) rgb(colorRamp(c("#f7f3f1", col))(pmin(x, 1)), maxColorValue = 255)
  legend_sims <- c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1)
  taxa <- taxa |>
    left_join(select(taxon_sim$closest, taxon, sim_up, sim_down), by = "taxon") |>
    mutate(difference = sim_up - sim_down)
  up <- filter(taxa, direction == "increased")
  down <- filter(taxa, direction == "decreased")
  taxa <- taxa[match(c(order_block(up$taxon, -up$difference), order_block(down$taxon, down$difference)), taxa$taxon), ]
  row_levels <- c("Difference", rev(perio_consensus$label[order(perio_consensus$perio_direction != "increased",
                                                               taxon_sim$lineage[perio_consensus$id])]))
  cells <- tidyr::expand_grid(select(perio_consensus, id, perio_direction, row = label),
                              select(taxa, taxon, direction, col = label)) |>
    mutate(sim = taxon_sim$sim[cbind(taxon, id)],
           fill = ifelse(perio_direction == "increased", shade(sim, "#c0392b"), shade(sim, "#1c5cab")))
  strip <- taxa |>
    transmute(taxon, direction, col = label, perio_direction = "difference", row = "Difference", sim = NA,
              fill = ifelse(difference > 0, shade(pmax(difference, 0) / 0.7, "#c0392b"),
                            shade(pmax(-difference, 0) / 0.7, "#1c5cab")))
  bind_rows(cells, strip) |>
    mutate(
      row = factor(row, levels = rev(row_levels)),
      col = factor(col, levels = taxa$label),
      perio_direction = factor(c(difference = " ", increased = "Periodontitis increased",
                                 decreased = "Periodontitis decreased")[perio_direction],
                               levels = c(" ", "Periodontitis increased", "Periodontitis decreased")),
      direction = factor(paste(cond, direction), levels = paste(cond, c("increased", "decreased")))
    ) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = col, y = row, fill = fill)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_tile(data = \(d) filter(d, !is.na(sim), sim > 0.999), color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.9, fill = NA) +
    # legend: the red scale (blue rows use the same scale); invisible tiles put every legend value in the data
    geom_tile(data = \(d) mutate(d[rep(1, length(legend_sims)), ], fill = shade(legend_sims, "#c0392b")), alpha = 0) +
    scale_fill_identity(guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1)), breaks = shade(legend_sims, "#c0392b"),
                        labels = legend_sims, name = "Lin similarity\n(blue rows:\nsame scale)") +
    facet_grid(perio_direction ~ direction, scales = "free", space = "free", labeller = label_wrap_gen(16)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 50, hjust = 1, face = "italic"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"),
          panel.grid = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
          legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9))
}

both_directions_heatmap("Colorectal cancer", crc_consensus)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each cell**: Lin similarity on the NCBI taxonomy between one PerioSigDB consensus taxon (row) and one colorectal cancer consensus taxon (column): 2 × information content of their closest shared ancestor ÷ (information content of the first + of the second), where a taxon's information content is higher the fewer descendants it has. 1 = same taxon (outlined); taxa in different phyla score about 0.1–0.2. Blue rows use the same scale as red rows.
- **PerioSigDB taxa (44 rows)**: every taxon, at the rank the paper reported it, that more PerioSigDB signatures report in one direction than the other (two-sided exact binomial test against 50%, unadjusted p < 0.05; 44 of 669 taxa tested, 22 of them also pass FDR). 32 increased, 12 decreased. A taxon needs at least 6 reports, all in one direction, to reach p < 0.05.
- **Ranks are not merged**: a genus and its species are separate rows/columns (e.g. *Treponema* (9/0) and *T. denticola* (44/0); colorectal cancer *Fusobacterium* (21/3) and *F. nucleatum* (8/0)). A study reporting only *F. nucleatum* does not count towards *Fusobacterium*.
- **Brackets**: rows count PerioSigDB *signatures* (187 signatures from 119 studies, so a study can count more than once); columns count colorectal cancer *studies* (each counted once per direction; a study can count in both directions).
- **Colorectal cancer taxa (15 columns)**: the same binomial rule applied to colorectal cancer studies in the filtered BugSigDB (human disease-vs-control, no meta-analyses; labels merged into colorectal cancer). Studies from all body sites are included, but nearly all are stool or gut tissue (79 of 88 increased and 68 of 74 decreased signatures are gastrointestinal). 595 taxa were tested, uncorrected. 11 columns are increased, 4 decreased.
- **Top strip**: for each column, (similarity to its closest periodontitis-increased taxon) − (to its closest periodontitis-decreased taxon). Full colour at ±0.7 or beyond; pale = equally close to both, or to neither.
- **Example (exact match)**: *F. nucleatum* row × *F. nucleatum* column = 1, outlined. Its strip value is 1 − 0.15 (its closest decreased taxon is *Haemophilus*) = 0.85, full red.
- **Example (relative)**: *F. nucleatum* row × *Fusobacterium* column = 0.88 (species vs its own genus). *Porphyromonas* column: 0.89 with *P. gingivalis* and 0.80 with *P. endodontalis*; *Parvimonas* column: 0.92 with *P. micra* (strip 0.63, slightly paler than full red).
- **Example (opposite direction)**: *Gemella* (increased in 9/0 colorectal cancer studies, 7 of them gut) is closest to the periodontitis-*decreased* *G. haemolysans* (0.88) and only 0.31 to its best increased match (*Peptostreptococcus*), so its strip is −0.57 (blue).
- **Example (distant)**: *Faecalibacterium* (1/11, decreased) is closest to *Peptostreptococcus* (0.51) and to *S. sanguinis* among decreased taxa (0.31), so its strip is a faint red (+0.20): it leans towards the periodontitis-increased Clostridia, but neither match is close.
- **Ordering**: rows are sorted by their full NCBI lineage text within each direction, which keeps relatives together but is not a phylogenetic tree. Columns are grouped by family, the first lineage name ending in "-aceae" (or the taxon itself if there is none, e.g. Enterobacteriaceae, Porphyromonadaceae).
- **No test** compares the two consensus sets here; the figure is descriptive. The block-level tests are in the whole-signature similarity section.
- **Watch out**: a taxon reported at a different rank in the two databases appears as a close relative (about 0.8–0.9), not an exact match. Lin similarity depends on how many descendants NCBI lists for each node, so equal values do not mean equal evolutionary distance.
:::

Four taxa are shared exactly (*F. nucleatum*, *Peptostreptococcus*, *P. stomatis*, *P. micra*) and several more are close relatives (e.g. *Porphyromonas*, *Fusobacterium*, *Parvimonas*); *Treponema*, *Tannerella*, *Fretibacterium* and *Desulfobulbus* have no close counterpart. *Gemella*, increased in colorectal cancer, is closest to the periodontitis-*decreased* *G. haemolysans*, the opposite direction. The colorectal cancer decreased consensus (butyrate producers such as *Faecalibacterium*, *Roseburia* and *Lachnospira*) is only distantly related to periodontitis taxa: the strip marks it as closer to the periodontitis-increased Clostridia, but at low similarity.

### Exact taxon overlap and taxonomic similarity between periodontitis, head and neck cancer and smoking

Head and neck cancer and smoking are the conditions whose genera are reported most often in the same directions as periodontitis (see the direction summary above). With 15–16 studies each, no taxon reaches even unadjusted p < 0.05 in a binomial test, so here they are shown with descriptive taxon sets selected by a relaxed rule, which are not equivalent to the consensus signatures.


```{r bsdb-hnc-heatmap}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-cap: "Lin similarity (higher = more closely related; 1 = same taxon, outlined) between the PerioSigDB consensus taxa (rows; red: increased, blue: decreased in periodontitis; binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures, unadjusted p < 0.05) and the taxa reported by at least 3 head and neck cancer studies with at least 75% of them in one direction (descriptive taxon set, no statistical test) (columns). Brackets: PerioSigDB signatures (rows) or head and neck cancer studies (columns) reporting the taxon increased / decreased. The top-left and bottom-right blocks are the same direction as periodontitis. Rows: ordered by NCBI taxonomic lineage within each direction. Top strip: similarity of the column taxon's best match among the periodontitis-increased taxa minus that among the periodontitis-decreased taxa (red: more like increased, blue: more like decreased; full colour at a difference of 0.7 or more). Columns: grouped by family; families ordered by their mean difference and taxa within a family by their own, red to blue for head and neck cancer's increased taxa and blue to red for its decreased taxa."
both_directions_heatmap("Head and neck cancer", consistent_taxa("Head and neck cancer"))
```

```{r bsdb-smoking-heatmap}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 10
#| fig-cap: "Lin similarity (higher = more closely related; 1 = same taxon, outlined) between the PerioSigDB consensus taxa (rows; red: increased, blue: decreased in periodontitis; binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures, unadjusted p < 0.05) and the taxa reported by at least 3 smoking studies with at least 75% of them in one direction (descriptive taxon set, no statistical test) (columns). Brackets: PerioSigDB signatures (rows) or smoking studies (columns) reporting the taxon increased / decreased. The top-left and bottom-right blocks are the same direction as periodontitis. Rows: ordered by NCBI taxonomic lineage within each direction. Top strip: similarity of the column taxon's best match among the periodontitis-increased taxa minus that among the periodontitis-decreased taxa (red: more like increased, blue: more like decreased; full colour at a difference of 0.7 or more). Columns: grouped by family; families ordered by their mean difference and taxa within a family by their own, red to blue for smoking's increased taxa and blue to red for its decreased taxa."
both_directions_heatmap("Smoking behavior", consistent_taxa("Smoking behavior"))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Same layout as the colorectal cancer heatmap**: rows are the same 44 PerioSigDB consensus taxa, cells are Lin similarities, outlines mark the same taxon, and the strip shows best increased match minus best decreased match.
- **Columns are a descriptive set, not a consensus**: a taxon is included if at least 3 of the condition's studies report it (at that exact rank) and at least 75% of them in one direction. There is no test and no multiple-testing control. Head and neck cancer: 10 of 26 taxa reported by ≥3 studies pass. Smoking: 17 of 31.
- **Other data**: filtered BugSigDB (human disease-vs-control, no meta-analyses). Head and neck cancer merges oral, pharyngeal and laryngeal cancer labels (15 studies). Smoking is BugSigDB's "Smoking behavior" (16 studies). Both are mostly oral samples (signatures: head and neck cancer 38 oral, 4 gastrointestinal, 2 upper airway; smoking 35 oral, 4 gastrointestinal, 8 upper airway).
- **Brackets**: columns count studies reporting the taxon increased / decreased (each study once per direction); rows count PerioSigDB signatures.
- **Example (head and neck cancer)**: *Haemophilus* (1/5, decreased) exactly matches the periodontitis-decreased *Haemophilus* row (1, outlined) but is also 0.76 to the periodontitis-increased *A. actinomycetemcomitans* (same family), so its strip is only −0.24. *Rothia* (0/5) is 0.83 to *R. aeria*, strip −0.59.
- **Example (opposite direction)**: head and neck cancer *Porphyromonas* (0/3) and *Leptotrichia* (0/3) are decreased but closest to periodontitis-increased taxa (*P. gingivalis* 0.89; *F. nucleatum* 0.78), so they are red strips in the decreased block. Smoking *Peptostreptococcus* (1/4) is decreased but identical to the periodontitis-increased *Peptostreptococcus* row (strip 0.70).
- **Example (genus vs species)**: head and neck cancer *Streptococcus* (1/4) is 0.71 to *S. sanguinis* (decreased) and only 0.39 to its best increased match (*Peptostreptococcus*), so its strip is −0.32 (blue).
- **Higher ranks appear too**: the smoking set includes the phylum Pseudomonadota (1/4) and the class Fusobacteriia (3/1), which have only moderate similarity to any species.
- **Watch out**: only 3–8 studies support each column, so one study changes the share by 12–33 points; the 75% cut-off is arbitrary. Studies reporting a species (e.g. *F. nucleatum*) do not count towards its genus column.
:::

**Shows:** both conditions match periodontitis mainly in the periodontitis-decreased taxa. Head and neck cancer reports *Haemophilus*, *Neisseria*, *Rothia* and *Corynebacterium* decreased, the same genera as or relatives of the periodontitis-decreased taxa, and *Fusobacterium*, *Parvimonas* and *Selenomonas* increased. *Porphyromonas* and *Leptotrichia* (a relative of *Fusobacterium*) were reported in the opposite direction. *Streptococcus*, also reported decreased, is closest to the periodontitis-decreased *S. sanguinis*, now the consensus's only *Streptococcus* species. *Haemophilus* also resembles the periodontitis-increased *Aggregatibacter* (same family), though its exact match is the periodontitis-decreased *Haemophilus*. Smoking reports *Haemophilus*, *Neisseria*, *Corynebacterium* and *Granulicatella* decreased and *Treponema*, *Fusobacterium* and *Prevotella* increased, but also *Peptostreptococcus*, *Selenomonas* and *Aggregatibacter* decreased, the opposite of periodontitis. Each taxon in these descriptive sets is supported by 3–6 (head and neck cancer) or 3–8 (smoking) studies, so they are less certain than the colorectal cancer consensus.

### Are periodontitis-associated genera differentially abundant in colorectal cancer stool datasets?

Everything above compares published signatures. The BugSigDB paper also tested signatures directly on participant-level data: ten colorectal cancer stool metagenome datasets from curatedMetagenomicData, ranking every BugSigDB signature by how strongly its genera differ between cancer and control samples (Geistlinger et al. 2024, Figure 3). The same is done here with the PerioSigDB consensus signatures added, against two colorectal cancer meta-analysis signatures (Wirbel et al. 2019 and Thomas et al. 2019) as positive controls. Those meta-analyses used several of the same datasets, so they are expected to rank near the top.

**How to read the first figure.** Each dataset is analysed separately. Within a dataset, every genus is tested for a difference between cancer and control stool samples, and then about 2,000 BugSigDB signatures are ranked by how strongly their genera, as a set, differ. Each point shows where one signature ranks in one dataset, as a top percentage: 1% means only 1 in 100 BugSigDB signatures is more strongly associated with cancer in that dataset.

- **If the answer is yes**, the red points (periodontitis-increased signature) sit at the left, in the shaded top 5%, close to the grey colorectal cancer signatures (the positive controls), in most datasets. Filled points pass FDR < 0.05.
- **If the answer is no**, the red points are scattered around the dashed line at 50%, where a typical, unrelated signature would rank.
- **Uninformative rows:** in some datasets even the positive controls rank low. In over-representation analysis, a dataset with no genus differing at FDR < 0.05 puts every signature at 100%.

These tests ask whether a signature's genera differ between cancer and controls, not in which direction. Direction is shown in the second figure.

```{r crc-enrichment}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "How highly the periodontitis signatures rank for association with colorectal cancer in each dataset, compared with about 1,600–2,100 BugSigDB signatures (those with at least 5 genera present in the dataset). Red: periodontitis-increased signature; blue: periodontitis-decreased signature; grey: colorectal cancer meta-analysis signatures as positive controls (Wirbel 2019, circle; Thomas 2019, triangle). Left of the axis is stronger association; shaded: top 5%; dashed line: 50%, a typical signature. Filled: FDR < 0.05 across all signatures in that dataset and method. Rows: datasets with their cancer / control samples, largest at top. Genera are tested for differential abundance between cancer and control samples with limma-trend on log counts per million. Over-representation analysis: hypergeometric test of the share of the signature's genera that differ at FDR < 0.05 (ties ranked last). PADOG: gene set test that down-weights genera shared by many signatures (1,000 sample-label permutations)."
# precomputed by scripts/crc_bugset_enrichment.R
crc_enrichment <- readRDS("../../output/crc_bugset_enrichment.rds")

crc_datasets <- crc_enrichment$datasets |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", dataset, n_crc, n_control)) |>
  arrange(n_crc + n_control)

crc_enrichment$ranks |>
  left_join(select(crc_datasets, dataset, ds = label), by = "dataset") |>
  mutate(ds = factor(ds, levels = crc_datasets$label),
         method = factor(toupper(method), levels = c("ORA", "PADOG"),
                         labels = c("Over-representation analysis", "PADOG")),
         signature = factor(label, levels = c("PerioSigDB_consensus_increased", "PerioSigDB_consensus_decreased",
                                              "Wirbel2019", "Thomas2019"),
                            labels = c("Periodontitis increased", "Periodontitis decreased",
                                       "Wirbel 2019 (colorectal cancer)", "Thomas 2019 (colorectal cancer)")),
         significant = fdr < 0.05) |>
  ggplot(aes(percentile, ds)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.1, xmax = 5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#fbe9e4") +
  annotate("text", x = 5, y = Inf, label = "top 5%", hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.3, size = 3, color = "#c0392b") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = 50, y = Inf, label = "typical", hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.3, size = 3, color = "grey40") +
  # lines between datasets, so each dataset's points are grouped together
  geom_hline(yintercept = seq_len(nrow(crc_datasets) - 1) + 0.5, color = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(color = signature, shape = signature, fill = ifelse(significant, as.character(signature), NA)),
             size = 2.8, stroke = 0.9, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 1, 10, 100), labels = c("0.1%", "1%", "10%", "100%")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Periodontitis increased" = "#c0392b", "Periodontitis decreased" = "#1c5cab",
                                "Wirbel 2019 (colorectal cancer)" = "grey35", "Thomas 2019 (colorectal cancer)" = "grey35"),
                     name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 21, 21, 24), name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Periodontitis increased" = "#c0392b", "Periodontitis decreased" = "#1c5cab",
                               "Wirbel 2019 (colorectal cancer)" = "grey35", "Thomas 2019 (colorectal cancer)" = "grey35"),
                    na.value = "white", guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~method) +
  labs(x = "Rank among BugSigDB signatures (top %, log scale)\n← more strongly associated with colorectal cancer", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each point**: one signature's rank in one dataset and method, as rank ÷ number of signatures tested × 100. Ties are given the worst rank. Lower is more strongly associated. The x axis is log scale.
- **PerioSigDB signatures tested**: the genera of the consensus taxa, not the top-20 genus lists. Species are collapsed to their genus; taxa with no genus in their MetaPhlAn lineage (the three "oral taxon" placeholders and the *[Eubacterium]* species) drop out. Increased: 16 genera (*Aggregatibacter* … *Treponema*). Decreased: 9 genera.
- **Comparison pool**: every BugSigDB signature except periodontitis signatures, from any host, study design or contrast, converted to genus. A signature needs ≥5 genera overall and ≥5 detected in the dataset (sets of more than 500 are dropped), giving 1,598–2,088 signatures per dataset. The pool includes the original signatures of some of these cohorts (e.g. Zeller 2014, Feng 2015) and non-disease contrasts (e.g. air pollution).
- **Positive controls**: BugSigDB signatures from the Wirbel 2019 (14–17 genera in a dataset) and Thomas 2019 (21–30) meta-analyses, ranked within the same pool.
- **Datasets**: the 10 curatedMetagenomicData stool studies with colorectal cancer cases (ThomasAM_2019_c excluded because it overlaps YachidaS_2019). Only cancer vs control samples are used (adenomas dropped), one sample per participant. Species counts (relative abundance × reads) are summed to genus.
- **Per-genus test**: limma-trend on log2 counts per million (prior count 3), cancer vs control, BH across the genera in the dataset.
- **Over-representation analysis**: one-sided hypergeometric test of how many of the signature's genera are among the dataset's FDR < 0.05 genera, against all detected genera. **Direction-agnostic**: a genus counts whether it is higher or lower in cancer.
- **PADOG**: a direction-agnostic set test on absolute moderated t, down-weighting genera that appear in many signatures, with p from 1,000 permutations of the cancer/control labels.
- **Filled**: BH FDR < 0.05 across all signatures in that dataset × method. There is no correction across datasets or methods.
- **Example (filled)**: in YachidaS_2019 (258/251), over-representation analysis: 8 of the periodontitis-increased signature's 15 detected genera differ at FDR < 0.05, against 16 of all 218 genera in the dataset. p = 6.5 × 10⁻⁷, rank 7 of 2,088 = 0.34%, FDR = 0.0002.
- **Example (filled, few hits)**: in ZellerG_2014, only 3 genera differ at all (*Fusobacterium*, *Peptostreptococcus*, *Porphyromonas*), and all 3 are in the periodontitis-increased signature: rank 37 of 2,073 = 1.8%, FDR = 0.016. Smaller sets containing 2–3 of those genera rank above it.
- **Example (unfilled)**: with PADOG in YachidaS_2019, the periodontitis-increased signature has p = 0.001, rank 26 of 2,088 = 1.25%, but FDR = 0.08. No periodontitis signature passes FDR with PADOG.
- **Uninformative rows**: HanniganGD_2017 and ThomasAM_2018a have 0 FDR < 0.05 genera, so over-representation analysis gives every signature p = 1 and ranks them all at 100%. VogtmannE_2016 has 1 such genus; ThomasAM_2018b and ZellerG_2014 have 3.
- **Watch out**: a signature can rank high because its genera are *lower* in cancer; use the next figure for direction. The ranks are not independent of the meta-analysis controls, which share *Fusobacterium*, *Parvimonas*, *Peptostreptococcus* and *Porphyromonas*.
:::

```{r crc-enrichment-genera}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Difference in each genus of the PerioSigDB consensus signatures between colorectal cancer and control stool samples in each curatedMetagenomicData colorectal cancer dataset (columns, with cancer / control samples, ordered by sample size, largest at right). Cells: log2 fold change (red: higher in cancer; blue: lower), from limma-trend on log counts per million. Outlined: FDR < 0.05 across all genera in the dataset. Rows: genera of the periodontitis-increased (top) and -decreased (bottom) signature, ordered by the number of datasets in which they are higher in cancer at FDR < 0.05. Grey: genus not detected in the dataset."
crc_genera <- crc_enrichment$genera |>
  mutate(signature = factor(signature, levels = c("PerioSigDB_consensus_increased", "PerioSigDB_consensus_decreased"),
                            labels = c("Increased in periodontitis", "Decreased in periodontitis")),
         up = fdr < 0.05 & logFC > 0)
genus_order <- crc_genera |>
  summarise(up = sum(up), lfc = mean(logFC), .by = genus) |>
  arrange(up, lfc) |>
  pull(genus)

crc_genera |>
  tidyr::complete(signature, genus, dataset) |>
  filter(genus %in% crc_genera$genus[crc_genera$signature == signature[1]], .by = signature) |>
  left_join(select(crc_datasets, dataset, ds = label), by = "dataset") |>
  mutate(ds = factor(ds, levels = crc_datasets$label), genus = factor(genus, levels = genus_order)) |>
  ggplot(aes(ds, genus, fill = logFC)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_tile(data = \(d) filter(d, fdr < 0.05), color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.7, width = 0.9, height = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#1c5cab", mid = "#f0efec", high = "#c0392b", midpoint = 0, limits = c(-4, 4),
                       oob = scales::squish, na.value = "grey85", name = "log2 fold change\n(cancer vs control)") +
  facet_grid(signature ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1),
        axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each cell**: limma-trend log2 fold change of one genus, cancer vs control, in one dataset (the same model as the previous figure). Colours saturate at ±4; real values range from −3.6 to 10.3.
- **Outlined**: BH FDR < 0.05 across all genera detected in that dataset, in either direction.
