- **Grey**: genus not detected in any sample of the dataset (e.g. *Tannerella* is missing from 6 of 10 datasets, *Filifactor* from 4).
- **Rows**: the genus-level PerioSigDB consensus signatures used in the enrichment (16 increased, 9 decreased; *Desulfobulbus* is not detected in any dataset, so 15 increased rows are shown). These are not the top-20 genera of the heatmaps.
- **Row order**: by the number of datasets where the genus is higher in cancer at FDR < 0.05, then by mean log2 fold change; most at top. Both panels share this order.
- **Example**: *Peptostreptococcus* is higher in cancer at FDR < 0.05 in 7 of 10 datasets, *Parvimonas* in 6, *Fusobacterium* and *Porphyromonas* in 5. In YachidaS_2019: *Parvimonas* log2FC 2.95, *Peptostreptococcus* 2.51, *Fusobacterium* 3.39, *Porphyromonas* 0.90, all outlined.
- **Periodontitis-decreased genera**: only 3 outlined cells. *Gemella* is higher in cancer in WirbelJ_2018 and YachidaS_2019 (opposite to "decreased"), and *Corynebacterium* is lower in FengQ_2015.
- **Columns**: datasets with cancer / control sample counts, smallest at left; each dataset is analysed separately (no meta-analysis across datasets).
- **Watch out**: fold changes come from compositional (relative abundance) data, so a genus can look higher in cancer partly because others fell. Small fold changes can pass FDR in large datasets (e.g. *Fretibacterium* 0.50 in YachidaS_2019).
:::

```{r crc-enrichment-values}
cr <- crc_enrichment$ranks
top_n_datasets <- \(lab, m, cutoff) sum(cr$percentile[cr$label == lab & cr$method == m] <= cutoff)
fdr_datasets <- \(lab, m) with(filter(cr, label == lab, method == m, fdr < 0.05), paste(dataset, collapse = " and "))
genus_up <- \(g) with(filter(crc_genera, genus == g, signature == "Increased in periodontitis"),
                      sprintf("%d of %d datasets", sum(up), length(up)))
```

**Shows:** the periodontitis-increased signature ranks high for association with colorectal cancer in participant-level stool data, though the support varies by dataset and method. It ranks in the top 5% of all BugSigDB signatures in `r top_n_datasets("PerioSigDB_consensus_increased", "ora", 5)` of 10 datasets with over-representation analysis and `r top_n_datasets("PerioSigDB_consensus_increased", "padog", 5)` with PADOG, and passes FDR in `r fdr_datasets("PerioSigDB_consensus_increased", "ora")` (over-representation analysis). With PADOG, few signatures pass FDR: the positive controls do in only `r sum(cr$method == "padog" & cr$role == "positive control" & cr$fdr < 0.05)` of 20 dataset-signature combinations, and no periodontitis signature does. The signal comes mainly from a few genera that generally had higher estimated abundance in cancer, with FDR-significant differences in some datasets: *Peptostreptococcus* (FDR < 0.05 in `r genus_up("Peptostreptococcus")`), *Parvimonas* (`r genus_up("Parvimonas")`), *Fusobacterium* (`r genus_up("Fusobacterium")`) and *Porphyromonas* (`r genus_up("Porphyromonas")`), the same four genera as in the literature-based enrichment heatmaps. The periodontitis-decreased signature is not enriched in any dataset, and its genera are not consistently lower in cancer; *Gemella* is even higher in cancer in two datasets, as in the BugSigDB direction heatmaps. In HanniganGD_2017 and ThomasAM_2018a no genus differs at FDR < 0.05, so over-representation analysis ranks every signature last, and GuptaA_2019 ranks even the positive controls low. The periodontitis-increased signature shares several genera with the two meta-analysis signatures, so part of its ranking reflects the same colorectal cancer genera they contain.

### How consistent are periodontitis signatures across studies?

How well do a condition's signatures from different studies agree with each other? The BugSigDB paper ranked conditions by this (Geistlinger et al. 2024, Figure 2), finding antibiotics and HIV infection the most consistent. Here periodontitis (PerioSigDB) is placed among the BugSigDB conditions. Because oral signatures share many taxa with each other, each condition is compared with random signatures from the same body sites, drawn from all signatures including the condition's own (a label permutation test).

```{r replicability}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| fig-cap: "Agreement between signatures of the same condition from different studies. Point: mean taxonomic similarity between the condition's signatures from different studies (best-match average of Lin similarity; signatures with at least 5 taxa). Each pair of studies counts once. Grey bar and tick: central 95% and mean of the same score for 1,000 random sets of signatures matched to the condition in number, direction and body site group, drawn from the signatures of all other conditions. Rows: the 10 conditions per direction whose score most exceeds the random mean, ordered by that excess, with the number of studies in brackets. Filled: FDR < 0.05, one-sided resampling test with Benjamini–Hochberg correction across all conditions tested in that direction. Green: periodontitis, and its signatures from sequencing (16S and shotgun) or from targeted assays (PCR and checkerboard hybridization) only. Blue: the BugSigDB signatures sampled from dental plaque, pooled across their conditions, whose random sets come from all other oral signatures of the direction. The assay and plaque rows are checks on periodontitis's agreement, ranked by excess like the other rows and filled at unadjusted p < 0.05."
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_replicability.R
rep_sim <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_replicability_sim.rds")

rep_sigs <- bind_rows(
  tibble(id = paste0("perio:", dat$perio_row), Study = dat$Study, Condition = "Periodontitis",
         direction = dat$`Abundance in Group 1`, site_group = "oral"),
  tibble(id = bsdb_cc$`BSDB ID`, Study = bsdb_cc$Study, Condition = bsdb_cc$Condition,
         direction = bsdb_cc$`Abundance in Group 1`, site_group = site_group(bsdb_cc$`Body site`))
) |>
  filter(id %in% rownames(rep_sim)) |>
  mutate(pos = match(id, rownames(rep_sim)))

# mean similarity between different studies, each pair of studies counting once: similarities are
# averaged over the two studies' signatures, then over pairs of studies
cross_study_sim <- function(idx) {
  study <- rep_sigs$Study[idx]
  s <- rep_sim[rep_sigs$pos[idx], rep_sigs$pos[idx]]
  sums <- rowsum(t(rowsum(s, study)), study)
  n <- as.vector(table(study)[rownames(sums)])
  means <- sums / outer(n, n)
  mean(means[upper.tri(means)])
}

# observed score vs random sets of signatures of *other* conditions with the same direction and site groups
set.seed(1)
replicability <- rep_sigs |>
  mutate(i = row_number()) |>
  filter(n_distinct(Study) >= 5, .by = c(Condition, direction)) |>
  summarise(studies = n_distinct(Study), idx = list(i), .by = c(Condition, direction)) |>
  mutate(
    observed = map_dbl(idx, cross_study_sim),
    random = pmap(list(idx, Condition, direction), \(idx, cond, dir) {
      # the pool excludes the condition's own signatures, so the question is whether its studies agree more
      # than studies of other conditions from the same site groups (as in the whole-signature similarity tests)
      other <- rep_sigs$direction == dir & rep_sigs$Condition != cond
      pool <- split(which(other), rep_sigs$site_group[other])
      need <- table(rep_sigs$site_group[idx])
      # site groups with fewer signatures than needed are drawn from all other signatures of this direction
      draw <- \(g) {
        from <- if (!is.null(pool[[g]]) && length(pool[[g]]) >= need[[g]]) pool[[g]] else unlist(pool)
        from[sample.int(length(from), need[[g]])]
      }
      r <- replicate(1000, cross_study_sim(unlist(map(names(need), draw))))
      r[!is.na(r)]
    }),
    random_mean = map_dbl(random, mean),
    lo = map_dbl(random, quantile, 0.025), hi = map_dbl(random, quantile, 0.975),
    p = map2_dbl(observed, random, \(o, r) (1 + sum(r >= o)) / (1 + length(r))),
    excess = observed - random_mean
  ) |>
  mutate(fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"), .by = direction)

# one value of periodontitis's row (used in the figure details and text)
rv <- \(dir, col) replicability[[col]][replicability$Condition == "Periodontitis" & replicability$direction == dir]

# the same test on subsets of the periodontitis signatures, and on BugSigDB's plaque signatures
rep_perio <- rep_sigs |> filter(Condition == "Periodontitis")
rep_assay <- assay_of(method_of(dat$`Sequencing type`, dat$`Sequencing platform`))[
  match(as.integer(sub("perio:", "", rep_perio$id)), dat$perio_row)]
rep_plaque <- rep_sigs |>
  filter(Condition != "Periodontitis", site_group == "oral") |>
  filter(grepl("plaque", bsdb_cc$`Body site`[match(id, bsdb_cc$`BSDB ID`)], ignore.case = TRUE))

rep_subsets <- bind_rows(
  rep_sigs,
  mutate(rep_perio[rep_assay == "Sequencing", ], Condition = "Periodontitis (sequencing only)"),
  mutate(rep_perio[rep_assay == "Targeted", ], Condition = "Periodontitis (targeted only)"),
  mutate(filter(rep_sigs, id %in% rep_plaque$id), Condition = "BugSigDB dental plaque")
)
subset_sim <- function(idx) {
  study <- rep_subsets$Study[idx]
  s <- rep_sim[rep_subsets$pos[idx], rep_subsets$pos[idx]]
  sums <- rowsum(t(rowsum(s, study)), study)
  n <- as.vector(table(study)[rownames(sums)])
  means <- sums / outer(n, n)
  mean(means[upper.tri(means)])
}
subset_levels <- c("Periodontitis", "Periodontitis (sequencing only)", "Periodontitis (targeted only)",
                   "BugSigDB dental plaque")
set.seed(1)
rep_sens <- rep_subsets |>
  mutate(i = row_number()) |>
  filter(Condition %in% subset_levels) |>
  summarise(studies = n_distinct(Study), idx = list(i), .by = c(Condition, direction)) |>
  mutate(
    observed = map_dbl(idx, subset_sim),
    random = pmap(list(idx, Condition, direction), \(idx, cond, dir) {
      # periodontitis subsets keep the published pool (all other conditions, matched on site group);
      # the plaque row is compared with all other oral signatures of the direction
      other <- if (cond == "BugSigDB dental plaque") {
        rep_subsets$direction == dir & rep_subsets$site_group == "oral" &
          !rep_subsets$Condition %in% subset_levels
      } else {
        rep_subsets$direction == dir & !grepl("^Periodontitis", rep_subsets$Condition) &
          rep_subsets$Condition != "BugSigDB dental plaque"
      }
      pool <- split(which(other), rep_subsets$site_group[other])
      need <- table(rep_subsets$site_group[idx])
      draw <- \(g) {
        from <- if (!is.null(pool[[g]]) && length(pool[[g]]) >= need[[g]]) pool[[g]] else unlist(pool)
        from[sample.int(length(from), need[[g]])]
      }
      r <- replicate(1000, subset_sim(unlist(map(names(need), draw))))
      r[!is.na(r)]
    }),
    random_mean = map_dbl(random, mean), lo = map_dbl(random, quantile, 0.025),
    hi = map_dbl(random, quantile, 0.975),
    p = map2_dbl(observed, random, \(o, r) (1 + sum(r >= o)) / (1 + length(r)))
  )
rs <- \(cond, dir, col) rep_sens[[col]][rep_sens$Condition == cond & rep_sens$direction == dir]
rs2 <- \(cond, dir, col) sprintf("%.2f", rs(cond, dir, col))

# the 10 conditions per direction with the largest excess, plus periodontitis if outside them (FDR stays
# computed over all conditions), and the checks, all ranked by excess
check_labels <- c("Periodontitis (sequencing only)" = "Periodontitis: sequencing only",
                  "Periodontitis (targeted only)" = "Periodontitis: targeted only",
                  "BugSigDB dental plaque" = "Dental plaque, BugSigDB pooled")
rep_rows <- bind_rows(
  replicability |>
    filter(rank(-excess) <= 10 | Condition == "Periodontitis", .by = direction) |>
    mutate(kind = ifelse(Condition == "Periodontitis", "perio", "condition"), filled = fdr < 0.05,
           label = Condition, key = excess),
  rep_sens |>
    filter(Condition %in% names(check_labels)) |>
    mutate(kind = ifelse(Condition == "BugSigDB dental plaque", "plaque", "perio"), filled = p < 0.05,
           label = check_labels[Condition], key = observed - random_mean)) |>
  mutate(direction = factor(direction, levels = c("increased", "decreased"),
                            labels = c("Increased in the condition", "Decreased in the condition")),
         label = paste0(label, " (", studies, ")"),
         row = fct_reorder(paste(label, direction, sep = "___"), key))

ggplot(rep_rows, aes(y = row)) +
  # shading drawn on every row (transparent for most), as a filtered layer would reorder the rows
  geom_tile(aes(x = 0), width = Inf, height = 1,
            fill = c(perio = "#dff3ea", plaque = "#e6eef8", condition = NA)[rep_rows$kind]) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0, linewidth = 2.5, color = "grey85") +
  geom_point(aes(x = random_mean), shape = "|", size = 3, color = "grey45") +
  geom_point(aes(x = observed, fill = filled), shape = 21, size = 2.8, color = "grey10", stroke = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey10", `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) sub("___.*", "", x)) +
  facet_wrap(~direction, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Mean similarity between signatures from different studies", y = NULL) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Score (point)**: for each pair of signatures, best-match average Lin similarity: each taxon's best Lin match in the other signature, averaged in both directions, with taxa at their reported rank. These are averaged over all signature pairs from two different studies, then over study pairs. Pairs within one study are excluded.
- **Signatures**: PerioSigDB signatures (all treated as oral) and filtered BugSigDB signatures (human disease-vs-control, no meta-analyses), each with ≥5 taxa. Periodontitis: 68 increased and 35 decreased signatures with ≥5 taxa (one per study in each direction).
- **Rows**: of the conditions with ≥5 studies in that direction after the ≥5-taxa filter, the 10 with the largest excess (observed − random mean) and periodontitis, with that number of studies in brackets. Increased and decreased are analysed separately.
- **Random sets (grey bar, tick)**: 1,000 draws without replacement, each with the same number of signatures as the condition, of the same direction and the same body site groups, from the signatures of all other conditions, so the null is that the condition's studies agree no more than studies of other conditions from the same sites. (Site groups with too few such signatures are drawn from all other signatures of the direction.) Each draw is scored with the same between-study average. The bar is the central 95% and the tick the mean.
- **Test**: one-sided resampling p = (1 + number of random scores ≥ observed) ÷ 1,001, so the smallest possible p is 0.001. BH within each direction (32 decreased and 31 increased conditions).
- **Example**: periodontitis increased: observed `r sprintf("%.3f", rv("increased", "observed"))` vs random mean `r sprintf("%.3f", rv("increased", "random_mean"))` (95%: `r sprintf("%.3f", rv("increased", "lo"))`–`r sprintf("%.3f", rv("increased", "hi"))`), p = `r signif(rv("increased", "p"), 1)`, FDR = `r signif(rv("increased", "fdr"), 1)`, excess = `r sprintf("%.3f", rv("increased", "excess"))`. Periodontitis decreased: `r sprintf("%.3f", rv("decreased", "observed"))` vs `r sprintf("%.3f", rv("decreased", "random_mean"))`, p = `r signif(rv("decreased", "p"), 1)`, FDR = `r signif(rv("decreased", "fdr"), 1)`.
- **Ordering**: by excess (observed − random mean), not by absolute similarity. The check rows are ranked the same way.
- **Green assay rows:** periodontitis's signatures and score restricted to one assay group. Sequencing: `r rs("Periodontitis (sequencing only)", "increased", "studies")` increased and `r rs("Periodontitis (sequencing only)", "decreased", "studies")` decreased studies; targeted: `r rs("Periodontitis (targeted only)", "increased", "studies")` and `r rs("Periodontitis (targeted only)", "decreased", "studies")`. The targeted-decreased row rests on 6 studies, so its interval is wide.
- **Blue plaque row:** BugSigDB signatures whose body site names dental plaque (`r rs("BugSigDB dental plaque", "increased", "studies")` increased and `r rs("BugSigDB dental plaque", "decreased", "studies")` decreased studies, across 10–11 conditions, mostly rheumatoid arthritis, type II diabetes, Alzheimer's disease and gingivitis; all are plaque-only signatures, subgingival in two thirds). They are pooled across conditions, so this is not a within-condition score: it asks whether plaque sampling alone makes signatures look alike. Its random sets are drawn from all other oral signatures of the direction.
- **Check rows, test:** the same resampling test, unadjusted. They check one condition rather than rank conditions, so they carry no FDR.
- **Watch out (random pool)**: periodontitis's random sets are drawn from the `r sum(rep_sigs$direction == "increased" & rep_sigs$site_group == "oral" & rep_sigs$Condition != "Periodontitis")` oral increased and `r sum(rep_sigs$direction == "decreased" & rep_sigs$site_group == "oral" & rep_sigs$Condition != "Periodontitis")` oral decreased BugSigDB signatures, with `r sum(rep_sigs$direction == "increased" & rep_sigs$Condition == "Periodontitis")` and `r sum(rep_sigs$direction == "decreased" & rep_sigs$Condition == "Periodontitis")` needed per draw, so draws overlap substantially and the grey bar is narrow; it is specific to this pool of oral signatures.
- **Watch out**: "body site group" is coarse. PerioSigDB is subgingival plaque only, while the oral pool mixes saliva, tongue and plaque. Similarity rewards studies that report the same taxa, which targeted panels encourage, regardless of effect size.
:::

```{r replicability-values}
rv2 <- \(dir, col) sprintf("%.2f", rv(dir, col))
rank_excess <- \(dir) with(filter(replicability, direction == dir), rank(-excess)[Condition == "Periodontitis"])
# other conditions passing FDR in a direction
rep_others <- \(dir) with(filter(replicability, direction == dir, fdr < 0.05, Condition != "Periodontitis") |> arrange(fdr),
                          if (length(Condition)) paste(Condition, collapse = ", ") else "none")
```

**Shows:** periodontitis's increased signatures agree between studies more than site-matched random sets do (mean similarity `r rv2("increased", "observed")` vs `r rv2("increased", "random_mean")`, FDR = `r signif(rv("increased", "fdr"), 1)`). They rank `r rank_excess("increased")` of `r sum(replicability$direction == "increased")` conditions by excess over the random expectation, and rest on far more studies (`r rv("increased", "studies")`) than any other condition. The decreased signatures are only slightly, and not significantly, more similar than random oral ones (`r rv2("decreased", "observed")` vs `r rv2("decreased", "random_mean")`, FDR = `r signif(rv("decreased", "fdr"), 1)`): studies agree more on which taxa rise in periodontitis than on which fall. Other conditions passing FDR: `r rep_others("increased")` (increased), `r rep_others("decreased")` (decreased). The score counts which taxa studies report, not how large the differences are.


Two features of PerioSigDB could produce this agreement on their own: its fixed-panel assays, which report the same taxa by construction, and its sampling, since every signature is subgingival plaque while the random oral sets also draw on saliva, tongue and mucosa. The periodontitis assay rows and the dental plaque row of the figure test both.

**Shows (check rows):** neither explanation accounts for the agreement. Sequencing signatures alone agree as strongly as the full set (increased `r rs2("Periodontitis (sequencing only)", "increased", "observed")` vs `r rs2("Periodontitis (sequencing only)", "increased", "random_mean")` expected, p = `r signif(rs("Periodontitis (sequencing only)", "increased", "p"), 2)`), and so do targeted signatures alone (`r rs2("Periodontitis (targeted only)", "increased", "observed")` vs `r rs2("Periodontitis (targeted only)", "increased", "random_mean")`, p = `r signif(rs("Periodontitis (targeted only)", "increased", "p"), 2)`), so fixed panels are not what drives it. The decreased signatures behave differently: sequencing studies agree (`r rs2("Periodontitis (sequencing only)", "decreased", "observed")` vs `r rs2("Periodontitis (sequencing only)", "decreased", "random_mean")`, p = `r signif(rs("Periodontitis (sequencing only)", "decreased", "p"), 2)`) while the 6 targeted ones do not (`r rs2("Periodontitis (targeted only)", "decreased", "observed")` vs `r rs2("Periodontitis (targeted only)", "decreased", "random_mean")`, p = `r signif(rs("Periodontitis (targeted only)", "decreased", "p"), 2)`), which fits panels built to detect pathogens rather than commensals. Plaque sampling does not create agreement either: BugSigDB's own plaque signatures are no more alike than random oral sets (increased `r rs2("BugSigDB dental plaque", "increased", "observed")` vs `r rs2("BugSigDB dental plaque", "increased", "random_mean")`, p = `r signif(rs("BugSigDB dental plaque", "increased", "p"), 2)`; decreased `r rs2("BugSigDB dental plaque", "decreased", "observed")` vs `r rs2("BugSigDB dental plaque", "decreased", "random_mean")`, p = `r signif(rs("BugSigDB dental plaque", "decreased", "p"), 2)`), and they come from 10–11 different conditions, so their agreement is what the site alone buys.


This test is stricter than the BugSigDB paper's, which used fecal signatures only, counted pairs of signatures from the same study, and drew random signatures from all fecal signatures. Run that way on the current BugSigDB, HIV infection and COVID-19 decreased signatures replicate, as the paper reported, as do Parkinson's disease decreased signatures. Here COVID-19 also includes oral and nasopharyngeal studies, which dilute its fecal agreement. Parkinson's disease weakens mainly because the disease-vs-control filter drops comparisons between Parkinson's subtypes and treatments, which agree with each other; with fecal disease-vs-control signatures only, it is borderline (p = 0.05). Antibiotics are not a disease-vs-control comparison and are not included.

### Where does periodontitis sit among oral conditions?

The BugSigDB paper pooled the signatures of each condition at a body site into a metasignature, weighting each taxon by the sample size of the studies reporting it, and compared conditions by the similarity of their metasignatures (Geistlinger et al. 2024, Figure 4). Here this is done for the conditions studied in the mouth. Unlike the binomial consensus, the pooled signature is weighted by sample size, so large studies count more.

```{r oral-metasignatures}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Similarity of oral conditions' pooled signatures. For each condition, each genus gets a signed weight: the summed sample size of the condition's studies reporting it increased, divided by the total sample size of the condition's increased signatures, minus the same for decreased. Studies (study units for BugSigDB: study, condition, direction and body site group) count once, with the largest sample size of their signatures. Conditions: periodontitis (PerioSigDB) and BugSigDB conditions with at least 3 oral studies in a direction (disease-vs-control comparisons); a direction with fewer than 3 studies (0 in brackets) is left out and contributes no weight, so such a condition's similarity reflects its other direction only. Cells: cosine similarity between two conditions' signed genus weights (red: genera shift in the same direction; blue: opposite). Rows and columns: ordered by hierarchical clustering (average linkage on 1 − similarity). Brackets: oral studies reporting increased / decreased taxa. Asterisks on the periodontitis row: p < 0.05 (*) or < 0.01 (**), two-sided permutation test of the similarity to periodontitis against 1,000 random reassignments of condition labels among the BugSigDB oral studies of each direction."
oral_units <- bind_rows(
  tibble(unit = paste("perio", dat$Study), Condition = "Periodontitis", direction = dat$`Abundance in Group 1`,
         n = as.numeric(dat$`Group 0 sample size`) + as.numeric(dat$`Group 1 sample size`),
         taxon = map(dat$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, genera)),
  bsdb_cc_sigs |>
    filter(site_group == "oral") |>
    transmute(unit = paste("bsdb", unit), Condition, direction,
              n = as.numeric(bsdb_cc$`Group 0 sample size`[sig]) + as.numeric(bsdb_cc$`Group 1 sample size`[sig]),
              taxon = map(bsdb_cc$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`[sig], genera))
) |>
  summarise(n = suppressWarnings(max(n, na.rm = TRUE)), taxon = list(unique(unlist(taxon))),
            .by = c(unit, Condition, direction)) |>
  filter(is.finite(n), lengths(taxon) > 0) |>
  filter(n() >= 3, .by = c(Condition, direction))

# signed genus weights (columns: conditions)
signed_weights <- function(units) {
  units |>
    mutate(total = sum(n), .by = c(Condition, direction)) |>
    unnest(taxon) |>
    summarise(w = sum(n / total), .by = c(Condition, direction, taxon)) |>
    mutate(w = ifelse(direction == "increased", w, -w)) |>
    summarise(w = sum(w), .by = c(Condition, taxon)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = Condition, values_from = w, values_fill = 0) |>
    column_to_rownames("taxon") |>
    as.matrix()
}
cosine <- \(m) crossprod(m) / tcrossprod(sqrt(colSums(m^2)))

oral_cos <- cosine(signed_weights(oral_units))

set.seed(1)
bsdb_oral <- oral_units$Condition != "Periodontitis"
null_cos <- replicate(1000, {
  u <- oral_units
  u$Condition[bsdb_oral] <- ave(u$Condition[bsdb_oral], u$direction[bsdb_oral], FUN = sample)
  cosine(signed_weights(u))["Periodontitis", colnames(oral_cos)]
})
oral_p <- map_dbl(colnames(oral_cos), \(cond) {
  obs <- oral_cos["Periodontitis", cond]
  min(1, 2 * min(mean(c(null_cos[cond, ] >= obs, TRUE)), mean(c(null_cos[cond, ] <= obs, TRUE))))
}) |>
  setNames(colnames(oral_cos))

oral_order <- colnames(oral_cos)[hclust(as.dist(1 - oral_cos), method = "average")$order]
oral_labels <- oral_units |>
  count(Condition, direction) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", Condition, increased, decreased)) |>
  (\(x) setNames(x$label, x$Condition))()

as_tibble(oral_cos, rownames = "row") |>
  pivot_longer(-row, names_to = "col", values_to = "cosine") |>
  mutate(
    star = ifelse(row == "Periodontitis" & col != "Periodontitis",
                  case_when(oral_p[col] < 0.01 ~ "**", oral_p[col] < 0.05 ~ "*", .default = ""), ""),
    label = ifelse(row == col, "", paste0(sprintf("%.2f", cosine), star)),
    row = factor(oral_labels[row], levels = oral_labels[rev(oral_order)]),
    col = factor(oral_labels[col], levels = oral_labels[oral_order])
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(col, row, fill = ifelse(as.character(row) == as.character(col), NA, cosine))) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.6, color = "grey15") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#1c5cab", mid = "#f0efec", high = "#c0392b", midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1),
                       na.value = "grey85", name = "Cosine\nsimilarity") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1), legend.position = "right",
        legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
        axis.text.y = element_text(face = ifelse(grepl("^Periodontitis", levels(factor(oral_labels[rev(oral_order)],
                                                                                         levels = oral_labels[rev(oral_order)]))),
                                                 "bold", "plain")))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Genus weight**: for condition C and genus g, (summed sample size of C's increased units reporting g ÷ summed sample size of all C's increased units) − (the same for decreased). The weight ranges from −1 to 1. All taxa are collapsed to genus; taxa above genus are dropped.
- **Units**: PerioSigDB, one per study and direction (all subgingival plaque). BugSigDB, one per study, condition and direction, from signatures whose body sites are all oral ("mixed"-site signatures are excluded), from the filtered BugSigDB (human disease-vs-control, no meta-analyses). Sample size is Group 0 + Group 1, the largest among the unit's signatures; units without a sample size are dropped.
- **Example weight**: *Porphyromonas* in periodontitis: 77 increased studies with 7,467 of the 11,023 participants in increased studies (0.68), minus 10 decreased studies with 342 of 5,180 (0.07) = 0.61, the largest. The most negative is *Actinomyces* (−0.29).
- **Each cell**: cosine similarity between two conditions' weight vectors over the union of 243 genera. +1 = same genera shifted in the same proportions; 0 = unrelated; −1 = opposite.
- **Conditions**: those with ≥3 oral units in at least one direction (a direction with <3 is set to 0). Arthritis and obesity have only increased units (3/0). Periodontitis has 115/70 units.
- **Test (periodontitis row)**: BugSigDB oral units have their condition labels shuffled within each direction (unit sizes and genera stay fixed; periodontitis is never shuffled), and the cosine to periodontitis is recomputed 1,000 times. Two-sided p = 2 × the smaller tail, with +1 correction. Unadjusted.
- **Example**: rheumatoid arthritis 0.48, p = 0.022 (10 of 1,000 permutations at least as high; 2 × 11/1,001); head and neck cancer 0.34, p = 0.35, where random labels give a mean of 0.18 (central 95%: −0.10 to 0.46); colorectal cancer −0.01 (only 4/4 oral units).
- **Rheumatoid arthritis depends on study inclusion:** its p-value changes with which PerioSigDB studies are included: 0.056 before the full-text review, 0.05 with all reviewed studies, 0.052 with only the two rheumatoid arthritis studies entered as periodontitis (450, 2025-PubMed-130) removed, and 0.022 now, with all 9 excluded studies removed. The similarity itself is stable (0.46–0.48).
- **Clustering**: average linkage on 1 − cosine. Branch order is arbitrary within a merge, so neighbouring rows are not necessarily the most similar.
- **Watch out**: periodontitis contributes ~185 units against 3–26 for each other condition, so its vector is far more stable. Small conditions' vectors are dominated by a few studies, which is why the null range is wide. Weights reflect reporting frequency, not effect size.
:::

```{r oral-metasignature-values}
oc <- \(cond) sprintf("%.2f, p = %s", oral_cos["Periodontitis", cond], signif(oral_p[cond], 1))
```

**Shows:** the largest positive similarities to periodontitis were for rheumatoid arthritis (`r oc("Rheumatoid arthritis")`), head and neck cancer (`r oc("Head and neck cancer")`), esophageal cancer (`r oc("Esophageal cancer")`) and smoking (`r oc("Smoking behavior")`): in their oral studies, many of the same genera are reported in the same directions. Parkinson's disease, obesity, Alzheimer's disease and arthritis lean the opposite way. Colorectal cancer appears here only through its few oral studies (`r oc("Colorectal cancer")`): its resemblance to periodontitis elsewhere in this report comes from its gut samples, where periodontitis-increased genera are reported, not from oral samples. Permuting the condition labels puts almost all of these similarities inside the random range. Only rheumatoid arthritis reaches p < 0.05 (p = `r signif(oral_p[["Rheumatoid arthritis"]], 2)`, unadjusted across 10 conditions, so it would not pass a correction for 10 tests; 0.02–0.06 depending on which PerioSigDB studies are included, see Figure details): random sets the size of head and neck cancer's give `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(null_cos["Head and neck cancer", ]))` on average but range widely (central 95%: `r sprintf("%.2f", quantile(null_cos["Head and neck cancer", ], 0.025))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", quantile(null_cos["Head and neck cancer", ], 0.975))`), so with the number of oral studies available, these similarities are imprecise. The paper's semantic similarity, applied to these pooled oral signatures, scores almost every pair above 0.8, including periodontitis-increased against periodontitis-decreased: pooled oral signatures share so many oral taxa that it cannot separate them, so genus weights are used instead.

### Are the periodontitis-decreased genera simply common oral taxa?

Across BugSigDB, genera common in healthy samples tend to be reported decreased in disease and rare ones increased, whatever the disease (Geistlinger et al. 2024, Figure 4). If periodontitis signatures only reflected this, the genera they report decreased would reflect a pattern common to many diseases rather than one particular to periodontitis. Prevalence here is from healthy Human Microbiome Project subgingival plaque (16S V3–V5).

```{r prevalence-direction}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: "Direction of genera reported in periodontitis (PerioSigDB, left) and in other conditions sampled in the mouth (BugSigDB, right) against their prevalence in healthy subgingival plaque (share of Human Microbiome Project samples, first visit, with the genus at 0.1% relative abundance or more). y: share of signatures (PerioSigDB) or study units (BugSigDB) reporting the genus that report it increased; the two databases are counted in different units. Prevalence in subgingival plaque is used as the reference for all oral sampling sites. Genera reported at least 5 times in each database. Colour: direction in periodontitis of the 20 genera per direction in the genus heatmaps; grey: other genera. Dashed line: 50% (no consistent direction). Panel titles: Spearman correlation between prevalence and share increased, with its p-value."
# precomputed by scripts/hmp_oral_prevalence.R
hmp_prevalence <- readRDS("../../output/hmp_oral_prevalence.rds") |>
  filter(site == "Subgingival Plaque")

share_increased <- function(d) {
  d |>
    filter(direction %in% c("increased", "decreased")) |>
    count(taxon, direction) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
    mutate(n = increased + decreased, share = increased / n) |>
    filter(n >= 5)
}

oral_units <- bsdb_sigs$sig[bsdb_sigs$site_group == "oral"]
prevalence_direction <- bind_rows(
  PerioSigDB = share_increased(sig_genera(dat)),
  BugSigDB = share_increased(filter(bsdb_genera, sig %in% oral_units)),
  .id = "db"
) |>
  filter(n_distinct(db) == 2, .by = taxon) |>
  inner_join(select(hmp_prevalence, taxon, prevalence = prevalence_01), by = "taxon") |>
  left_join(select(perio_genera, taxon, perio = direction), by = "taxon") |>
  mutate(perio = coalesce(perio, "other"))

prevalence_cor <- prevalence_direction |>
  summarise(test = list(cor.test(prevalence, share, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)), genera = n(), .by = db) |>
  mutate(rho = map_dbl(test, "estimate"), p = map_dbl(test, "p.value"),
         panel = sprintf("%s (%s)\nSpearman rho = %.2f, p = %s",
                         db, ifelse(db == "PerioSigDB", "periodontitis", "other oral conditions"),
                         rho, signif(p, 2)))

prevalence_direction |>
  left_join(select(prevalence_cor, db, panel), by = "db") |>
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = prevalence_cor$panel[match(db_levels, prevalence_cor$db)])) |>
  ggplot(aes(prevalence, share)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(fill = perio), shape = 21, size = 2.6, color = "grey15", stroke = 0.4) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = taxon), size = 2.6, fontface = "italic", color = "grey25", seed = 1,
                  max.overlaps = Inf, min.segment.length = 0.2, segment.color = "grey70") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(increased = "#c2410c", decreased = "#1c5cab", other = "grey80"),
                    labels = c(increased = "Increased in periodontitis", decreased = "Decreased in periodontitis",
                               other = "Other genera"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  labs(x = "Prevalence in healthy subgingival plaque", y = "Reports of the genus that are increased") +
  theme(legend.position = "top", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each point**: one genus. x = share of the 183 HMP healthy subgingival plaque samples (16S V3–V5, first visit) where the genus is ≥0.1% of all reads. y = share of the genus's reports that say increased.
- **Units differ by panel**: PerioSigDB counts signatures (all 187, every one subgingival plaque). BugSigDB counts study units (study × condition × direction) from 260 oral-only units of other conditions in the filtered BugSigDB.
- **Genera included**: ≥5 reports in *each* database (45 genera) and present in HMP under the same name (37). Renamed genera drop out because HMP uses older names: *Parvimonas*, *Alloprevotella*, *Fretibacterium*, *Schaalia*, *Segatella*, *Hoylesella*, *Arachnia*, *Lachnoanaerobaculum*. The same 37 genera are in both panels.
- **Colour**: the 20 genera per direction from the genus heatmaps (top binomial p in PerioSigDB): 15 increased, 14 decreased and 8 other among the 37. Colour reflects the PerioSigDB direction in both panels.
- **Test**: Spearman correlation of x vs y within each panel (asymptotic p, two-sided). PerioSigDB rho = −0.37, p = 0.023; BugSigDB rho = −0.29, p = 0.080. The difference between the two correlations is not tested.
- **Example**: *Rothia*: 88.5% prevalence, decreased in 23 of 25 periodontitis reports (8% increased) but only 30 of 52 oral BugSigDB units (42% increased). *Porphyromonas*: 92% prevalence, yet increased in 77 of 87 periodontitis reports and 25 of 55 BugSigDB units.
- **Spread**: 31 of 37 genera fall between 30% and 70% increased in BugSigDB, vs 10 of 37 in PerioSigDB.
- **Watch out**: the reference is subgingival plaque for all BugSigDB oral sites (saliva, tongue and others), where prevalence differs. PerioSigDB includes targeted-panel signatures, which report only the genera on the panel.
:::

```{r prevalence-values}
pc <- \(d, col) prevalence_cor[[col]][prevalence_cor$db == d]
# the same correlation with mean relative abundance in place of prevalence (no second figure: the two
# HMP measures rank these genera almost identically, so they are not independent evidence)
abundance_cor <- prevalence_direction |>
  inner_join(select(hmp_prevalence, taxon, abundance = mean_abundance), by = "taxon") |>
  summarise(test = list(cor.test(abundance, share, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)),
            rho_measures = cor(prevalence, abundance, method = "spearman"), .by = db) |>
  mutate(rho = map_dbl(test, "estimate"), p = map_dbl(test, "p.value"))
ac <- \(d, col) abundance_cor[[col]][abundance_cor$db == d]
# genera without a consistent direction: 30-70% of their reports increased
mixed <- \(d) with(filter(prevalence_direction, db == d), sum(share >= 0.3 & share <= 0.7))
# share of reports of a genus that are decreased, with the counts
pd <- \(d, g) with(filter(prevalence_direction, db == d, taxon == g),
                   sprintf("%.0f%% (%d/%d)", 100 * decreased / n, decreased, n))
```

**Shows:** genera common in healthy subgingival plaque are more often reported decreased in periodontitis. The association is stronger for periodontitis (rho = `r sprintf("%.2f", pc("PerioSigDB", "rho"))` over `r pc("PerioSigDB", "genera")` genera) than for other oral conditions (rho = `r sprintf("%.2f", pc("BugSigDB", "rho"))`, p = `r signif(pc("BugSigDB", "p"), 1)`); the two correlations are not compared formally. Studies of other oral conditions disagree on the direction of most genera: `r mixed("BugSigDB")` of the `r pc("BugSigDB", "genera")` genera are reported increased by between 30% and 70% of the studies reporting them. In periodontitis only `r mixed("PerioSigDB")` of the `r pc("PerioSigDB", "genera")` are split like this; the rest are reported in one direction by more than 70% of signatures. The periodontitis-decreased genera lean decreased in other oral conditions too, so part of their decrease is shared with other oral diseases, but periodontitis studies report it more consistently: *Rothia*, *Haemophilus* and *Corynebacterium* are reported decreased in `r pd("PerioSigDB", "Rothia")`, `r pd("PerioSigDB", "Haemophilus")` and `r pd("PerioSigDB", "Corynebacterium")` of periodontitis reports but only `r pd("BugSigDB", "Rothia")`, `r pd("BugSigDB", "Haemophilus")` and `r pd("BugSigDB", "Corynebacterium")` of reports in other oral conditions. Nor is the periodontitis increase only rare genera appearing: *Porphyromonas*, *Prevotella* and *Fusobacterium* are present in nearly every healthy subgingival sample and still consistently reported increased.

Mean relative abundance gives the same answer as prevalence (periodontitis rho = `r sprintf("%.2f", ac("PerioSigDB", "rho"))`, p = `r signif(ac("PerioSigDB", "p"), 2)`; other oral conditions rho = `r sprintf("%.2f", ac("BugSigDB", "rho"))`, p = `r signif(ac("BugSigDB", "p"), 2)`). The two HMP measures rank these genera almost identically (Spearman rho = `r sprintf("%.2f", ac("PerioSigDB", "rho_measures"))`), so they are not independent evidence.

### Where do periodontitis genera occur in the healthy mouth?

The Human Microbiome Project sampled nine sites in the mouth of the same healthy participants. Where a genus occurs in health suggests whether the genera that rise in periodontitis are already resident in the gingival pocket or are common elsewhere in the mouth, which could act as a reservoir. These are healthy people sampled once, so this shows where genera live, not where periodontitis taxa come from.

```{r oral-habitat}
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 9.5
#| fig-cap: "Prevalence (A) and mean relative abundance (B) of periodontitis genera across the nine oral sites of the Human Microbiome Project (healthy participants, first visit, 16S V3–V5). A: share of samples from that site with the genus at 0.1% relative abundance or more. B: mean over the site's samples of the genus's share of reads, in percent (label); colour is scaled within each genus, relative to its highest site on a log scale, so it shows where each genus peaks rather than how abundant genera are compared with each other. Rows: the 20 genera per direction from the genus heatmaps that are present in HMP under the same name, ordered within each direction by prevalence in subgingival plaque minus mean prevalence at the seven non-plaque sites (plaque-associated at top); the same rows in both panels. Genera at 0% prevalence at five or more sites are left out. Columns: sites, with the number of samples, grouped by the three oral community types of Segata et al. 2012 (plaque; buccal mucosa, gingiva and palate; tongue, saliva, tonsils and throat)."
# precomputed by scripts/hmp_oral_prevalence.R (all nine oral sites)
# sites grouped into the three community types of Segata et al. 2012 (same HMP samples)
site_levels <- c("Subgingival Plaque", "Supragingival Plaque", "Buccal Mucosa", "Attached Keratinized Gingiva",
                 "Hard Palate", "Tongue Dorsum", "Saliva", "Palatine Tonsils", "Throat")
site_labels <- c("Sub-\ngingival\nplaque", "Supra-\ngingival\nplaque", "Buccal\nmucosa", "Attached\ngingiva",
                 "Hard\npalate", "Tongue\ndorsum", "Saliva", "Palatine\ntonsils", "Throat")
site_groups <- setNames(rep(c("Plaque", "Buccal mucosa, gingiva, palate", "Tongue, saliva, tonsils, throat"),
                            c(2, 3, 4)), site_levels)
hmp_sites <- readRDS("../../output/hmp_oral_prevalence.rds")
site_n <- distinct(hmp_sites, site, samples)

oral_habitat <- perio_genera |>
  select(taxon, direction) |>
  inner_join(select(hmp_sites, site, taxon, prevalence = prevalence_01, abundance = mean_abundance), by = "taxon") |>
  mutate(plaque_bias = prevalence[site == "Subgingival Plaque"] -
           mean(prevalence[!site %in% c("Subgingival Plaque", "Supragingival Plaque")]),
         .by = taxon)
# genera at 0% prevalence (rounded) at five or more of the nine sites are left out of the figure
habitat_rare <- oral_habitat |>
  summarise(zero_sites = sum(round(100 * prevalence) == 0), .by = taxon) |>
  filter(zero_sites >= 5) |>
  pull(taxon)

habitat_plot <- oral_habitat |>
  filter(!taxon %in% habitat_rare) |>
  mutate(habitat = factor(site_groups[site], levels = unique(site_groups)),
         site = factor(site, levels = site_levels,
                       labels = paste0(site_labels, "\n(", site_n$samples[match(site_levels, site_n$site)], ")")),
         direction = factor(direction, levels = c("increased", "decreased"),
                            labels = c("Increased in\nperiodontitis", "Decreased in\nperiodontitis")),
         taxon = fct_reorder(taxon, plaque_bias))

# abundance labels in percent of reads, with fewer decimals for larger values
pct_label <- \(a) {
  p <- 100 * a
  case_when(p == 0 ~ "0", p < 0.01 ~ "<0.01", p < 1 ~ sprintf("%.2f", p),
            p < 10 ~ sprintf("%.1f", p), TRUE ~ sprintf("%.0f", p))
}
# one heatmap; d has columns value (fill), label and dark (white text)
habitat_panel <- function(d, fill_scale) {
  ggplot(d, aes(site, taxon)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = value), color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label, color = dark), size = 2.7) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey20"), guide = "none") +
    fill_scale +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
    guides(fill = guide_colourbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5)) +
    facet_grid(direction ~ habitat, scales = "free", space = "free", switch = "y") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"), strip.placement = "outside",
          strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold"), strip.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
          panel.grid = element_blank(), panel.spacing.x = unit(0.25, "cm"),
          legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_text(size = 9), legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "cm"))
}
prev_panel <- habitat_panel(
  mutate(habitat_plot, value = prevalence, label = round(100 * prevalence), dark = prevalence > 0.55),
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7f7f7", high = "#08306b", labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1),
                      name = "Prevalence (≥ 0.1% of reads)")
)
abund_panel <- habitat_panel(
  # colour scaled within each genus: log10 of abundance relative to the genus's highest site, floored at 1/100
  habitat_plot |>
    mutate(value = pmax(log10(abundance / max(abundance)), -2), .by = taxon) |>
    mutate(label = pct_label(abundance), dark = value > -0.75),
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7f7f7", high = "#08306b", limits = c(-2, 0), breaks = c(-2, -1, 0),
                      labels = c("≤ 1/100", "1/10", "Highest site"),
                      name = "Mean relative abundance,\nrelative to the genus's highest site")
) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), strip.text.y.left = element_blank())

prev_panel + abund_panel + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```

```{r oral-habitat-values}
hp <- \(g, s) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * with(oral_habitat, prevalence[taxon == g & site == s]))
# mean relative abundance, in percent of reads
ha <- \(g, s) paste0(pct_label(with(oral_habitat, abundance[taxon == g & site == s])), "%")
ha_range <- \(g, sites) with(filter(oral_habitat, taxon == g, site %in% sites),
                             paste0(pct_label(min(abundance)), "–", pct_label(max(abundance)), "%"))
non_sub <- setdiff(site_levels, "Subgingival Plaque")
soft <- c("Attached Keratinized Gingiva", "Buccal Mucosa", "Hard Palate")
# per genus, Spearman correlation across the nine sites between the two measures
habitat_rho <- oral_habitat |>
  filter(sd(prevalence) > 0, sd(abundance) > 0, .by = taxon) |>
  summarise(rho = cor(prevalence, abundance, method = "spearman"), .by = taxon)
habitat_missing <- setdiff(perio_genera$taxon, oral_habitat$taxon)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each cell (A)**: share of HMP samples from one site (healthy adults, first visit) in which the genus makes up at least 0.1% of reads, the same threshold as the prevalence figure above. The subgingival plaque column is the x-axis of that figure.
- **Each cell (B)**: mean over the site's samples of the genus's reads ÷ all reads in the sample, in percent (`mean_abundance` from `scripts/hmp_oral_prevalence.R`). Colour is scaled within each row: log10 of the cell's abundance ÷ the genus's highest abundance across the nine sites, so the darkest cell in each row is where the genus peaks; 100-fold or more below the peak is the lightest colour. Labels are absolute. Panel A is not row-scaled because prevalence is on a common 0–100% scale and saturates near 100% for common genera, where row scaling would magnify differences of a few percent.
- **The two measures**: they rank the nine sites similarly (Spearman rho ≥ 0.8) for `r sum(habitat_rho$rho >= 0.8)` of the `r nrow(habitat_rho)` genera detected at some site. They differ mainly for genera in nearly every sample at every site, where prevalence saturates near 100% and only abundance separates the sites.
- **Genera**: the 20 per direction from the genus heatmaps, `r n_distinct(oral_habitat$taxon)` of 40 present in HMP. Left out because HMP uses older names: `r paste0("*", habitat_missing, "*", collapse = ", ")`.
- **Left out as mostly 0**: genera with prevalence rounding to 0% at five or more of the nine sites: `r paste0("*", habitat_rare, "*", collapse = ", ")`. All are at most `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * max(oral_habitat$prevalence[oral_habitat$taxon %in% habitat_rare]))` prevalent at any site.
- **Ordering**: subgingival prevalence minus the mean over the seven non-plaque sites (gingiva, buccal mucosa, hard palate, tongue, saliva, tonsils, throat). Top rows are mainly in plaque; bottom rows are as common or more common elsewhere.
- **Column groups**: Segata et al. 2012 (Genome Biology 13:R42) found, in these HMP samples, that the nine oral sites form three community types: sub- and supragingival plaque; buccal mucosa, attached gingiva and hard palate; and tongue, saliva, tonsils and throat. The groups come from that paper, not from these data.
- **Same people**: the nine sites were sampled from the same participants, so differences between columns are not differences between cohorts.
- **No test.**
- **Watch out**: mean abundance is driven by the samples where the genus is most abundant. A genus can be present below 0.1% at a site, so low values mean rare at that threshold, not absent. Saliva collects cells shed from all surfaces, including plaque. Genus level hides species: *Porphyromonas* and *Treponema* include commensal species as well as the periodontal pathogens.
:::

**Shows:** most periodontitis-decreased genera fall into two groups: genera common throughout the mouth and most abundant on the soft tissues (*Streptococcus* `r ha_range("Streptococcus", soft)` of reads on the gingiva, cheek and palate vs `r ha("Streptococcus", "Subgingival Plaque")` in subgingival plaque; *Haemophilus*, *Gemella*, *Granulicatella*, *Neisseria*), and genera largely confined to plaque, both supra- and subgingival (*Corynebacterium* `r hp("Corynebacterium", "Subgingival Plaque")` in subgingival plaque vs `r hp("Corynebacterium", "Tongue Dorsum")` on the tongue; *Kingella*, *Cardiobacterium*, *Propionibacterium*, *Lautropia*). The periodontitis-increased genera are more varied. *Porphyromonas*, *Prevotella*, *Fusobacterium* and *Campylobacter* are present in nearly every sample at nearly every site, so they could reach the pocket from anywhere in the mouth, but abundance separates them: *Fusobacterium* is most abundant in subgingival plaque (`r ha("Fusobacterium", "Subgingival Plaque")` of reads vs `r ha_range("Fusobacterium", non_sub)` elsewhere), *Prevotella* in saliva, tonsils and throat, and *Porphyromonas* is similar at every site (`r ha_range("Porphyromonas", site_levels)`). *Treponema*, *Tannerella*, *Selenomonas* and *Dialister* are most prevalent in subgingival plaque but also found in saliva and on the tonsils (*Treponema* `r hp("Treponema", "Subgingival Plaque")` subgingival, `r hp("Treponema", "Saliva")` saliva, `r hp("Treponema", "Palatine Tonsils")` tonsils), and are more prevalent below the gumline than above it. By abundance *Treponema* is more clearly subgingival: `r ha("Treponema", "Subgingival Plaque")` of reads there vs at most `r ha("Treponema", "Supragingival Plaque")` at any other site. *Filifactor* and *Anaeroglobus* are rare at every site in health, at most `r hp("Filifactor", "Palatine Tonsils")` anywhere; *Johnsonella*, *Desulfobulbus* and *Pseudoramibacter* are rarer still, found at 0.1% or more almost only in subgingival plaque (left out of the figure as mostly 0). *Peptostreptococcus* and *Mogibacterium* are the exception: more prevalent on the tongue, palate, tonsils and throat (*Peptostreptococcus* `r hp("Peptostreptococcus", "Tongue Dorsum")` on the tongue) than in subgingival plaque (`r hp("Peptostreptococcus", "Subgingival Plaque")`), and more abundant there too (`r ha("Peptostreptococcus", "Saliva")` of reads in saliva vs `r ha("Peptostreptococcus", "Subgingival Plaque")`), so these sites are candidate reservoirs. Whether periodontitis taxa actually move between sites cannot be told from healthy, single-visit genus-level data; paired samples from people with periodontitis, such as Study 1141's subgingival, supragingival and tongue samples, would be the next step.

### Which periodontitis-associated genera are less widely reported in other conditions?

The BugSigDB paper proposed genera reported in only one condition, by several studies, as candidate condition-specific markers (Geistlinger et al. 2024, Supplementary Figure). Few periodontitis-associated genera are exclusive, so here each genus's support in PerioSigDB is compared with how many other conditions report it in the same direction. These counts describe the curated literature, not diagnostic specificity, and depend on the number and methods of studies available for each condition.

```{r specificity}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: "Genera reported in periodontitis and how many other conditions report them. x: PerioSigDB studies reporting the genus increased (left) or decreased (right) in periodontitis. y: other BugSigDB conditions (human disease-vs-control comparisons, all body sites) with at least one study reporting the genus in the same direction. Genera reported by at least 3 PerioSigDB studies in that direction; labelled: at least 10 studies, or reported by no more than 5 other conditions. Shaded: genera reported by at least 10 PerioSigDB studies and no more than 15 other conditions. The cut-offs are descriptive, not a classification: the points form a continuum, and moving them changes which genera fall inside."
perio_support <- sig_genera(dat) |>
  left_join(tibble(sig = seq_len(nrow(dat)), Study = dat$Study), by = "sig") |>
  distinct(Study, direction, taxon) |>
  count(taxon, direction, name = "perio_studies") |>
  filter(perio_studies >= 3)

other_support <- bsdb_genera |>
  left_join(select(bsdb_sigs, sig, Condition, site_group), by = "sig") |>
  summarise(other_conditions = n_distinct(Condition), .by = c(taxon, direction))

specificity <- perio_support |>
  left_join(other_support, by = c("taxon", "direction")) |>
  mutate(other_conditions = coalesce(other_conditions, 0L),
         direction = factor(direction, levels = c("increased", "decreased"),
                            labels = c("Increased in periodontitis", "Decreased in periodontitis")))

ggplot(specificity, aes(perio_studies, other_conditions)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 10, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = 15.5, fill = "#fbe9e4") +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf, label = "Well supported in periodontitis,\nfew other conditions",
           hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.5, size = 2.8, color = "#c0392b", lineheight = 0.9) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2.6, fill = "grey70", color = "grey15", stroke = 0.4) +
  geom_text_repel(data = \(d) filter(d, perio_studies >= 10 | other_conditions <= 5), aes(label = taxon),
                  size = 2.6, fontface = "italic", color = "grey25", seed = 1, max.overlaps = Inf,
                  min.segment.length = 0.2, segment.color = "grey70") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~direction) +
  labs(x = "PerioSigDB studies reporting the genus (log scale)", y = "Other conditions reporting it") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Figure details
- **Each point**: one genus in one periodontitis direction. A genus can appear in both panels (e.g. *Porphyromonas*: 77 studies increased, 10 decreased).
- **x**: distinct PerioSigDB studies (not signatures) reporting the genus in that direction (log scale). Species are collapsed to genus. Genera need ≥3 studies: 46 increased and 38 decreased genera.
- **y**: number of distinct other conditions with ≥1 study unit reporting the genus in the same direction. Units come from the filtered BugSigDB (human disease-vs-control, no meta-analyses, any body site, merged condition labels). 311 conditions have any increased unit. There is no minimum number of studies per condition, so a condition with 1 study counts the same as one with 50.
- **Shaded**: x ≥ 10 and y ≤ 15. Five genera fall inside: *Desulfobulbus* (19 studies, 5 other conditions), *Fretibacterium* (21, 9), *Filifactor* (35, 12), *Tannerella* (69, 15) and *Cardiobacterium* (decreased; 11, 10).
- **Example**: *Tannerella* increased: 69 PerioSigDB studies. Twelve of the 15 other conditions are oral studies (e.g. gingivitis, halitosis, rheumatoid arthritis, smoking, type II diabetes); the rest are lower-airway (COPD, respiratory system disease) and gut (diabetic nephropathy) samples. *Treponema* is just above the shading at 57 studies, 21 conditions.
- **Example (widespread)**: *Prevotella* increased: 51 studies, 117 other conditions; *Streptococcus* increased: 18 studies, 123 conditions.
- **Labels**: x ≥ 10 or y ≤ 5 (so rare genera such as *Peptoanaerobacter*, 3 studies and 0 conditions, are labelled).
- **No test**: the figure is descriptive. y grows with how much a genus is studied and sequenced anywhere, and closely related conditions such as gingivitis are not excluded; only labels containing "periodont" are removed.
- **Watch out**: x counts are inflated for taxa on checkerboard/PCR panels (e.g. *Tannerella*, *Filifactor*, *Treponema*). Counting at genus level hides species differences (e.g. *P. gingivalis* vs *P. catoniae*).
:::

```{r specificity-values}
sp <- \(g, dir = "Increased in periodontitis") with(filter(specificity, taxon == g, direction == dir),
                                                  sprintf("%d studies, %d other conditions", perio_studies, other_conditions))
```

**Shows:** increases in the most-reported periodontitis genera, *Porphyromonas* (`r sp("Porphyromonas")`), *Prevotella* (`r sp("Prevotella")`) and *Fusobacterium* (`r sp("Fusobacterium")`), are reported across many conditions and so are not unique to the periodontitis literature. *Desulfobulbus* (`r sp("Desulfobulbus")`), *Fretibacterium* (`r sp("Fretibacterium")`), *Filifactor* (`r sp("Filifactor")`) and *Tannerella* (`r sp("Tannerella")`) fall in the shaded zone: substantial support in PerioSigDB but reported in the same direction by fewer other conditions. *Treponema* (`r sp("Treponema")`) sits just above it. *Peptoanaerobacter* and *Johnsonella* are reported by almost no other condition, but also by few periodontitis studies. Several of these are targets of the checkerboard and PCR panels used in many PerioSigDB studies, which may raise their periodontitis counts. Most periodontitis-decreased genera (e.g. *Streptococcus*, *Haemophilus*, *Neisseria*, *Rothia*) are reported decreased by many other conditions; only *Cardiobacterium* (`r sp("Cardiobacterium", "Decreased in periodontitis")`) falls in the shaded zone, with *Lautropia* (`r sp("Lautropia", "Decreased in periodontitis")`) just above it.

### Do the periodontitis-associated genera already co-vary in health?

Periodontitis studies report some genera increased together (e.g. *Treponema* and *Tannerella*) and others decreased together. Is that grouping particular to disease, or do these genera already co-vary in healthy mouths? The BugSigDB paper asked this for stool and found the second: genera reported together in disease signatures mostly mirror how they co-occur in healthy stool (Geistlinger et al. 2024, Figure 4). Here the same question is asked for the periodontitis-associated genera, using healthy subgingival plaque from the Human Microbiome Project (one first-visit sample from each of 183 participants). For each pair of genera, a positive correlation means that, across healthy participants, the two tend to have high relative abundance in the same plaque samples; a negative correlation means that where one is relatively abundant the other tends to be scarce. Relative abundances sum to one, so a genus taking a larger share lowers the share of every other genus and creates correlations that need not reflect how the genera's amounts vary (Friedman and Alm 2012). The correlations are therefore computed on centred log-ratio (CLR) abundance, each genus relative to the geometric mean of all genera in the same sample, which removes most of this effect. They still need not reflect direct ecological interactions. The five PerioSigDB 16S studies with per-sample data (see "Abundance of the top consensus taxa in individual participants") allow the same pairs to be correlated across the healthy participants and, separately, across the periodontitis patients of the same studies.

```{r co-occurrence-data}
hmp_cor <- readRDS("../../output/hmp_subgingival_correlation.rds")

perio_dir <- setNames(perio_genera$direction, perio_genera$taxon)
in_hmp <- intersect(perio_genera$taxon, rownames(hmp_cor))
pair_cor <- as_tibble(as.table(hmp_cor[in_hmp, in_hmp]), .name_repair = "minimal") |>
  setNames(c("a", "b", "healthy")) |>
  mutate(across(c(a, b), as.character)) |>
  filter(a < b) |>
  mutate(pair = case_when(perio_dir[a] != perio_dir[b] ~ "One increased,\none decreased",
                          perio_dir[a] == "increased" ~ "Both increased", .default = "Both decreased"))
# are pairs of two increased (or two decreased) genera more correlated than opposite-way pairs? Two tests,
# each of the difference in median correlation; pairs share genera, so instead of a test over pairs, the
# genera's directions in periodontitis are permuted (the same 1,000 permutations for every test)
type_gap <- \(d, dir, type) with(d, median(r[dir[a] == type & dir[b] == type]) - median(r[dir[a] != dir[b]]))
set.seed(1)
perms <- replicate(1000, setNames(sample(perio_dir[in_hmp]), in_hmp), simplify = FALSE)
type_test <- \(d) map_dfr(c("increased", "decreased"), \(type) {
  null <- map_dbl(perms, \(dir) type_gap(d, dir, type))
  gap <- type_gap(d, perio_dir, type)
  tibble(type, gap, null_mean = mean(null), null_975 = quantile(null, 0.975),
         p = (1 + sum(null >= gap)) / (1 + length(null)))
})

# genus relative abundance per participant (mean of their subgingival samples) in the five studies with
# participant data (see "Abundance of the top consensus taxa in individual participants")
participant_genera <- read.csv("../../output/participant_data/taxon_abundance.csv") |>
  filter(rank == "genus") |>
  # HMP uses the former name of Cutibacterium
  mutate(taxon = ifelse(taxon == "Cutibacterium", "Propionibacterium", taxon)) |>
  filter(taxon %in% in_hmp) |>
  inner_join(participant_samples, by = c("Study", "run_accession")) |>
  summarise(abundance = mean(relative_abundance), .by = c(Study, subject, group, taxon))

# centred log-ratio (CLR) abundance, as for HMP, so that the shares summing to one do not create
# correlations: over each participant's full genus profile, zeros replaced by half the participant's
# smallest non-zero abundance
participant_clr <- read.csv("../../output/participant_data/taxon_abundance.csv") |>
  filter(rank == "genus") |>
  mutate(taxon = ifelse(taxon == "Cutibacterium", "Propionibacterium", taxon)) |>
  inner_join(participant_samples, by = c("Study", "run_accession")) |>
  summarise(abundance = mean(relative_abundance), .by = c(Study, subject, group, taxon)) |>
  filter(any(abundance > 0), .by = c(Study, taxon)) |>
  mutate(x = ifelse(abundance > 0, abundance, min(abundance[abundance > 0]) / 2),
         clr = log(x) - mean(log(x)), .by = c(Study, subject)) |>
  # a genus never detected in a study's group gives no correlation there
  semi_join(filter(participant_genera, abundance > 0), by = c("Study", "group", "taxon")) |>
  select(Study, subject, group, taxon, clr)

# Spearman correlation of each pair within each study; a genus never detected in a study's participants
# gives no correlation there
study_cor <- function(g, d = participant_clr, v = "clr") {
  d |>
    filter(group == g) |>
    select(Study, subject, group, taxon, all_of(v)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = taxon, values_from = all_of(v)) |>
    nest(.by = Study) |>
    mutate(n = map_int(data, nrow),
           r = map(data, \(d) suppressWarnings(cor(select(d, -subject, -group), method = "spearman")))) |>
    mutate(r = map(r, \(m) as_tibble(as.table(m), .name_repair = "minimal") |> setNames(c("a", "b", "r")))) |>
    select(Study, n, r) |>
    unnest(r) |>
    mutate(across(c(a, b), as.character)) |>
    filter(a < b, !is.na(r))
}
# combined across studies as the mean of Fisher's z weighted by n - 3, so that differences between studies
# (16S region, platform) do not create correlations
combined_cor <- \(g, ...) study_cor(g, ...) |>
  summarise(r = tanh(weighted.mean(atanh(pmin(pmax(r, -0.99), 0.99)), n - 3)), studies = n(),
            participants = sum(n), .by = c(a, b))
pair_cor_participants <- pair_cor |>
  left_join(select(combined_cor("Periodontitis"), a, b, periodontitis = r, studies), by = c("a", "b")) |>
  left_join(select(combined_cor("Health"), a, b, health_studies = r), by = c("a", "b"))

# the same tests on the correlations combined across the five studies
combined_tests <- bind_rows(
  Health = type_test(transmute(pair_cor_participants, a, b, r = health_studies)),
  Periodontitis = type_test(transmute(filter(pair_cor_participants, !is.na(periodontitis)), a, b, r = periodontitis)),
  .id = "group")
health_vs_perio <- with(pair_cor_participants, cor(healthy, periodontitis, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"))

# one column for HMP and one for each study (correlations within that study), health in the top row and
# periodontitis in the bottom row, pair types within each panel
hmp_samples <- readRDS("../../output/hmp_oral_prevalence.rds") |>
  filter(site == "Subgingival Plaque") |>
  pull(samples) |>
  first()
study_n <- distinct(participant_clr, Study, subject, group) |>
  count(Study, group) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = n) |>
  mutate(column = sprintf("%s\n(%d healthy, %d periodontitis)", Study, Health, Periodontitis))
columns <- c(sprintf("HMP\n(%d healthy)", hmp_samples), study_n$column)
pair_types <- c("Both increased", "Both decreased", "One increased,\none decreased")
cooc_plot <- bind_rows(
  transmute(pair_cor, a, b, r = healthy, group = "Health", column = columns[1]),
  map(c("Health", "Periodontitis"), \(g) transmute(study_cor(g), Study, a, b, r, group = g)) |>
    bind_rows() |>
    inner_join(select(study_n, Study, column), by = "Study") |>
    select(-Study)
) |>
  inner_join(select(pair_cor, a, b, pair), by = c("a", "b")) |>
  mutate(column = factor(column, levels = columns), pair = factor(pair, levels = rev(pair_types)),
         group = factor(group, levels = c("Health", "Periodontitis")))
# the two tests within each panel (HMP, and each study and group; unadjusted p); a row of same-way pairs is
# faded when its test is not significant, the row of opposite-way pairs when neither is
cooc_tests <- cooc_plot |>
  nest(.by = c(column, group)) |>
  mutate(tests = map(data, type_test)) |>
  select(-data) |>
  unnest(tests)
row_significant <- cooc_tests |>
  mutate(pair = c(increased = "Both increased", decreased = "Both decreased")[type]) |>
  select(column, group, pair, p) |>
  (\(d) bind_rows(d, mutate(summarise(d, p = min(p), .by = c(column, group)), pair = "One increased,\none decreased")))() |>
  mutate(pair = factor(pair, levels = levels(cooc_plot$pair)), significant = p < 0.05)
cooc_plot <- left_join(cooc_plot, select(row_significant, -p), by = c("column", "group", "pair"))
cooc_median <- summarise(cooc_plot, r = median(r), .by = c(column, pair, group, significant))
row_p <- filter(row_significant, pair != "One increased,\none decreased")
ct <- \(g, type) signif(combined_tests$p[combined_tests$group == g & combined_tests$type == type], 2)

# one panel per column (HMP and each study) and group; cols selects the columns shown
cooc_figure <- function(cols, title) {
    ggplot(filter(cooc_plot, column %in% cols), aes(r, pair)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
    geom_quasirandom(aes(fill = pair, alpha = significant, color = significant), orientation = "y", width = 0.3,
                     shape = 21, size = 1.3, stroke = 0.2) +
    geom_crossbar(data = filter(cooc_median, column %in% cols), aes(xmin = r, xmax = r, color = significant), width = 0.65, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_label(data = filter(cooc_median, column %in% cols), aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", ifelse(abs(r) < 0.005, 0, r)), color = significant),
               nudge_y = 0.42, size = 2.7, fill = "white", border.colour = NA, label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines")) +
    geom_text(data = filter(row_p, column %in% cols), aes(x = -Inf, label = sprintf("p = %s", signif(p, 1)), color = significant),
              hjust = -0.08, nudge_y = 0.42, size = 2.6, fontface = "italic") +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 0.75, `FALSE` = 0.2), guide = "none") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey10", `FALSE` = "grey65"), guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Both increased" = "#c2410c", "Both decreased" = "#1c5cab",
                                 "One increased,\none decreased" = "grey75"), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-0.5, 0, 0.5)) +
    facet_grid(group ~ column, switch = "y") +
    labs(x = "Correlation of the pair across participants (Spearman, CLR abundance)", y = NULL,
         title = title) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
          strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1), strip.placement = "outside")
}
```

```{r co-occurrence-hmp}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| fig-align: left
#| fig-cap: "Correlation between pairs of the periodontitis-associated genera in healthy subgingival plaque from the Human Microbiome Project (first visit only, so one sample per participant; 183 participants). Genera: those of the genus heatmaps with at least 0.1% relative abundance in at least 10% of samples (13 of the 20 periodontitis-increased and 14 of the 20 periodontitis-decreased genera). Each point is a pair of genera: Spearman correlation of their CLR abundance (log of the genus relative to the geometric mean of all genera in the sample). Rows: whether the two genera are both increased (78 pairs), both decreased (91) or one of each (182) in periodontitis. Bar and number: median. p: are pairs of two increased (or two decreased) genera more correlated than pairs that change in opposite ways? One-sided permutation test of the difference in median correlation, shuffling which genera count as increased and which as decreased (1,000 permutations), since pairs share genera and are not independent. Faded: rows whose test is not significant (p ≥ 0.05). The same analysis in the five PerioSigDB studies with per-sample data is in the next figure."
cooc_figure(columns[1], NULL) + theme(strip.text.y.left = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = "Correlation of the pair across participants\n(Spearman, CLR abundance)")
```
